docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: Beyond AT Protocol (Bluesky) and ActivityPub (Mastodon), several other social protocols offer unique value propositions that could enhance the Nelson Tech community platform. This document analyzes these protocols and provides recommendations for potential integration.

docs.title: 1. Nostr (Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays)
docs.text:
Why Consider Nostr: - Simplicity: Deliberately simple protocol that's easy to implement - Censorship Resistance: Users can connect to multiple relays simultaneously - Bitcoin Integration: Native Lightning Network payments ("Zaps") for micropayments - Growing Momentum: $10M donation from Jack Dorsey in 2025, rapidly growing ecosystem - Versatility: Beyond social posts - supports marketplaces, wikis, code collaboration

Implementation Benefits for Community: - Micropayments: Members could tip valuable content creators - Enhanced Privacy: Cryptographic keys provide strong identity control - Resilience: No single point of failure, always available - Low Cost: Simple protocol means lower implementation overhead

Technical Implementation: 

interface NostrAdapter {
  // Nostr uses simple JSON events
  publishEvent(event: NostrEvent): Promise<void>;
  subscribeToRelay(relayUrl: string): WebSocket;
  signEvent(privateKey: string, content: any): SignedEvent;
}

interface NostrEvent {
  id?: string;
  pubkey: string;
  created_at: number;
  kind: number; // 0=metadata, 1=text note, etc.
  tags: string[][];
  content: string;
  sig?: string;
}

Estimated Implementation Effort: Low (2-3 weeks)

docs.title: 2. IndieWeb Protocols Suite
docs.text:
Why Consider IndieWeb: - Web Standards: W3C recommendations (Webmention, Micropub) - Existing Infrastructure: Works with current web architecture - Content Ownership: Users maintain control on their domains - SEO Benefits: Better discoverability through standard web

Core Protocols to Implement:

docs.title: Webmention (High Priority)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Cross-site conversations and interactions
  • Use Case: When community content is referenced externally, receive notifications
  • Implementation: Simple webhook-like system

docs.title: Micropub (Medium Priority)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Post to platform from third-party apps
  • Use Case: Members could use various apps to create content
  • Implementation: RESTful API endpoints

docs.title: Microsub (Low Priority)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Standardized feed reading
  • Use Case: Subscribe to community feeds in external readers

Implementation Example: 

// Webmention receiver
interface WebmentionReceiver {
  async receiveWebmention(source: URL, target: URL): Promise<void> {
    // Verify source links to target
    // Parse microformats for rich data
    // Store as social interaction
  }
}

// Micropub endpoint
interface MicropubEndpoint {
  async createPost(req: MicropubRequest): Promise<Response> {
    // Authenticate via IndieAuth
    // Create post from micropub data
    // Return location of created post
  }
}

Estimated Implementation Effort: Medium (3-4 weeks for basic support)

docs.title: 3. Matrix Protocol with Element Integration (Enhanced Messaging)
docs.text:
Why Consider Matrix: - Proven Scale: 115 million users globally - Institutional Trust: Used by German healthcare (150,000+ organizations), French government - Rich Messaging: Voice, video, file sharing, E2EE, threading - Bridging: Connect to Slack, Discord, Telegram, WhatsApp - Element Client: Official flagship client designed for embedding

Element Integration Options:

docs.title: Option 1: Embedded Element Web (Simplest)
docs.text:
// Embed Element directly in your platform
class ElementWebIntegration {
  embedElement(config: {
    roomId: string;

  }) {

        style="width: 100%; height: 600px; border: none;"

    `;

docs.title: Option 3: Hybrid Messaging Strategy (Recommended)
docs.text:
interface HybridMessagingSystem {
  // Keep existing for simple messages
  existingMessaging: {
    quickDMs: boolean;
    notifications: boolean;
    mobileFirst: boolean;
  };

  // Add Matrix/Element for rich features
  matrixElement: {
    groupDiscussions: boolean;
    videoConferences: boolean;
    fileSharing: boolean;
    threading: boolean;
    encryption: boolean;
  };

  // Bridge between systems
  async syncMessages(conversationId: string): Promise<void>;
  async mirrorToMatrix(message: Message): Promise<void>;
}

Key Element Features for Tech Communities: - Code Syntax Highlighting: Share code with proper formatting - LaTeX Rendering: Mathematical formulas for technical discussions - Screen Sharing: Built-in for demos and debugging - Voice Messages: Quick audio notes - Threaded Conversations: Organized technical discussions - Widgets: Embed Jitsi, Etherpad, custom tools - End-to-End Encryption: Secure by default

Implementation Approaches:

Light Integration (1-2 weeks): - Embed Element in iframe for groups - Single sign-on from main platform - Basic room creation per group - Minimal customization

Medium Integration (3-4 weeks): - Self-hosted Element with branding - Automatic room creation for groups/projects - User directory synchronization - Custom theme matching platform - Basic bridging to existing messages

Deep Integration (5-6 weeks): - Full Matrix homeserver (Synapse/Dendrite) - Complete Element customization - Two-way message bridging - Unified notification system - Custom widgets and bots - Migration of existing conversations

Deployment Options:

  1. Element Matrix Services (Managed)
  2. Cost: ~$3-5 per active user/month
  3. Setup: Hours
  4. Maintenance: None

  5. SLA: 99.9% uptime guaranteed

  6. Self-Hosted

  7. Cost: ~$50-200/month infrastructure
  8. Setup: 2-3 days
  9. Maintenance: Moderate
  10. Control: Complete

Real-World Success Examples: - Mozilla: Replaced IRC with Matrix for all community chat - Gitter: Migrated entirely to Matrix/Element - GNOME & KDE: Use Matrix for development discussions - German Healthcare: 150,000 organizations using TI-Messenger (Matrix-based)

Estimated Implementation Effort: - Light: 1-2 weeks - Medium: 3-4 weeks - Deep: 5-6 weeks

docs.title: 4. Farcaster (Web3 Social)
docs.text:
Consider If: - Community has crypto/web3 interest - Willing to pay for registration ($5/year) - Want advanced features like "Frames" (mini-apps in feed)

Pros: - Innovative Frames feature for interactive content - Strong VC backing and development - Growing ecosystem (40k DAUs)

Cons: - Requires cryptocurrency for registration - More complex than other options - Web3 focus might alienate some users

docs.title: 5. Lens Protocol (Creator-Focused)
docs.text:
Consider If: - Strong creator community - NFT/monetization interest - Polygon blockchain acceptance

Pros: - Built-in monetization (subscriptions, NFTs) - Creator ownership focus - Web3 native features

Cons: - Blockchain dependency - Lower engagement than alternatives - Complexity for non-crypto users

docs.title: Technical Architecture
docs.text:
// Universal Protocol Adapter Pattern
interface UniversalSocialAdapter {
  protocol: string;
  enabled: boolean;

  // Core operations
  publish(content: UniversalPost): Promise<string>;
  subscribe(callback: (post: ExternalPost) => void): void;

  // Social graph
  follow?(userId: string): Promise<void>;
  unfollow?(userId: string): Promise<void>;

  // Interactions
  like?(postId: string): Promise<void>;
  reply?(postId: string, content: string): Promise<void>;

  // Protocol-specific features
  customFeatures?: Record<string, Function>;
}

// Protocol Registry
class ProtocolRegistry {
  private adapters: Map<string, UniversalSocialAdapter> = new Map();

  register(adapter: UniversalSocialAdapter) {
    this.adapters.set(adapter.protocol, adapter);
  }

  async broadcast(content: UniversalPost) {
    const results = await Promise.allSettled(
      Array.from(this.adapters.values())
        .filter(a => a.enabled)
        .map(a => a.publish(content))
    );
    return results;
  }
}

docs.title: Nostr
docs.text:
• Cost: ~2 weeks development, minimal infrastructure
  • Benefit: Access to Bitcoin ecosystem, censorship resistance, simple protocol
  • ROI: High - Low cost, unique features

docs.title: IndieWeb Suite
docs.text:
• Cost: ~3-4 weeks development, standard web infrastructure
  • Benefit: SEO improvements, web standards compliance, third-party app ecosystem
  • ROI: Medium-High - Moderate cost, broad compatibility

docs.title: Matrix
docs.text:
• Cost: ~4-6 weeks development, homeserver costs or SaaS fees
  • Benefit: Enterprise-grade messaging, proven scale, rich features
  • ROI: Medium - Higher cost but could replace existing messaging

docs.title: Web3 Protocols (Farcaster/Lens)
docs.text:
• Cost: ~6-8 weeks development, blockchain infrastructure, user fees
  • Benefit: Access to crypto community, novel features, monetization
  • ROI: Low-Medium - High cost, niche audience

docs.title: Nostr
docs.text:
• Strength: Cryptographic signatures, no central authority
  • Risk: Relay operators could censor, key management complexity
  • Mitigation: Multiple relay connections, secure key storage

docs.title: IndieWeb
docs.text:
• Strength: Standard web security, no special requirements
  • Risk: Spam via Webmentions, authentication challenges
  • Mitigation: Webmention verification, IndieAuth implementation

docs.title: Matrix
docs.text:
• Strength: E2EE, proven security model
  • Risk: Homeserver compromise, metadata leakage
  • Mitigation: Regular updates, careful permission management

docs.title: Primary Recommendation: Implement Nostr + IndieWeb
docs.text: Rationale: 1. Complementary Approaches: Nostr for decentralized social, IndieWeb for web standards 2. Low Implementation Cost: Both are relatively simple protocols 3. Broad Appeal: Covers both crypto-curious and traditional web users 4. Future-Proof: Growing ecosystems with strong philosophical alignment

docs.title: Implementation Strategy:
docs.text:
1. Start with Nostr for quick win and Bitcoin community access
  2. Add Webmention for cross-site interactions
  3. Implement Micropub if third-party posting apps are desired
  4. Consider Matrix only if current messaging needs upgrade

docs.title: Avoid Initially:
docs.text:
• Web3 protocols unless community explicitly requests
  • Complex federation until core features are stable
  • Protocol-specific features that lock in to single ecosystem

docs.title: Key Metrics:
docs.text:
• Nostr: Number of relays connected, zaps sent/received
  • Webmention: External mentions received, engagement rate
  • Micropub: Third-party posts created, app diversity
  • Cross-Protocol: Unified engagement across all protocols

docs.title: Success Indicators:
docs.text:
• 10% of users enable at least one additional protocol
  • 50+ cross-protocol interactions per month
  • Positive feedback on protocol diversity
  • No significant increase in moderation burden

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
While AT Protocol and ActivityPub provide solid federation options, adding Nostr and IndieWeb protocols would give the Nelson Tech platform unique advantages:

  1. Nostr brings simplicity, Bitcoin integration, and true censorship resistance
  2. IndieWeb ensures web standards compliance and SEO benefits
  3. Matrix (optional) could revolutionize the messaging experience

These protocols can be implemented incrementally, with each adding value independently. The modular approach ensures the platform remains functional without any external protocols while progressively enhancing capabilities for users who want them.

The key is maintaining the standalone-first principle: every protocol integration should enhance, not define, the core platform experience.

docs.title: Database Architect Summary: Photo Gallery System
Project Overview
docs.text: As the Database Architect for the Nelson Tech Community Platform, I have designed and implemented a comprehensive photo gallery system that supports user-generated content, admin promotion workflows, and dynamic page header management. This system integrates seamlessly with the existing platform architecture while providing robust new capabilities.

docs.title: 1. Database Migration File
docs.text:
Location: /supabase/migrations/20250622000003_create_photo_gallery_system.sql

Key Components: - 8 core tables with proper relationships - 25+ indexes for optimal performance - Comprehensive RLS policies for security - Automated trigger functions - Database views for common queries - Utility functions for statistics

docs.title: Option 3: Docker + Self-Hosted
docs.text:
Dockerfile (create if needed): 

FROM node:18-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

FROM nginx:alpine
COPY --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
EXPOSE 80
CMD ["nginx", "-g", "daemon off;"]

Build and Run: 

# Build image
docker build -t nelson-tech-platform .

# Run container
docker run -d -p 80:80 \
  -e VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co \
  -e VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-key \

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: This audit identified and remediated critical security vulnerabilities in the Nelson Tech platform's error handling system. The platform was exposing sensitive internal system information in error messages, including database details, file paths, and internal service information.

docs.title: 1. Database Information Exposure
docs.text:
• Issue: Raw database error messages exposed table names, constraint names, and internal IDs
  • Risk: High - Provides attackers with database schema information
  • Examples Found:
  • PGRST116 error codes exposed
  • Table constraint violation details
  • Database connection strings in error messages

docs.title: 2. File System Path Exposure
docs.text:
• Issue: Full file paths exposed in upload and storage errors
  • Risk: Medium - Reveals server file structure
  • Examples Found:
  • /Users/... paths in development
  • Storage bucket internal paths
  • Temporary file locations

docs.title: 3. Authentication Service Details
docs.text:
• Issue: Internal authentication flow details exposed
  • Risk: High - Reveals authentication mechanisms
  • Examples Found:
  • Supabase internal error codes
  • JWT token structure hints
  • Session management internals

docs.title: 4. Stack Traces in Production
docs.text:
• Issue: Full stack traces visible to users
  • Risk: High - Exposes code structure and dependencies
  • Examples Found:
  • JavaScript stack traces in catch blocks
  • Library version information
  • Internal function names

docs.title: 1. Error Sanitization Utility
docs.text: Created src/utils/errorSanitization.ts with: - Pattern Matching: Regex patterns to identify and categorize errors - User-Friendly Messages: Generic messages that don't expose internals - Debug IDs: Unique identifiers for error tracking - Error Codes: Structured codes for debugging without exposure

docs.title: 2. Centralized Error Handling
docs.text: Created src/hooks/useErrorHandling.ts with: - Consistent Processing: All errors processed through sanitization - Retry Logic: Automatic retry for recoverable errors - Contextual Logging: Proper server-side logging for debugging

docs.title: 3. Error Display Components
docs.text: Created src/components/ui/ErrorAlert.tsx with: - Sanitized Display: Only user-safe messages shown - Consistent UI: Standardized error presentation - Actionable Options: Retry and dismiss functionality

docs.title: 4. Updated Authentication System
docs.text: Modified src/hooks/useAuth.ts: - Sanitized Auth Errors: All authentication errors now sanitized - Context-Aware Logging: Detailed logging without user exposure - User-Friendly Messages: Clear, actionable error messages

docs.text:
8 Core Features Had Missing Route Protection

Users could bypass disabled features by typing URLs directly because routes lacked FeatureGate components:

Feature Routes Unprotected Feature Key Impact Directory/Members /directory, /directory/:slug, /directory/create, /directory/:slug/edit members_directory High Companies /companies, /companies/:slug, /companies/create, /companies/:slug/edit companies_listing High Events /events, /events/:slug, /events/create, /events/:slug/edit events_system High News /news, /news/:slug, /news/create, /news/:id/edit news_blog High Groups /groups, /groups/:slug, /groups/create, /groups/:slug/edit groups_communities High Resources /resources, /resources/:slug, /resources/create, /resources/:slug/edit resources_library High Marketplace /marketplace, /marketplace/:slug, /marketplace/create, /marketplace/:slug/edit marketplace High Opportunities /opportunities, /opportunities/:slug, /opportunities/create, /opportunities/:slug/edit opportunities_board High

Security Impact: Users could access disabled features by: 1. Bookmarking URLs before feature disabled 2. Manually typing URLs 3. Receiving shared links 4. Finding URLs in search engines

docs.text:
Added FeatureGate wrappers to all unprotected routes:

}

docs.text:
// 1. Font Selection Handler
const handleFontChange = (fontFamily: string) => {
  loadGoogleFont(fontFamily);
  onChange({ 
    fontFamily,
    fontFallback: `${fontFamily}, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif`
  });
};

// 2. Dynamic Font Loading
const loadGoogleFont = (fontFamily: string) => {
  const fontId = `google-font-${fontFamily.replace(/\s+/g, '-')}`;
  let fontLink = document.getElementById(fontId);

  if (!fontLink) {
    fontLink = document.createElement('link');
    fontLink.id = fontId;
    fontLink.rel = 'stylesheet';
    fontLink.href = `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=${fontFamily.replace(/\s+/g, '+')}:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap`;
    document.head.appendChild(fontLink);
  }
};

// 3. Font Application in Theme Provider
const applyFontToDOM = (typography: ThemeTypography) => {
  const root = document.documentElement;

  // Apply CSS variables
  root.style.setProperty('--theme-font-family', typography.font_family);
  root.style.setProperty('--theme-font-family-heading', typography.font_family_heading);

  // Apply to body element
  document.body.style.fontFamily = typography.font_family;
};

export const useGalleryHybrid = (galleryId?: string) => {
  // React Query for data
  const galleriesQuery = useGalleries();
  const photosQuery = useGalleryPhotos(galleryId);

  // Redux for UI state
  const selectedPhotos = useAppSelector(selectSelectedPhotos);
  const uploadProgress = useAppSelector(selectUploadProgress);

  // Combined actions
  const uploadPhoto = async (input) => {
    // Update Redux progress state
    dispatch(setUploadProgress({ id, progress: 0 }));

    // Execute React Query mutation
    const photo = await uploadMutation.mutateAsync(input);

    // Update Redux on completion
    dispatch(setUploadProgress({ id, progress: 100 }));

    return photo;
  };

  return {
    // Data
    galleries: galleriesQuery.data,
    photos: photosQuery.data,

    // UI State
    selectedPhotos,
    uploadProgress,

    // Actions
    uploadPhoto,
    toggleSelection
  };
};

docs.title: 1. Optimistic Updates

const mutation = useMutation({
  mutationFn: api.updatePhoto,
  onMutate: async (newData) => {
    // Cancel queries
    await queryClient.cancelQueries(['photos']);

    // Snapshot previous value
    const previous = queryClient.getQueryData(['photos']);

    // Optimistically update
    queryClient.setQueryData(['photos'], old => {
      return updateInPlace(old, newData);
    });

    return { previous };
  },
  onError: (err, newData, context) => {
    // Rollback on error
    queryClient.setQueryData(['photos'], context.previous);
  }
});

        dispatch(updateProgress({

          progress: (e.loaded / e.total) * 100
        }));

docs.text:
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';

// Configure DOMPurify
const sanitizeConfig = {
  ALLOWED_TAGS: ['style', 'link', 'meta'], // For head
  ALLOWED_ATTR: ['rel', 'href', 'type', 'content', 'name'],
  ALLOW_DATA_ATTR: false,
};

// Sanitize before injection
const sanitizedHTML = DOMPurify.sanitize(
  settings.custom_head_html || '',
  sanitizeConfig
);

element.innerHTML = sanitizedHTML;

docs.title: Security Headers to Add:
docs.text:
# nginx.conf
add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
add_header X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block" always;
add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
add_header Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()" always;

# HSTS (only if using HTTPS)
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains" always;

# Content Security Policy
add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co https://api.openai.com https://api.anthropic.com; frame-ancestors 'self';" always;

docs.title: Known Issues and Limitations
docs.text:
Last Updated: June 23, 2025

This document tracks known issues, limitations, and areas for improvement in the Nelson Tech Community Platform.

docs.title: High Priority
docs.text:
1. Form Validation Inconsistency
  2. Issue: Manual validation across forms without standardization
  3. Impact: Inconsistent user experience and potential validation gaps
  4. Proposed Solution: Implement React Hook Form + Zod for schema validation

  5. Status: Planning phase

  6. Error Boundary Coverage

  7. Issue: Incomplete error boundary implementation
  8. Impact: Unhandled errors may crash the application
  9. Proposed Solution: Add error boundaries to all major route components
  10. Status: In progress

docs.title: Medium Priority
docs.text:
1. TypeScript Coverage
  2. Issue: Some components still use permissive typing
  3. Impact: Reduced type safety in certain areas
  4. Files Affected: Legacy components in /components directory

  5. Status: Ongoing migration

  6. Test Coverage Gaps

  7. Issue: 93% coverage with 31 failing tests
  8. Impact: Potential regression risks
  9. Areas: Gallery system integration tests, newsletter analytics

  10. Status: Active development

  11. Performance Monitoring

  12. Issue: No real-world performance metrics collection
  13. Impact: Unable to track actual user experience
  14. Proposed Solution: Integrate Web Vitals monitoring
  15. Status: Planned

docs.title: Low Priority
docs.text:
1. Component Documentation
  2. Issue: Incomplete JSDoc coverage
  3. Impact: Reduced developer onboarding efficiency

  4. Status: Ongoing documentation effort

  5. Accessibility Gaps

  6. Issue: Some interactive elements lack proper ARIA labels
  7. Impact: Reduced accessibility for screen reader users
  8. Status: Audit planned

docs.title: Architectural Limitations
docs.text:
1. No Real-time Updates
  2. WebSocket integration not implemented
  3. Users must refresh to see new content

  4. Planned for future release

  5. Limited Offline Support

  6. No PWA capabilities currently
  7. Requires active internet connection

  8. Service worker implementation planned

  9. File Size Constraints

  10. Gallery uploads limited to 10MB per file
  11. Batch uploads limited to 20 files at once
  12. Storage quotas apply per organization

docs.title: Feature Limitations
docs.text:
1. Search Functionality
  2. Basic text search only
  3. No advanced filters or faceted search

  4. Full-text search planned with Postgres extensions

  5. Notification System

  6. Email notifications only
  7. No in-app notifications

  8. No push notifications

  9. Mobile Experience

  10. Responsive web only
  11. No native mobile app
  12. Some features better suited for desktop

docs.title: Performance Limitations
docs.text:
1. Initial Load Time
  2. First load may take 2-3 seconds
  3. Subsequent loads faster due to caching

  4. Further optimization possible

  5. Large Data Sets

  6. Lists over 1000 items may show performance degradation
  7. Virtualization not implemented for all lists
  8. Pagination recommended for large sets

docs.title: MkDocs Documentation Site Setup
docs.text: This documentation is built using MkDocs with the Material for MkDocs theme.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Our documentation site includes:

  • Material Design - Modern, responsive theme
  • Search - Full-text search across all documentation
  • Dark/Light Mode - Automatic theme switching
  • Navigation - Multi-level navigation with tabs
  • Code Highlighting - Syntax highlighting for all languages
  • Admonitions - Notes, tips, warnings, and more
  • Mermaid Diagrams - Flowcharts and diagrams
  • Git Integration - Last updated dates from git history
  • Mobile Responsive - Optimized for all devices

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8 or higher
  • pip (Python package manager)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Install MkDocs and dependencies:
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt

docs.title: Running Locally
docs.text:
Start the development server:

mkdocs serve

The documentation will be available at http://127.0.0.1:8000

The dev server will auto-reload when you save changes to documentation files.

docs.title: Building
docs.text:
Build the static site:

mkdocs build

This creates a site/ directory with the static HTML files.

docs.title: Preview Build
docs.text:
Preview the built site:

mkdocs serve --dirtyreload

docs.title: GitHub Pages (Automatic)
docs.text:
The documentation is automatically deployed to GitHub Pages when changes are pushed to the main branch.

Workflow: .github/workflows/docs.yml

Triggers: - Push to main branch with changes to docs/**, mkdocs.yml, or workflow file - Manual workflow dispatch

URL: https://iaminawe.github.io/nelson-tech/

docs.title: Manual Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy manually to GitHub Pages:

mkdocs gh-deploy

This builds the site and pushes to the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Main Configuration
docs.text:
File: mkdocs.yml

Key sections: - site_name, site_description - Site metadata - theme - Material theme configuration - nav - Navigation structure - plugins - Enabled plugins - markdown_extensions - Markdown features

  1. Getting Started - Quick start, setup, contributing
  2. Architecture - System design and patterns

docs.title: NPM Vulnerability Analysis & Recommendations
docs.text: Date: November 10, 2025 Analysis: Post Phase 1 Security Fixes

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Initial State: 6 vulnerabilities (1 high, 4 moderate, 1 low) After npm audit fix: 5 vulnerabilities (4 moderate, 1 low) Fixed: 1 high severity vulnerability (linkifyjs) Remaining: 5 vulnerabilities requiring breaking changes

docs.title: 1. linkifyjs (HIGH) - FIXED ✅
docs.text: Issue: Prototype Pollution & HTML Attribute Injection (XSS) Advisory: GHSA-95jq-xph2-cx9h Resolution: Automatically updated to safe version Impact: High severity XSS vulnerability eliminated

docs.title: 1. ai (<=5.0.51) - MODERATE
docs.text:
Issue: Vercel's AI SDK filetype whitelists can be bypassed when uploading files Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rwvc-j5jr-mgvh Current: ai <= 5.0.51 Affected: blocknote/xl-ai package Fix Available: npm audit fix --force Breaking Change: Will update blocknote/xl-ai@0.39.2 → 0.41.1

Impact Assessment: - Severity: Moderate - Exploitability: Low (requires file upload feature with AI processing) - Used In: BlockNote AI editor features - Risk: Low - Project doesn't currently use AI SDK file uploads directly

Recommendation: - Short term: Safe to defer (low risk to this project) - Long term: Update when ready to test BlockNote AI features - Testing Required: Extensive testing of AI editor functionality

docs.title: 2. esbuild (<=0.24.2) - MODERATE
docs.text:
Issue: esbuild enables any website to send requests to dev server and read responses Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99 Current: esbuild <= 0.24.2 (via vite dependency) Fix Available: npm audit fix --force Breaking Change: Will update vite@5.0.12 → 7.2.2 (MAJOR VERSION)

Impact Assessment: - Severity: Moderate - Exploitability: Only affects development environment - Production Impact: None (dev server not used in production) - Risk: Low - Only impacts local development

Recommendation: - Short term: Safe to defer (dev-only vulnerability) - Long term: Update to Vite 7.x in separate effort - Mitigation: Don't expose dev server to untrusted networks - Testing Required: Full application testing after Vite upgrade

Vite 7.x Migration Considerations: - Review Vite 7.x changelog for breaking changes - Test build configuration - Verify all Vite plugins are compatible - Test HMR (Hot Module Replacement) - Verify environment variable handling

docs.title: 3. jsondiffpatch (<0.7.2) - MODERATE
docs.text:
Issue: XSS vulnerability via HtmlFormatter::nodeBegin Advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-33vc-wfww-vjfv Current: jsondiffpatch < 0.7.2 (dependency of blocknote/xl-ai) Fix Available: npm audit fix --force Breaking Change: Will update blocknote/xl-ai@0.39.2 → 0.41.1

Impact Assessment: - Severity: Moderate - Exploitability: Low (requires specific formatter usage) - Used In: BlockNote AI diff visualization (if used) - Risk: Low - Project likely doesn't use HtmlFormatter directly

Recommendation: - Short term: Safe to defer (low risk) - Long term: Update with blocknote/xl-ai upgrade - Testing Required: BlockNote AI editor features

docs.title: 📊 Vulnerability Risk Matrix
docs.text: Package Severity Production Risk Dev Risk Action Priority linkifyjs HIGH Medium Medium ✅ FIXED ai Moderate Low Low P3 - Defer esbuild Moderate None Low P3 - Defer jsondiffpatch Moderate Low Low P3 - Defer

docs.title: Option 1: Conservative Approach (Recommended)
docs.text:
Accept current state and defer breaking changes

Rationale: - All remaining vulnerabilities are MODERATE severity - Production impact is minimal (esbuild is dev-only) - Breaking changes require extensive testing - Current security posture is acceptable

Action: 1. ✅ Commit package-lock.json (linkifyjs fix) 2. ✅ Document remaining vulnerabilities (this file) 3. ✅ Add to Phase 2 or Phase 3 backlog 4. ✅ Schedule Vite 7 upgrade separately 5. ✅ Monitor for security updates

Timeline: Address in Phase 2-3 or post-release

docs.title: Option 2: Aggressive Approach (Higher Risk)
docs.text:
Force fix all vulnerabilities now

Commands: 

npm audit fix --force
npm run typecheck
npm run build
npm run test

Risks: - Vite 7.x may have breaking API changes - BlockNote AI features may break - Build configuration may need updates - Requires extensive testing before release

Required Testing: - Full application functionality - All editor features (especially AI) - Build and deployment - Development server - All integrations (Supabase, OpenAI, Anthropic)

Timeline: Additional 1-2 days of testing

docs.title: Option 3: Hybrid Approach
docs.text:
Fix low-risk vulnerabilities, defer Vite upgrade

Strategy: 1. Update blocknote/xl-ai manually (test AI features) 2. Defer Vite 7 upgrade to separate epic 3. Monitor for security patches

Complexity: High (manual dependency management) Not Recommended: Creates dependency conflicts

docs.title: Current State (After linkifyjs fix)
docs.text:
Production Vulnerabilities: 0 critical, 0 high, 3 moderate with low impact Development Vulnerabilities: 1 moderate (esbuild dev server) Overall Risk: LOW ✅

docs.title: Acceptable for Open Source Release?
docs.text:
YES ✅ with documentation

The remaining vulnerabilities are: 1. Not critical or high severity 2. Have low production impact 3. Require breaking changes to fix 4. Are documented and tracked

This is acceptable for open source release as long as: - ✅ Vulnerabilities are documented (this file) - ✅ Plan exists to address them (Phase 2-3) - ✅ Users are informed (SECURITY.md) - ✅ Monitoring is in place

docs.title: 📝 Conclusion
docs.text:
Recommendation: Accept current state and commit the linkifyjs fix

Rationale: 1. High severity vulnerability fixed ✅ 2. Remaining vulnerabilities are moderate with low impact 3. Breaking changes require extensive testing 4. Better to ship secure, stable release now 5. Can address remaining issues in post-release updates

Next Steps: 1. Commit package-lock.json 2. Push changes 3. Continue with Phase 2 (code quality) 4. Schedule dependency upgrades for later sprint

docs.title: Open Source Release Readiness Report
docs.text: Project: Nelson Tech Community Platform Review Date: November 10, 2025 Reviewer: Comprehensive Automated Review Version: 0.1.0

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: The Nelson Tech Community Platform is a well-architected, feature-rich React application with enterprise-grade patterns. The codebase demonstrates solid foundational architecture with comprehensive features and documentation. However, critical security issues must be addressed before public release, along with code quality improvements and documentation consolidation.

docs.title: Overall Assessment
docs.text: Category Status Grade Architecture ✅ Ready A- (9/10) Features ✅ Ready A (9.5/10) Security ⚠️ BLOCKERS C (5/10) Code Quality ⚠️ Needs Work C+ (6.5/10) Documentation ✅ Good B+ (8/10) Testing ⚠️ Insufficient D (4/10) Open Source Readiness ⚠️ Needs Work C (6/10)

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text: DO NOT release publicly until critical security issues are resolved. Estimated time to production-ready: 2-3 weeks with focused effort.

docs.title: Issue 1.1: Development Authentication Bypass
docs.text:
• Location: /src/shared/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:144-192
  • Severity: CRITICAL
  • Risk: Anyone can gain admin access with environment variable
  • Action: Complete removal of VITE_DEV_BYPASS_AUTH feature
  • Effort: 1-2 hours
  • Priority: P0 - Block release
// Lines 144-192 - MUST BE REMOVED
if (isDevelopment && import.meta.env.VITE_DEV_BYPASS_AUTH === 'true') {
  // Bypasses all authentication
}

docs.title: Issue 1.2: Unsafe HTML Injection
docs.text:
• Location: /src/lib/themes/utils.ts:164-189
  • Severity: CRITICAL
  • Risk: Stored XSS affecting all users via admin panel
  • Action: Add DOMPurify sanitization to custom_head_html and custom_body_html
  • Effort: 2-4 hours
  • Priority: P0 - Block release
// CURRENT (UNSAFE):
innerHTML: settings.custom_head_html

// REQUIRED:
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';
innerHTML: DOMPurify.sanitize(settings.custom_head_html)

docs.title: Issue 1.3: Page Content Sanitization Missing
docs.text:
• Location: /src/features/pages/components/PageDetail/index.tsx:187-192
  • Severity: HIGH
  • Risk: XSS via page builder content
  • Action: Ensure jsonToHtml() output is sanitized
  • Effort: 2-3 hours
  • Priority: P0 - Block release

docs.title: Issue 1.4: Insecure Session Storage
docs.text:
• Location: /src/pages/admin/MenuManagementPage.tsx
  • Severity: MEDIUM
  • Risk: Session IDs exposed to XSS attacks via sessionStorage
  • Action: Move to secure httpOnly cookies
  • Effort: 4-8 hours
  • Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 1.5: Missing Security Headers
docs.text:
• Location: Configuration files (nginx.conf, netlify.toml)
  • Severity: MEDIUM
  • Risk: Clickjacking, MIME sniffing, protocol downgrade attacks
  • Action: Add CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS
  • Effort: 2-3 hours
  • Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

Total Security Fix Effort: 11-20 hours (2-3 days)

docs.title: Issue 2.1: Extremely Large Component Files
docs.text:
• Count: 6 files exceed 1,000 lines (38 files > 500 lines)
  • Largest: SimpleUnifiedUsersPage.tsx (1,793 lines)
  • Problem: Unmaintainable, hard to test, performance issues
  • Action: Split into focused components (< 300 lines each)
  • Effort: 2-3 weeks
  • Priority: P1 - Pre-launch (at least split top 6 files)

Top 6 Files Requiring Immediate Refactoring: 1. /src/pages/admin/SimpleUnifiedUsersPage.tsx - 1793 lines 2. /src/pages/admin/MenuManagementPage.tsx - 1704 lines 3. /src/pages/UserSettingsPage.tsx - 1560 lines 4. /src/pages/admin/EnhancedSettingsPage.tsx - 1101 lines 5. /src/pages/admin/UnifiedUsersPage.tsx - 1016 lines 6. /src/pages/admin/newsletter/CampaignManager.tsx - 992 lines

docs.title: Issue 2.2: Unsafe Type Usage (261 occurrences)
docs.text:
• Problem: any types throughout codebase compromise type safety
  • Key Files:
  • useGroupQueries.ts - 5+ functions returning any[]
  • useMessagingQueries.ts - Multiple any return types
  • SimpleUnifiedUsersPage.tsx - any in state management
  • Action: Replace all production any with proper types
  • Effort: 1 week
  • Priority: P1 - Pre-launch (critical files only)

docs.title: Issue 2.3: Type Definition Redundancy
docs.text:
• Problem: 3 duplicate Supabase type files (12,000+ lines total)
  • Files:
  • /src/types/supabase.ts - 4673 lines
  • /src/shared/types/database.types.ts - 4183 lines
  • /src/shared/types/supabase.ts - 4180 lines
  • Action: Consolidate to single source, exclude from linting
  • Effort: 2-3 hours
  • Priority: P2 - Quick win

docs.title: Issue 2.4: Debug Console Statements
docs.text:
• Count: 11 files with console.log statements
  • Examples:
  • useOpportunityQueries.ts - 13 console logs
  • useImageProcessing.ts - 3 statements
  • Action: Remove all debug logs, use proper logger
  • Effort: 2-3 hours
  • Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 2.5: Unresolved TODO/FIXME Comments
docs.text:
• Count: 15+ unresolved TODO comments
  • Examples:
  • usePermissions.ts:78 - "TODO: Implement condition checking"
  • FormActions.tsx:67 - "TODO: Implement delete group functionality"
  • visual/index.ts - 7 "TODO: Implement" exports
  • Action: Resolve or create tickets for each
  • Effort: 4-6 hours review + implementation time
  • Priority: P2 - Document if not implementing

docs.title: Current State
docs.text:
• Test files: 17 (some in tests/, some colocated)
  • Source files: 1,478
  • Test ratio: ~1.2% (industry standard: 30-40%)
  • Coverage: Unknown (run npm run test:coverage)

docs.title: Missing Tests
docs.text:
• ❌ No tests for largest/most complex files
  • ❌ Newsletter features minimally tested
  • ❌ Admin panel features undertested
  • ❌ Integration tests limited
  • ❌ E2E tests incomplete

docs.title: Actions Required
docs.text:
1. Immediate (P1): Add tests for critical paths:
  2. Authentication flow
  3. User registration/onboarding
  4. Payment/transaction flows (if any)

  5. Data creation/modification

  6. Pre-launch (P1): Achieve 30% coverage minimum:

  7. All API services
  8. All custom hooks
  9. Major page components

  10. Utility functions

  11. Post-launch (P2): Increase to 80% coverage

Effort: 2-3 weeks (focused testing sprint) Priority: P1 - Pre-launch (at least critical paths)

docs.title: Issue 4.1: Redundant Documentation
docs.text:
• Hybrid State Management: 7 duplicate files (~3000 lines)
  • Gallery System: 6 duplicate files (~2500 lines)
  • Admin Documentation: Scattered across 5+ locations
  • API Documentation: Scattered across 25+ files

Action Plan: 1. Consolidate hybrid state docs (7 → 2 files) 2. Consolidate gallery docs (6 → 2-3 files) 3. Create unified API reference 4. Create admin documentation index

Effort: 1 week Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 4.2: Missing Standard Documentation
docs.text:
• ✅ FIXED: CONTRIBUTING.md created
  • ✅ FIXED: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md created
  • ✅ FIXED: SECURITY.md created
  • ✅ FIXED: CHANGELOG.md created
  • ⚠️ NEEDS UPDATE: Contact email placeholders in security docs

Remaining Actions: - Add security contact email to SECURITY.md - Add contact email to CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md - Create GETTING_STARTED.md guide - Update README.md with open source info

Effort: 2-3 hours Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 5.1: Environment Variable Documentation
docs.text:
• .env.example exists but lacks comprehensive documentation
  • 50+ environment variables without inline explanations
  • No setup guide linking env vars to features

Action: Create comprehensive environment setup guide Effort: 3-4 hours Priority: P1 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 5.2: Service Keys Exposure Risk
docs.text:
• Frontend has VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (acceptable)
  • Must verify no service keys exposed in source
  • Must verify no keys committed to git history

Action: Audit git history, run secrets scanner Effort: 1-2 hours Priority: P0 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 6.1: Import Organization
docs.text:
• 19 deeply nested imports (4+ levels: ../../../../../../)
  • 250 barrel exports creating circular dependency risk
  • Inconsistent use of @/ path alias

Action: Enforce path alias usage, reduce barrel exports Effort: 3-5 hours Priority: P2 - Post-launch

docs.title: Issue 6.2: Error Boundaries
docs.text:
• Only 3 error boundary implementations
  • Large features not wrapped (MenuManagement, UserSettings, CampaignManager)

Action: Add error boundaries around major features Effort: 4-6 hours Priority: P2 - Pre-launch

docs.title: Issue 7.1: Relaxed Strict Mode
docs.text:
• noUnusedLocals: false (should be true)
  • noUnusedParameters: false (should be true)
  • noUncheckedIndexedAccess: false (should be true)

Action: Gradually enable strict flags Effort: 1 week (fixing violations) Priority: P2 - Post-launch

docs.title: Issue 8.1: Tree-Shaking Disabled
docs.text:
• Location: vite.config.ts:91
  • Note: "disabled to fix bundle issue"
  • Impact: Larger bundle sizes

Action: Investigate and re-enable if possible Effort: 4-8 hours debugging Priority: P2 - Post-launch

  • ✅ Hybrid state management - Redux + React Query pattern is solid
  • ✅ Type safety foundation - TypeScript used throughout
  • ✅ Modern React patterns - Hooks, lazy loading, code splitting
  • ✅ Comprehensive database schema - Well-designed with RLS
  • ✅ Multiple deployment options - Docker, Coolify, Netlify

docs.text:

  • ✅ AI integration - OpenAI + Anthropic support

  • ✅ Theme system - 5 presets with dark mode
  • ✅ Admin panel - Feature-rich management interface

// Fully typed with documentation
/**
 * Hook to fetch group activities (member actions, posts, events, etc.)
 *
 * @param groupId - The ID of the group to fetch activities for
 * @returns Query result containing array of GroupActivity objects
 *
 * @example
 * ```typescript
 * const { data: activities, isLoading } = useGroupActivities('group-123');
 * activities?.forEach(activity => {
 *   console.log(`${activity.actor?.name} ${activity.action}`);
 * });
 * ```
 */
export function useGroupActivities(groupId?: string): UseQueryResult<GroupActivity[], Error> {
  return useQuery<GroupActivity[], Error>({
    queryFn: async (): Promise<GroupActivity[]> => {
      const activities = await groupsApi.getGroupActivities(groupId);
      return activities as GroupActivity[];
    }
  });
}

docs.text: The photo galleries feature is now fully integrated with the feature toggle system. When disabled, all gallery-related functionality will be safely hidden and inaccessible.

  • Default State: Enabled (true)

docs.title: When ENABLED:
docs.text:
✅ Admin Interface - Media Gallery menu item appears in admin sidebar - /admin/media route is accessible - Full CRUD operations for galleries available

✅ Public Routes - /galleries - Browse public galleries - /galleries/create - Create new galleries - /galleries/:slug - View gallery details - /galleries/:slug/edit - Edit galleries - /my-galleries - User's personal galleries

✅ API Access - All gallery API endpoints functional - Photo upload/management enabled - Comments and likes on photos

✅ Entity Integrations - Galleries can be attached to groups - Galleries can be attached to events - Galleries can be attached to news - Galleries can be attached to companies - Galleries can be attached to marketplace listings - Galleries can be attached to resources - Galleries can be attached to pages - Galleries can be attached to user profiles

docs.title: When DISABLED:
docs.text:
❌ Admin Interface - Media Gallery menu item hidden - /admin/media returns 404

❌ Public Routes - All gallery routes return 404 - No gallery UI components render

❌ API Access - Gallery API calls throw error - Upload endpoints blocked

❌ Entity Integrations - Gallery attachment fields hidden - Existing gallery relationships preserved but inaccessible

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Kootenay Tech Community platform uses a custom rich text editor built on top of Tiptap v2, providing a modern, extensible editing experience with drag-and-drop functionality, slash commands, and image support.

docs.title: 1. Global Drag Handles

  • Click and drag to reorder paragraphs, headings, lists, and other blocks
  • Powered by tiptap-extension-global-drag-handle

  • Quick access to:
  • Headings (H1, H2, H3)
  • Lists (bullet and numbered)
  • Block quotes
  • Images

docs.text:

  • Available formats:
  • Bold (Ctrl/Cmd + B)
  • Italic (Ctrl/Cmd + I)
  • Strikethrough
  • Headings
  • Lists
  • Quotes

docs.title: 4. Image Support
docs.text:
• Add images via:
  • Slash command (/image)
  • Bubble menu image button
  • Currently supports URL-based images
  • Images are responsive and styled with rounded corners

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the comprehensive solution implemented to fix RLS issues affecting conversation updates and operations in the messaging system. The solution addresses 406 (Not Acceptable) errors, "JSON object requested, multiple (or no) rows returned" errors, and RLS blocking conversation updates.

docs.title: Core Issues Identified
docs.text:
1. 406 (Not Acceptable) Errors: PATCH requests returning 406 due to multiple or no rows returned
  2. RLS Policy Conflicts: Row Level Security policies blocking legitimate conversation updates
  3. Participant Verification: Complex participant verification causing recursive policy checks
  4. Error Handling: Poor error messages and lack of fallback strategies

docs.title: Root Causes
docs.text:
• Complex RLS Policies: Recursive policy checks causing infinite loops
  • Multiple Row Returns: Queries returning multiple rows when single row expected
  • Permission Verification: Inefficient participant checking causing performance issues
  • Fallback Strategies: Lack of graceful degradation when operations are blocked

docs.text:

Features: - Participant verification before update - Creator permission checking - Atomic operation with proper error handling - Returns updated conversation record

docs.title: Enhanced Error Handling
docs.text:
// Primary approach: Use secure database function
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .rpc('update_conversation_title', {
    conversation_id: id,
    new_title: updates.title
  });

// Fallback 1: Participant verification + direct update
if (error) {
  const participantInfo = await this.checkParticipantStatus(id);
  if (!participantInfo.canUpdate) {
    throw new Error('You do not have permission to update this conversation');
  }
  return await this.updateConversationFallback(id, updates);
}

docs.title: 406 Error Mitigation
docs.text:
// Try single() first
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from('conversations')
  .update(updateData)
  .eq('id', id)
  .select()
  .single();

if (error?.code === 'PGRST106') {
  // Fallback: Try without .single() to avoid 406 errors
  const { data: arrayData, error: arrayError } = await supabase
    .from('conversations')
    .update(updateData)
    .eq('id', id)
    .select();

  return arrayData?.[0];
}

docs.title: Participant Status Checking
docs.text:
private async checkParticipantStatus(conversationId: string): Promise<{
  isParticipant: boolean;
  isCreator: boolean;
  role: string | null;
  canUpdate: boolean;
}> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .rpc('check_conversation_participant', {
      conversation_id: conversationId
    });

  const info = data || {};
  return {
    isParticipant: info.is_participant || false,
    isCreator: info.is_creator || false,
    role: info.role || null,
    canUpdate: (info.is_participant && ['admin', 'moderator'].includes(info.role)) || info.is_creator
  };
}

docs.title: Enhanced Retry Logic
docs.text:
retry: (failureCount, error) => {
  // Don't retry permission errors
  if (error?.message?.includes('permission')) return false;

  // Don't retry RLS policy errors
  if (error?.code === '42501') return false;

  // Retry 406 errors once (might be transient)
  if (error?.code === 'PGRST106' && failureCount < 1) return true;

  return failureCount < 2;
}

docs.title: User-Friendly Error Messages
docs.text:
onError: (error) => {
  if (error.message?.includes('permission')) {
    error.message = 'You do not have permission to update this conversation';
  } else if (error.code === '42501') {
    error.message = 'Unable to update conversation due to security restrictions';
  } else if (error.code === 'PGRST106') {
    error.message = 'Conversation update failed due to a database issue';
  }
}

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: This document outlines the comprehensive specification for implementing a standalone social media platform within the Nelson Tech community system. The platform is designed to be fully functional independently, with optional federation capabilities through AT Protocol (Bluesky) and ActivityPub (Mastodon) that can be enabled as progressive enhancements.

docs.title: Core Design Principles
docs.text:
1. Standalone First: The system must be fully functional without any external protocol dependencies
  2. Progressive Enhancement: Federation capabilities are optional add-ons that enhance but don't define the core functionality
  3. Existing Infrastructure Reuse: Leverage current gallery, messaging, and member systems
  4. Privacy by Design: Granular privacy controls at every level
  5. Community-Centric: Features designed specifically for professional tech communities

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text:
-- Core social posts table
CREATE TABLE social_posts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  author_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  content TEXT NOT NULL,
  content_html TEXT, -- Sanitized HTML version
  reply_to_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  thread_root_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  media_attachments JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  video_embeds JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  visibility VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'public',
  is_pinned BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  is_edited BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  edit_history JSONB DEFAULT '[]'::jsonb,
  metrics JSONB DEFAULT '{"likes": 0, "reposts": 0, "replies": 0}'::jsonb,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

-- Indexes for performance
CREATE INDEX idx_social_posts_author ON social_posts(author_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_social_posts_thread_root ON social_posts(thread_root_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_social_posts_created_at ON social_posts(created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_social_posts_visibility ON social_posts(visibility);

-- Social interactions
CREATE TABLE social_likes (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  post_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, post_id)
);

CREATE TABLE social_reposts (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  post_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  comment TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, post_id)
);

-- Following relationships
CREATE TABLE social_follows (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  follower_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  following_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active', -- active, pending, blocked
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(follower_id, following_id),
  CHECK (follower_id != following_id)
);

-- Hashtags
CREATE TABLE social_hashtags (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tag VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  usage_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE social_post_hashtags (
  post_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  hashtag_id UUID REFERENCES social_hashtags(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  PRIMARY KEY (post_id, hashtag_id)
);

-- Mentions
CREATE TABLE social_mentions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  post_id UUID REFERENCES social_posts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  mentioned_user_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Activity feed caching
CREATE TABLE social_feed_cache (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  feed_type VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  post_ids UUID[] NOT NULL,
  generated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() + INTERVAL '1 hour'
);

-- Federation mapping (optional)
CREATE TABLE social_federation_identities (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  protocol VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, -- 'atprotocol', 'activitypub'
  external_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  handle TEXT,
  instance_url TEXT,
  metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT TRUE,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(user_id, protocol)
);

docs.title: 4.2 Feed Algorithm
docs.text:
interface FeedAlgorithm {
  // Base scoring
  calculateRelevance(post: SocialPost, user: User): number {
    let score = 0;

    // Recency (exponential decay)
    const ageHours = (Date.now() - post.createdAt) / (1000 * 60 * 60);
    score += Math.exp(-ageHours / 24) * 100;

    // Engagement metrics
    score += post.likes * 2;
    score += post.reposts * 3;
    score += post.replies * 1.5;

    // Relationship factors
    if (user.following.includes(post.authorId)) score += 50;
    if (user.company === post.authorCompany) score += 30;
    if (hasSharedGroups(user, post.author)) score += 20;

    // Content relevance
    if (matchesUserInterests(post, user)) score += 40;

    return score;
  }
}

docs.title: Federation Adapter Pattern
docs.text:
// Abstract federation interface
interface FederationAdapter {
  readonly protocol: 'atprotocol' | 'activitypub';
  readonly isEnabled: boolean;

  // Connection management
  connect(): Promise<void>;
  disconnect(): Promise<void>;
  testConnection(): Promise<boolean>;

  // Content synchronization
  publishPost(post: SocialPost): Promise<string>;
  updatePost(post: SocialPost): Promise<void>;
  deletePost(postId: string): Promise<void>;

  // Social graph sync
  syncFollowers(): Promise<FederatedUser[]>;
  followUser(externalId: string): Promise<void>;
  unfollowUser(externalId: string): Promise<void>;

  // Incoming content
  subscribeToUpdates(callback: (update: FederatedUpdate) => void): void;
  fetchUserTimeline(externalId: string): Promise<FederatedPost[]>;
}

// AT Protocol implementation
class ATProtocolAdapter implements FederationAdapter {
  readonly protocol = 'atprotocol';

  async publishPost(post: SocialPost): Promise<string> {
    if (!this.isEnabled) return post.id;

    // Transform to AT Protocol format
    const atProtoPost = {
      $type: 'app.bsky.feed.post',
      text: post.content,
      createdAt: post.createdAt,
      reply: post.replyTo ? {
        root: { uri: post.threadRootId },
        parent: { uri: post.replyToId }
      } : undefined
    };

    // Publish to AT Protocol network
    const response = await this.client.createRecord(atProtoPost);
    return response.uri;
  }
}

// Mastodon/ActivityPub implementation
class MastodonAdapter implements FederationAdapter {
  readonly protocol = 'activitypub';

  async publishPost(post: SocialPost): Promise<string> {
    if (!this.isEnabled) return post.id;

    // Transform to ActivityPub format
    const activityPubNote = {
      '@context': 'https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams',
      type: 'Note',
      content: post.contentHtml,
      published: post.createdAt,
      to: ['https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams#Public'],
      cc: [`${this.instanceUrl}/users/${post.authorId}/followers`]
    };

    // Publish to ActivityPub network
    const response = await this.client.createActivity(activityPubNote);
    return response.id;
  }
}

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
This social media platform specification provides a comprehensive blueprint for building a standalone, community-centric social platform that can optionally integrate with the broader federated social web. The modular design ensures that the core functionality remains robust and independent while allowing for future enhancements and integrations as needed.

The focus on reusing existing infrastructure, implementing progressive enhancement, and maintaining clear separation between core and optional features ensures a sustainable and maintainable implementation that can grow with the community's needs.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the comprehensive Supabase storage architecture implemented for the photo gallery system, featuring user-specific folder structures, automated thumbnail generation, and robust security policies.

docs.title: Buckets

  6. Optimized thumbnails and medium-sized images
  7. 10MB file size limit

  8. Supports: JPEG, PNG, WebP

  9. gallery-temp (Private)

  10. Temporary uploads during processing
  11. 50MB file size limit
  12. Auto-cleanup after 24 hours

├── originals/          # Full-resolution images

docs.title: Gallery Photos Table
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE gallery_photos (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  gallery_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES user_galleries(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES members(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

  -- File information
  file_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  original_file_name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  file_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  mime_type VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,

  -- Storage paths
  storage_path TEXT NOT NULL,        -- Original file path
  thumbnail_path TEXT,               -- Thumbnail path
  medium_path TEXT,                  -- Medium-sized version path

  -- Image metadata
  width INTEGER,
  height INTEGER,

  -- Organization
  title VARCHAR(255),
  description TEXT,
  tags TEXT[],
  sort_order INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  visibility VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'visible',

  -- Processing status
  processing_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'completed',
  moderation_status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'approved',

  -- Timestamps
  created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT now()
);

docs.title: Gallery Photos Access
docs.text:
1. Public Viewing 

    CREATE POLICY "Users can view public gallery photos" ON storage.objects
FOR SELECT USING (
  bucket_id = 'gallery-photos' AND
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM user_galleries ug
    JOIN gallery_photos gp ON ug.id = gp.gallery_id
    WHERE ug.privacy_level = 'public' 
      AND ug.visibility = 'visible'
      AND gp.visibility = 'visible'
      AND gp.moderation_status = 'approved'
      AND storage.objects.name = gp.storage_path
  )
);

  2. User Upload Permissions 

    CREATE POLICY "Users can upload to their own gallery folder" ON storage.objects
FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (
  bucket_id = 'gallery-photos' AND
  auth.uid()::text = (string_to_array(name, '/'))[2] AND
  name ~ '^users/[0-9a-f-]+/galleries/[0-9a-f-]+/(originals|thumbnails|medium)/[^/]+\.(jpg|jpeg|png|webp|gif|bmp|tiff)$'
);

  3. Ownership Verification 

    CREATE POLICY "Users can delete their own gallery photos" ON storage.objects
FOR DELETE USING (
  bucket_id = 'gallery-photos' AND
  auth.uid()::text = (string_to_array(name, '/'))[2]
);

  if (!allowedTypes.includes(file.type)) return { valid: false, error: 'Invalid type' };

  // Extension check

docs.text:
-- Get user storage statistics
CREATE FUNCTION get_user_storage_usage(user_uuid UUID)
RETURNS JSON AS $$
  SELECT json_build_object(
    'total_files', COUNT(*),
    'total_size_bytes', COALESCE(SUM(size), 0),
    'total_size_mb', ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(size), 0) / 1048576.0, 2),
    'photos_count', COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE bucket_id = 'gallery-photos'),
    'thumbnails_count', COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE bucket_id = 'gallery-thumbnails')
  ) FROM storage.objects
  WHERE (string_to_array(name, '/'))[2] = user_uuid::text;
$$;

-- Storage usage by user
CREATE VIEW storage_usage_by_user AS
SELECT 
  user_id,
  COUNT(*) as total_files,
  SUM(size) as total_size_bytes,
  MAX(created_at) as last_upload
FROM storage.objects o
WHERE bucket_id IN ('gallery-photos', 'gallery-thumbnails')
GROUP BY user_id;

-- Orphaned files detection
CREATE VIEW orphaned_storage_files AS
SELECT name, size, created_at
FROM storage.objects 
WHERE bucket_id = 'gallery-photos'
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM gallery_photos 
  WHERE storage_path = storage.objects.name
);

-- Set up RLS policies for public read access
DO $$
BEGIN
  -- Content Images Policies
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname = 'Public Access' AND tablename = 'objects' AND schemaname = 'storage') THEN
    CREATE POLICY "Public Access" ON storage.objects FOR SELECT USING (bucket_id IN ('content-images', 'profile-images', 'group-images', 'background-images'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname = 'Authenticated users can upload' AND tablename = 'objects' AND schemaname = 'storage') THEN
    CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can upload" ON storage.objects FOR INSERT WITH CHECK (bucket_id IN ('content-images', 'profile-images', 'group-images', 'background-images') AND auth.role() = 'authenticated');
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname = 'Authenticated users can update' AND tablename = 'objects' AND schemaname = 'storage') THEN
    CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can update" ON storage.objects FOR UPDATE USING (bucket_id IN ('content-images', 'profile-images', 'group-images', 'background-images') AND auth.role() = 'authenticated');
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE policyname = 'Authenticated users can delete' AND tablename = 'objects' AND schemaname = 'storage') THEN
    CREATE POLICY "Authenticated users can delete" ON storage.objects FOR DELETE USING (bucket_id IN ('content-images', 'profile-images', 'group-images', 'background-images') AND auth.role() = 'authenticated');
  END IF;
END $$;

docs.title: How Fonts Are Loaded
docs.text:
1. Font Selection
  2. User selects a font from the FontSelector component
  3. Component displays popular fonts and allows searching

  4. Preview text can be customized for testing

  5. Dynamic Loading

  6. When a font is selected, a Google Fonts link is created
  7. Link includes weight variations (300-700)
  8. Font is loaded asynchronously to prevent blocking

  9. Font Loading API ensures font is ready before use

  10. Application

  11. Font is applied via CSS variables
  12. Body font: --theme-font-family
  13. Heading font: --theme-font-family-heading

  14. Fallback chain ensures text remains readable

  15. Persistence

  16. Font choice is saved to database
  17. Applied on page load for all users
  18. Cached in browser for performance

docs.title: Font Fallback System
docs.text:
/* Example fallback chain */
font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 
             'Segoe UI', Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, 
             'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif;
  • Primary: Selected Google Font
  • System: Native system fonts for performance
  • Generic: Final fallback (sans-serif, serif, monospace)

docs.title: Performance Optimization
docs.text:
1. Font Display Strategy
  2. Uses display=swap for better loading experience
  3. Text remains visible with fallback during load

  4. Smooth transition when custom font loads

  5. Caching

  6. Google Fonts are cached by browsers
  7. Popular fonts often pre-cached

  8. Reduces load time on repeat visits

  9. Weight Optimization

  10. Only requested weights are loaded (300-700)
  11. Reduces download size
  12. Synthetic bold/italic avoided

docs.title: Font Not Loading
docs.text:
1. Check internet connection
  2. Verify Content Security Policy allows fonts.googleapis.com
  3. Check browser console for errors
  4. Try a different font to isolate issue

docs.title: Font Looks Different
docs.text:
1. Ensure correct weights are loaded
  2. Check font rendering settings in OS
  3. Verify font supports required characters
  4. Test in different browsers

docs.title: Performance Issues
docs.text:
1. Use popular fonts (better cached)
  2. Limit number of font weights
  3. Consider system fonts for critical text
  4. Enable font-display: swap

docs.title: Brand Name: Uluntu
docs.text: Pronounced: oo-LOON-too

docs.title: Etymology & Meaning
docs.text:
• Origin: Derived from the Ubuntu philosophy of African humanism
  • Ubuntu: "I am because we are" (the philosophy)
  • Uluntu: "The place where Ubuntu happens" (the space)

docs.title: Brand Essence
docs.text: Uluntu is not just a platform—it's the digital place where communities of practice gather, grow, and thrive.

docs.title: Core Brand Principle
docs.text: While Ubuntu represents the philosophy of human interconnectedness, Uluntu represents the actual place—physical or digital—where this interconnectedness occurs. We provide the infrastructure for community to happen.

docs.title: The Origin Story
docs.text:
In African philosophy, Ubuntu teaches us that "I am because we are"—that our humanity is inextricably linked to others. But philosophy needs a place to become practice. That place is Uluntu.

Just as every village has its gathering place—the market square, the community center, the local café—every modern community needs its digital Uluntu. A place designed not for broadcasting or networking, but for practicing together, learning together, and growing together.

Uluntu was born from a simple observation: while we have countless tools for communication, we lack true places for community. Places where professionals gather to practice their craft. Where hobbyists share their passion. Where neighbors solve local challenges. Where knowledge flows naturally and connections form organically.

docs.title: The Vision
docs.text: We envision a world where every community of practice has its own Uluntu—a digital place as vital as any physical gathering space. A place that respects privacy while fostering connection. That automates administration while preserving human interaction. That connects locally while thinking globally.

docs.title: The Mission
docs.text: To provide every community of practice with their own Uluntu—a complete digital place that brings the Ubuntu philosophy to life through intelligent infrastructure, meaningful connections, and respect for human community.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document describes the comprehensive author information display system implemented for the Nelson Tech application. The system provides flexible, reusable components for displaying author/member information with proper data fetching, caching, loading states, and error handling.

docs.title: Core Components
docs.text:
1. useAuthor Hook (/src/hooks/useAuthor.ts)
  2. Enhanced data fetching with caching and error handling
  3. Supports both single and batch author queries

  4. Automatic retry logic and stale-while-revalidate caching

  5. AuthorLink Component (/src/shared/components/ui/AuthorLink/)

  6. Main component for displaying author information
  7. Flexible display options (avatar, name, title)
  8. Multiple size variants and customization options

  9. Built-in loading and error states

  10. Utility Functions (/src/utils/authorUtils.ts)

  11. Helper functions for author data manipulation
  12. Initials generation, color assignment, filtering, sorting
  13. Data validation and extraction utilities

docs.title: Component Hierarchy
docs.text:
AuthorLink (Main component)
├── AuthorAvatar (Avatar only)
├── AuthorName (Name only)
├── AuthorCard (Full display with styling)
├── AuthorSelector (Interactive selection)
├── AuthorListItem (List display)
└── AuthorInitialsAvatar (Fallback avatar)

docs.title: Data Fetching
docs.text:
• Smart Caching: 5-minute stale time with background updates
  • Batch Queries: Efficient loading of multiple authors
  • Error Recovery: Automatic retries with exponential backoff
  • Content Integration: Automatic author ID extraction from various content types

docs.title: Display Options
docs.text:
• Flexible Sizing: Small, medium, large variants
  • Component Variants: Avatar-only, name-only, full display, card format
  • Customizable Styling: Tailwind classes, custom avatars, colors
  • Link Behavior: Optional linking to author profiles

docs.title: Loading States
docs.text:
• Skeleton Loading: Animated placeholders during data fetch
  • Error Fallbacks: Graceful handling of missing/failed data
  • Custom Fallbacks: User-defined loading and error components

docs.title: Interactive Features
docs.text:
• Author Selection: Multi-select and single-select components
  • Search: Real-time filtering of author lists
  • Click Handlers: Custom interaction behavior
  • Keyboard Navigation: Full accessibility support

docs.text:

docs.title: Potential Improvements
docs.text:
1. Real-time Updates: WebSocket integration for live author status
  2. Advanced Filtering: Role-based filtering, organization grouping
  3. Bulk Operations: Mass author assignment/management
  4. Analytics: Author interaction tracking
  5. Internationalization: Multi-language author display support

docs.title: Scalability Considerations
docs.text:
• Virtualized lists for large author sets
  • Progressive loading strategies
  • CDN integration for author images
  • Background prefetching for common authors

docs.title: From Existing Components
docs.text:
1. Replace hardcoded author displays with <AuthorLink>
  2. Update content components to use content prop pattern
  3. Migrate custom loading states to built-in skeletons
  4. Update styling to use new size variants

docs.title: Configuration Updates
docs.text:
1. Ensure proper TypeScript types are imported
  2. Add new components to export index
  3. Update Storybook stories for documentation
  4. Add tests for critical user flows

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The author system provides a comprehensive, flexible, and performant solution for displaying author information throughout the application. It maintains consistency with existing patterns while offering significant improvements in usability, accessibility, and maintainability.

The system is designed to grow with the application's needs while providing a solid foundation for current requirements. The modular architecture allows for easy customization and extension without breaking existing functionality.

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
import { FooterMenuProvider } from '@/shared/components/layout/Footer/FooterMenuProvider';
import { DynamicFooterMenu } from '@/shared/components/layout/Footer/DynamicFooterMenu';

function CustomFooter() {
  return (
    <FooterMenuProvider userRoles={['user', 'admin']}>
      <DynamicFooterMenu
        enableDynamicMenu={true}
        featureFlagKey="dynamic_footer_menus"
        columnLayout="equal"
        maxColumns={4}
        config={{
          groupingStrategy: 'by-category',
          maxItemsPerColumn: 8,
          showIcons: false,
          preserveHierarchy: true
        }}
      />
    </FooterMenuProvider>
  );
}

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: This research provides comprehensive analysis of monitoring, observability, and debugging solutions for multi-agent AI systems in 2025. The landscape has evolved significantly with specialized tools, standardized protocols, and enterprise-grade solutions designed specifically for the unique challenges of LLM-based systems.

docs.title: 1.1 LangSmith (LangChain)
docs.text:
Key Capabilities: - Full visibility into agent behavior with step-by-step tracing - Agent observability with tool call and run statistics monitoring (2025 updates) - Real-time monitoring with business-critical metrics (costs, latency, response quality) - Comprehensive evaluation framework with LLM-as-Judge evaluators - Production trace collection and dataset management

Strengths: - Deep LangChain/LangGraph integration - No latency impact (async distributed processing) - Comprehensive debugging capabilities - Built-in evaluation framework

Limitations: - Closed source with enterprise-only self-hosting - Limited to LangChain ecosystem - Past security vulnerabilities

docs.title: 1.2 Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
docs.text:

Strengths: - Automatic cost and token tracking - Flexible attribution across organizational dimensions - Strong dashboard capabilities - Enterprise-grade scalability

Pricing Model: - Based on ingested bytes (trace metadata, inputs/outputs) - Scalable pricing for enterprise deployments

# Example hallucination detection pipeline
def detect_hallucinations(response, context, ground_truth):

docs.title: Slug System Implementation
docs.text: This document describes the comprehensive slug system implemented for all content tables in the application.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The slug system provides URL-friendly identifiers for all major content types: - Members - Generated from member names - Events - Generated from event titles - Opportunities - Generated from opportunity titles - Groups - Generated from group names - News - Generated from news article titles

docs.title: Primary Migration: 20250819000030_add_content_table_slugs.sql
docs.text: This migration: 1. ✅ Adds slug columns to all content tables that don't have them 2. ✅ Creates utility functions for slug generation and uniqueness 3. ✅ Populates existing records with generated slugs 4. ✅ Adds unique constraints and indexes for performance 5. ✅ Creates automatic triggers for future record creation 6. ✅ Provides helper functions for management

docs.title: Test Migration: 20250819000031_test_slug_functionality.sql
docs.text: This migration: 1. ✅ Tests slug generation functions 2. ✅ Verifies all columns, indexes, and triggers exist 3. ✅ Checks for duplicate slugs 4. ✅ Generates a comprehensive status report

docs.title: generate_slug_from_text(input_text TEXT) → TEXT
docs.text:
Converts any text into a URL-friendly slug: - Removes special characters - Converts to lowercase - Replaces spaces with hyphens - Trims leading/trailing hyphens

Example: 

SELECT generate_slug_from_text('Hello World! This is a Test');
-- Returns: 'hello-world-this-is-a-test'

docs.title: ensure_unique_slug(table_name, slug_column, proposed_slug, exclude_id) → TEXT
docs.text:
Ensures slug uniqueness by appending numbers if needed: - Checks for existing slug in specified table - Appends -2, -3, etc. for duplicates - Excludes current record when updating

Example: 

SELECT ensure_unique_slug('members', 'slug', 'john-doe', NULL);
-- Returns: 'john-doe' or 'john-doe-2' if 'john-doe' exists

docs.title: regenerate_table_slugs(table_name TEXT) → INTEGER
docs.text:
Regenerates all slugs for a table: 

SELECT regenerate_table_slugs('members');
-- Returns: number of updated records

docs.title: check_duplicate_slugs() → TABLE(table_name, slug, count)
docs.text:
Finds duplicate slugs across all tables: 

SELECT * FROM check_duplicate_slugs();

docs.title: Automatic Triggers
docs.text:
Each content table has a trigger that automatically generates slugs: - auto_generate_members_slug - auto_generate_events_slug - auto_generate_opportunities_slug - auto_generate_groups_slug - auto_generate_news_slug

Trigger behavior: - Fires on INSERT and UPDATE - Only generates slug if slug field is NULL or empty - Uses appropriate source field (name/title) for each table - Ensures uniqueness automatically

ALTER TABLE members ALTER COLUMN slug SET NOT NULL;

docs.text: Use /scripts/manage-slugs.sh for slug management:

docs.text:
# Check slug status across all tables
./scripts/manage-slugs.sh check

# Regenerate slugs for a specific table

# Find duplicate slugs

docs.title: themes table
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE public.themes (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    description TEXT,
    is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    is_default BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    is_system BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    colors JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    typography JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    spacing JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    borders JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    shadows JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    components JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    custom_css TEXT,
    preview_image TEXT,
    created_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    CONSTRAINT only_one_active CHECK (
        NOT (is_active = true AND EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM themes t2 
            WHERE t2.id != themes.id AND t2.is_active = true
        ))
    )
);

-- Indexes
CREATE INDEX idx_themes_active ON public.themes(is_active);
CREATE INDEX idx_themes_slug ON public.themes(slug);

docs.title: theme_configurations table
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE public.theme_configurations (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    theme_id UUID REFERENCES public.themes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    config_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    config_value JSONB NOT NULL,
    config_type TEXT CHECK (config_type IN ('color', 'typography', 'spacing', 'component', 'custom')),
    description TEXT,
    is_required BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    validation_rules JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(theme_id, config_key)
);

-- Index
CREATE INDEX idx_theme_configs_theme ON public.theme_configurations(theme_id);

docs.title: theme_assets table
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE public.theme_assets (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    theme_id UUID REFERENCES public.themes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    asset_type TEXT CHECK (asset_type IN ('logo', 'favicon', 'banner', 'background', 'custom')),
    asset_key TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_url TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_size INTEGER,
    mime_type TEXT,
    dimensions JSONB,
    alt_text TEXT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(theme_id, asset_key)
);

-- Index
CREATE INDEX idx_theme_assets_theme ON public.theme_assets(theme_id);

docs.title: theme_history table (for version control)
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE public.theme_history (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    theme_id UUID REFERENCES public.themes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    changes JSONB NOT NULL,
    changed_by UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),

CREATE INDEX idx_theme_history_date ON public.theme_history(created_at);

docs.title: CSS Variable Generation
docs.text:
interface ThemeColors {
  primary: { r: number; g: number; b: number };
  secondary: { r: number; g: number; b: number };
  accent: { r: number; g: number; b: number };
  // ... more colors
}

function generateCSSVariables(theme: Theme): string {
  const vars = [];

  // Colors
  Object.entries(theme.colors).forEach(([key, value]) => {
    vars.push(`--color-${key}: ${value.r}, ${value.g}, ${value.b};`);
  });

  // Typography
  if (theme.typography.fontFamily) {
    vars.push(`--font-family: ${theme.typography.fontFamily};`);
  }

  // Spacing, borders, etc.
  // ...

  return `:root {\n${vars.join('\n')}\n}`;
}
