docs.title: Dynamic Font Loading
docs.text:
const loadGoogleFont = (fontFamily: string) => {
  const fontId = `google-font-${fontFamily.replace(/\s+/g, '-')}`;
  let fontLink = document.getElementById(fontId);

  if (!fontLink) {
    fontLink = document.createElement('link');
    fontLink.id = fontId;
    fontLink.rel = 'stylesheet';
    fontLink.href = `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=${fontFamily.replace(/\s+/g, '+')}:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap`;
    document.head.appendChild(fontLink);

    // Use Font Loading API
    fontLink.addEventListener('load', async () => {
      if ('fonts' in document) {
        await document.fonts.load(`16px ${fontFamily}`);
      }
    });
  }
};

docs.title: Creating a Gallery

1. Click the "Create Gallery" button in the top-right corner
  2. Fill in the required fields:

  4. Description: Gallery description (optional)
  5. Privacy Level:

    • Members Only: Visible to authenticated users
    • Private: Visible only to owner and admins
  6. Visibility:

    • Hidden: Gallery accessible via direct link only

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the hybrid state management pattern implemented across the Kootenay Tech Community platform. This architecture combines React Query for server state with Redux for UI state, providing optimal performance, caching, and developer experience.

docs.title: 1. Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
• React Query: Handles all server state (API calls, caching, background updates, error handling)
  • Redux: Manages UI-only state (filters, selections, view modes, pagination, form state)

docs.title: 2. Single Source of Truth
docs.text:
• Server data lives only in React Query cache
  • UI state lives only in Redux store
  • No duplication between the two systems

docs.title: 3. Performance Optimization
docs.text:
• React Query provides intelligent caching and background updates
  • Redux provides predictable UI state management
  • Code splitting with lazy loading for all pages

docs.title: High-Level Structure
docs.text:
┌─────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────┐
│   React Query   │    │     Redux       │
│  (Server State) │    │   (UI State)    │
├─────────────────┤    ├─────────────────┤
│ • API calls     │    │ • Filters       │
│ • Caching       │    │ • Selections    │
│ • Background    │    │ • View modes    │
│   updates       │    │ • Pagination    │
│ • Error states  │    │ • Form state    │
│ • Loading states│    │ • UI toggles    │
└─────────────────┘    └─────────────────┘
        │                       │
        └───────────┬───────────┘
                    │
            ┌───────▼───────┐
            │ Hybrid Hooks  │
            │ (Integration) │
            └───────────────┘

docs.title: 1. API Layer (React Query)
docs.text:
Located in: /src/features/{feature}/api/

// Example: eventsApi.ts
export const useEvents = () => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: queryKeys.events,
    queryFn: eventsApi.getAll,
    staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 minutes
  });
};

export const useEventsWithFilters = (filters?: EventFilters) => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: queryKeys.eventsWithFilters(filters || {}),
    queryFn: () => eventsApi.getAll(filters),
    enabled: !!filters,
  });
};

docs.title: 2. UI State Layer (Redux)
docs.text:
Located in: /src/features/{feature}/store/

// Example: eventsUISlice.ts
export interface EventsUIState {
  filters: EventFilters;
  selectedEvents: string[];
  viewMode: 'list' | 'calendar';
  sortBy: 'date' | 'title' | 'popularity';
  sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc';
  pagination: {
    page: number;
    itemsPerPage: number;
  };
}

const eventsUISlice = createSlice({
  name: 'eventsUI',
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    updateFilters: (state, action) => {
      state.filters = { ...state.filters, ...action.payload };
    },
    setViewMode: (state, action) => {
      state.viewMode = action.payload;
    },
    toggleEventSelection: (state, action) => {
      const eventId = action.payload;
      const index = state.selectedEvents.indexOf(eventId);
      if (index > -1) {
        state.selectedEvents.splice(index, 1);
      } else {
        state.selectedEvents.push(eventId);
      }
    },
  },
});

docs.title: 3. Integration Layer (Hybrid Hooks)
docs.text:
Located in: /src/features/{feature}/hooks/

// Example: useEventsHybrid.ts
export function useEventsHybrid() {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
  const filters = useAppSelector(selectEventsFilters);

  // React Query for server state
  const hasFilters = Object.keys(filters).length > 0;
  const eventsQuery = useEventsWithFilters(hasFilters ? filters : undefined);

  // Redux actions for UI state
  const updateFiltersAction = (newFilters: Partial<EventFilters>) => {
    dispatch(updateFilters(newFilters));
  };

  const setSearchTerm = (search?: string) => {
    updateFiltersAction({ search });
  };

  return {
    // Data from React Query
    events: eventsQuery.data || [],
    isLoading: eventsQuery.isLoading,
    isError: eventsQuery.isError,
    error: eventsQuery.error,
    refetch: eventsQuery.refetch,

    // UI state from Redux
    filters,

    // Actions
    setSearchTerm,
    updateFilters: updateFiltersAction,
  };
}

docs.title: For List/Collection Features
docs.text:
1. Create API hooks for different data access patterns: 

    // Basic list
export const useEvents = () => useQuery(/*...*/);

// Filtered list
export const useEventsWithFilters = (filters) => useQuery(/*...*/);

// Single item
export const useEvent = (id) => useQuery(/*...*/);

// Mutations
export const useCreateEvent = () => useMutation(/*...*/);
export const useUpdateEvent = () => useMutation(/*...*/);
export const useDeleteEvent = () => useMutation(/*...*/);

  2. Create UI slice for state that doesn't come from server: 

    interface FeatureUIState {
  filters: FilterType;
  selectedItems: string[];
  viewMode: 'list' | 'grid' | 'calendar';
  sortBy: string;
  sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc';
  pagination: PaginationState;
}

  3. Create hybrid hook that combines both: 

    export function useFeatureHybrid() {
  // Get UI state from Redux
  const uiState = useAppSelector(selectFeatureUI);

  // Get server data from React Query based on UI state
  const dataQuery = useFeatureData(uiState.filters);

  // Provide actions to update UI state
  const actions = {
    setFilter: (filter) => dispatch(updateFilter(filter)),
    toggleSelection: (id) => dispatch(toggleSelection(id)),
  };

  return {
    // Server data
    data: dataQuery.data,
    isLoading: dataQuery.isLoading,
    error: dataQuery.error,

    // UI state
    ...uiState,

    // Actions
    ...actions,
  };
}

docs.title: Page Components
docs.text:
export default function EventsPage() {
  // Use hybrid hook - no need to manage state manually
  const {
    events,
    isLoading,
    error,
    filters,
    setSearchTerm,
    setViewMode
  } = useEventsHybrid();

  return (
    <div>
      <SearchInput onSearch={setSearchTerm} />
      <ViewToggle onViewChange={setViewMode} />
      {isLoading ? <Loading /> : <EventsList events={events} />}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: List Components (Flexible Pattern)
docs.text:
interface EventsListProps {
  // Optional: allow parent to provide data
  events?: Event[];
  loading?: boolean;
  error?: Error;
}

export default function EventsList({ 
  events: parentEvents,
  loading: parentLoading,
  error: parentError 
}: EventsListProps) {
  // Determine data source
  const useParentData = parentEvents !== undefined;

  // Use hybrid hook only if no parent data provided
  const { events, isLoading, error } = useEventsHybrid();

  // Use appropriate data source
  const finalEvents = useParentData ? parentEvents : events;
  const finalLoading = useParentData ? parentLoading : isLoading;
  const finalError = useParentData ? parentError : error;

  // Render logic...
}

docs.title: Read Operations
docs.text:
User Interaction → UI State Update (Redux) → React Query Refetch → Component Re-render
  1. User changes filter
  2. Redux action updates filter state
  3. Hybrid hook detects filter change
  4. React Query automatically refetches with new filters
  5. Component receives new data and re-renders

docs.title: Write Operations
docs.text:
User Action → Mutation (React Query) → Optimistic Update → Cache Invalidation → UI Update
  1. User submits form
  2. React Query mutation executes
  3. Optimistic updates provide immediate feedback
  4. On success, related queries are invalidated
  5. Fresh data is fetched and UI updates

docs.title: React Query Advantages
docs.text:
• Intelligent Caching: Reduces API calls
  • Background Updates: Keeps data fresh automatically
  • Request Deduplication: Prevents duplicate requests
  • Optimistic Updates: Improves perceived performance
  • Error Retry Logic: Built-in resilience

docs.title: Redux Advantages
docs.text:
• Predictable Updates: UI state changes are deterministic
  • DevTools: Excellent debugging experience
  • Time Travel: Can replay state changes
  • Middleware: Logging, persistence, etc.

docs.title: Combined Benefits
docs.text:
• Separation of Concerns: Clear responsibilities
  • Reduced Complexity: No manual cache management
  • Better UX: Faster perceived performance
  • Developer Experience: Great debugging tools for both systems

docs.text:
// ❌ Old pattern - everything in Redux
const { events, isLoading, fetchEvents } = useEventsRedux();

import { renderHook } from '@testing-library/react-hooks';
import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { Provider } from 'react-redux';

const createWrapper = () => {
  const queryClient = new QueryClient({
    defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false } }

  return ({ children }) => (
    <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>
      <Provider store={testStore}>
        {children}
      </Provider>
    </QueryClientProvider>
  );
};

test('useEventsHybrid returns correct data', () => {

docs.title: Product Requirements Document: Hyper Local Community Events Site and Marketplace
docs.text: Version: 1.0 Date: May 25, 2025 Prepared For: SPARC Development Team Prepared By: Gemini AI (Senior Product Manager & Business Analyst) Source Document: Zero-Code User Blueprint for SPARC Program Generation (Date: May 24, 2025)

docs.title: 1.1 Project Overview
docs.text: The Hyper Local Community Events Site and Marketplace is a web-based platform designed to serve as a centralized hub for a local community. It aims to "supercharge" local engagement by providing a comprehensive solution for discovering and posting local events, forming and joining interest-based groups, facilitating a local marketplace for goods and services, disseminating local news, offering a directory of community resources, and listing local job and volunteer opportunities. The platform's primary objective is to connect local residents, businesses, and organizations, thereby fostering a more vibrant, engaged, and informed community. It addresses the problem of fragmented community information and interaction by consolidating these functions into a single, accessible platform.

docs.title: 1.2 Goals & Objectives
docs.text:
The primary goals and objectives for this platform are:

  • Goal 1: Foster a thriving, connected, and informed local community.
    • Objective 1.1: Increase community member participation in local events and activities.
    • Objective 1.2: Facilitate connections between community members with shared interests.
    • Objective 1.3: Provide a reliable source for local news and information.
  • Goal 2: Simplify access to local opportunities and resources.
    • Objective 2.1: Make it easy for community members to find local job and volunteer opportunities.
    • Objective 2.2: Provide a centralized directory for essential community resources and services.
  • Goal 3: Support local commerce and organizations.
    • Objective 3.1: Enable local businesses and residents to easily buy and sell goods and services within the community.
    • Objective 3.2: Provide local organizations and businesses a platform to promote their initiatives and reach community members.
  • Goal 4: Centralize fragmented community information.
    • Objective 4.1: Reduce the effort required for community members to find information about local happenings, services, and opportunities.

docs.title: 1.3 Target Audience & User Personas
docs.text:
The platform caters to several key user groups within a hyperlocal geographic area:

  1. Persona: "Active Community Member" (Corresponds to Community Members/Residents)

    • Description: Individuals of various ages living in the local area who are keen to stay informed, participate in community life, and connect with neighbors.
    • Goals:
      • Easily find and register for local events (e.g., festivals, workshops, meetings).
      • Discover and join groups aligned with their hobbies or interests (e.g., book clubs, gardening groups).
      • Buy unique items or find services from local sellers.
      • Sell unused items or offer personal services to neighbors.
      • Stay updated on local news and announcements.
      • Find local volunteer opportunities or part-time jobs.
    • Technical Proficiency: Varies, generally comfortable with web Browse.

  2. Persona: "Local Entrepreneur" (Corresponds to Local Businesses)

    • Description: Small to medium-sized business owners operating within the community. They are looking for affordable and effective ways to reach local customers and talent.
    • Goals:
      • List products or services in the marketplace to increase local sales.
      • Promote special events or workshops hosted by their business.
      • Post job openings to find local employees.
      • Enhance their business's visibility within the community.
    • Technical Proficiency: Comfortable with online tools for business.

  3. Persona: "Community Organizer" (Corresponds to Local Organizations & Non-profits)

    • Description: Representatives of local non-profits, clubs, or community organizations focused on community welfare, engagement, or specific causes.
    • Goals:
      • Promote community events and initiatives to a wider local audience.
      • Recruit volunteers for their programs and activities.
      • Share news and updates about their organization's work.
      • Create and manage online groups to engage with members and supporters.
    • Technical Proficiency: Generally proficient with web-based communication tools.

  4. Persona: "Platform Steward" (Corresponds to Platform Administrators & Moderators)

    • Description: Individuals designated with the responsibility of maintaining the platform's integrity, managing content, and supporting users.
    • Goals:
      • Ensure content adheres to community guidelines.
      • Manage user accounts and roles effectively.
      • Keep platform resources and news sections updated and relevant.
      • Oversee the overall health and functionality of the platform.
    • Technical Proficiency: High, with understanding of platform administration tools.

  5. Persona: "Curious Onlooker" (Corresponds to Guest Users)

    • Description: Individuals who may be new to the community or exploring what it has to offer without wanting to commit to creating an account immediately.
    • Goals:
      • Browse local events, news, and marketplace listings.
      • Get a feel for the community's activities and offerings.
      • Access publicly available resources.
    • Technical Proficiency: Basic web Browse skills.

docs.title: 2.1 Core Features
docs.text: The platform will include the following core modules: 1. User Account Management: Registration, login, profile management, roles and permissions. 2. Events Management: Creation, discovery, management of local events. 3. Groups Management: Creation, discovery, management of community groups. 4. Marketplace: Listing, Browse, and facilitating connections for buying/selling goods and services. 5. News: Publication and consumption of local news articles with commenting functionality. 6. Resources: A curated directory of helpful community resources. 7. Opportunities: A board for local job, volunteer, and event announcements. 8. Company Profile Management: (For Company Representatives)

docs.title: 2.2.1 User Account Management
docs.text:
• UAM-001: As a new user, I want to register for an account using my email address and a password, so that I can access features available to registered members.
  • UAM-002: As a registered user, I want to log in to the platform with my credentials, so that I can access my account and personalized content.
  • UAM-003: As a registered user, I want to log out of my account, so that my session is securely ended.
  • UAM-004: As a registered user, I want to view my user profile, so that I can see my information.
  • UAM-005: As a registered user, I want to edit my user profile (e.g., bio, profile picture), so that I can keep my information up-to-date and personalize my presence.
  • UAM-006: As an Administrator, I want to manage user roles and permissions, so that I can control access to platform functionalities.
  • UAM-007: As a user, I want to be able to reset my password if I forget it, so that I can regain access to my account.

docs.title: 2.2.2 Events Management
docs.text:
• EVT-001: As a Registered User (Organizer), I want to create a new event with details such as name, date, time (start/end), location, description, category, a cover image, and registration information, so that I can inform the community about the event.
  • EVT-002: As an Event Organizer, I want to manage attendees for my event (e.g., view list, if applicable), so that I can track participation.
  • EVT-003: As an Event Organizer, I want to update the details of an event I created, so that I can provide current information.
  • EVT-004: As an Event Organizer, I want to be able to communicate with event participants (e.g., send updates or reminders), so that I can keep them informed.
  • EVT-005: As any User (Guest or Registered), I want to discover and search for local events by category, date, location, and keywords/interests, so that I can find events relevant to me.
  • EVT-006: As a Registered User, I want to register for an event (if registration is enabled), so that I can confirm my attendance.
  • EVT-007: As any User, I want to view event details including name, date, time, location, full description, organizer, and how to register/attend, so that I have all necessary information.

docs.title: Detailed Flow for Creating an Event (from Blueprint "Key Feature Deep Dive"):
docs.text:
1. As a Registered User/Organizer, I want to log into my account.
  2. I want to navigate to the "Events" page (e.g., via a main navigation link).
  3. On the Events page, I expect to see a list of existing events and a prominent "Create Event" button.
  4. When I click the "Create Event" button, I want to be presented with a form.
  5. The form should allow me to input: Event Name (text), Date (date picker), Start Time/End Time (time pickers), Location (text input, with potential map integration), Description (rich text editor), Category (dropdown), Cover Image (file upload), Registration Information (e.g., external link, internal collection fields, ticket price), and Contact Person/Email.
  6. I want to fill in all required details and optionally upload an image.
  7. After filling the form, I want to click a "Save" or "Publish Event" button.
  8. The system should validate my input and display clear error messages next to any problematic fields if validation fails.
  9. Upon successful submission, I want my event to be saved to the database.
  10. I expect to be redirected to the newly created event's page or my list of managed events.
  11. I want to see a confirmation message (e.g., "Event Created Successfully!").
  12. The new event should then be visible in public event listings.

docs.title: 2.2.3 Groups Management
docs.text:
• GRP-001: As a Registered User, I want to create a new group with a name, description, and defined interests/hobbies/goals, so that I can start a community around a specific topic.
  • GRP-002: As a Group Administrator, I want to manage group members (e.g., approve/remove members, assign roles if applicable), so that I can maintain the group's integrity.
  • GRP-003: As a Group Administrator, I want to organize group activities or post announcements, so that I can engage group members.
  • GRP-004: As a Group Administrator, I want to share resources (e.g., links, documents) within the group, so that members can access relevant information.
  • GRP-005: As a Registered User, I want to discover and search for existing groups, so that I can find communities of interest.
  • GRP-006: As a Registered User, I want to join a group, so that I can participate in its activities and discussions.
  • GRP-007: As a Registered User, I want to leave a group I am a member of, so that I no longer participate.

docs.title: 2.2.4 Marketplace
docs.text:
• MKT-001: As a Registered User (Seller), I want to list an item or service for sale with a description, price, images, and contact information, so that I can sell to the local community.
  • MKT-002: As a Seller, I want to manage my marketplace listings (e.g., edit details, mark as sold, remove listing), so that I can keep my offerings current.
  • MKT-003: As a Seller, I want to be able to communicate with potential buyers (e.g., via a secure messaging system or by displaying my chosen contact info), so that I can answer questions and arrange sales.
  • MKT-004: As any User (Guest or Registered), I want to browse and search marketplace listings by category, keywords, and price range, so that I can find items or services I need.
  • MKT-005: As a Buyer, I want to contact sellers about their listings, so that I can ask questions or express interest in purchasing.
  • MKT-006: As a Buyer, I want to be able to purchase items (clarification needed on whether this is offline coordination or if the platform facilitates transactions), so that I can acquire goods/services.

docs.title: 2.2.5 News
docs.text:
• NWS-001: As an Administrator or Moderator, I want to publish news articles with a title, content, and publication date, so that I can share local news and announcements.
  • NWS-002: As any User (Guest or Registered), I want to read news articles, so that I can stay informed about what's happening in the community.
  • NWS-003: As a Registered User, I want to comment on news articles, so that I can engage in discussions and share my thoughts.
  • NWS-004: As an Administrator or Moderator, I want to manage comments on news articles (e.g., delete inappropriate comments), so that discussions remain constructive.

docs.title: 2.2.6 Resources
docs.text:
• RES-001: As an Administrator or Moderator, I want to add resources (e.g., links to local services, guides, important information) with a title, description, URL/link, and category, so that community members can find helpful information.
  • RES-002: As any User (Guest or Registered), I want to browse and search the resources library by category and keywords, so that I can find helpful information and services.
  • RES-003: As a Registered User, I want to suggest new resources to be added to the library (subject to moderation), so that I can contribute to the collective knowledge.

docs.title: 2.2.7 Opportunities
docs.text:
• OPP-001: As a Company Representative or Organization representative (Registered User), I want to post job listings with details like title, description, company, location, and application instructions, so that I can find local talent.
  • OPP-002: As a Company Representative or Organization representative (Registered User), I want to post volunteer opportunities with relevant details, so that I can recruit volunteers.
  • OPP-003: As a Company Representative or Organization representative (Registered User), I want to post event announcements related to my organization, so that I can promote our activities.
  • OPP-004: As any User (Guest or Registered), I want to browse and search the opportunities board (jobs, volunteer positions, event announcements) by type, keywords, and location, so that I can find relevant opportunities.
  • OPP-005: As a Registered User, I want to be able to apply for jobs or volunteer positions (e.g., by following a link or using an on-platform application mechanism if developed), so that I can pursue these opportunities.

docs.title: 2.2.8 Company Profile Management
docs.text:
• CPF-001: As a Company Representative (Registered User), I want to create and manage a company profile with details such as company name, description, contact information, and logo, so that I can present my organization on the platform.
  • CPF-002: As a Company Representative, I want my company profile to be associated with the job opportunities I post, so that applicants know who is hiring.

docs.title: 2.3.1 Information to be Managed:
docs.text:
• User Account Information: User ID, username, hashed password, email address, user role (Administrator, Moderator, Registered User, Guest, Company Representative), optional profile picture, optional user bio.
  • Event Details: Event ID, event name, date, start time, end time, location (address, potentially latitude/longitude), description, registration information/link, images, event category, organizer ID, list of attendee IDs.
  • Group Details: Group ID, group name, description, interests/goals, group rules, list of member IDs, group admin ID(s).
  • Marketplace Item Details: Item ID, item name/title, description, price, images, seller contact information (optional to display), category, seller ID, status (e.g., available, sold).
  • News Article Details: Article ID, title, content/body, publication date, author ID, list of comments (each with comment ID, text, commenter ID, timestamp).
  • Resource Details: Resource ID, title, description, URL/link, category, uploader ID.
  • Opportunity Details: Opportunity ID, title, description, type (job, volunteer, event announcement), company/organization name, location, application instructions/link, contact information, poster ID.
  • Company Profile Details: Company ID, company name, description, contact information, logo, representative ID(s).

docs.title: 2.3.2 Data Relationships:
docs.text:
• An Event has one Organizer (User) and can have many Attendees (Users).
  • A Group has one or more Administrators (Users) and many Members (Users).
  • A Marketplace Listing belongs to one Seller (User).
  • A News Article has one Author (Admin/Moderator User) and can have many Comments. Each Comment belongs to one User.
  • An Opportunity is posted by one User (Company Representative/Organization User) and may relate to one Company Profile.
  • A Company Profile is managed by one or more Company Representatives (Users).
  • A User can: create multiple Events, join/administer multiple Groups, list multiple Marketplace Items, post multiple Opportunities (if a Company Rep), make multiple Comments, and suggest multiple Resources.

docs.title: 3.1 User Interface (UI) & User Experience (UX)
docs.text:
• NFR-UI-001: The platform shall have a Community-focused & Welcoming, User-Friendly & Accessible, Organized & Informative, Clean & Modern look and feel.
  • NFR-UI-002: Navigation shall be intuitive, allowing users to easily find core sections (Events, Groups, Marketplace, News, Resources, Opportunities).
  • NFR-UI-003: The UI shall be responsive and provide a consistent experience across common web browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge) and screen sizes (desktop, tablet, mobile).
  • NFR-UI-004: Forms for creating content (events, listings, posts) shall be user-friendly, with clear labels, input validation, and helpful error messages.
  • NFR-UI-005: Search functionality within each module shall be efficient and provide relevant results.
  • NFR-UI-006: The platform should strive for accessibility, adhering to WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines where feasible.
  • NFR-UX-001: Visual inspiration for appearance (to be provided by the Visionary) should guide the design. Examples could include a clean local news site, a well-organized community forum, or a modern events platform.

docs.title: 3.2 Platform & Environment
docs.text:
• NFR-PLT-001: The primary environment for the platform shall be a Website, accessible through standard web browsers.
  • NFR-PLT-002: The platform will utilize Supabase for backend-as-a-service (data storage, authentication, real-time updates).
  • NFR-PLT-003: The frontend and backend are implied to be JavaScript-based, given npm usage (Node.js for APIs, a JavaScript framework for UI).
  • NFR-PLT-004: The platform requires an active internet connection for all functionalities. Offline support is not a requirement for this version.

docs.title: 3.3 Constraints & Business Rules
docs.text:
• NFR-BR-001: Guest users shall have read-only access to public content (events, marketplace, news, resources, opportunities). Registration is required for content creation, joining groups, commenting, or applying for opportunities.
  • NFR-BR-002: Only Registered Users can create and manage their own events, group memberships (joining/leaving), and marketplace listings.
  • NFR-BR-003: Only users designated as Company Representatives can create/manage their associated Company Profile and post opportunities on behalf of that company.
  • NFR-BR-004: Administrator users shall have full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access over all platform content and user management capabilities.
  • NFR-BR-005: Moderator users shall have permissions to approve/reject user-generated content (e.g., marketplace listings if moderation is enabled, comments, suggested resources) and manage users according to defined community guidelines.
  • NFR-BR-006: Community guidelines (to be defined by the Visionary) must be established and accessible to users. Moderators will enforce these guidelines.
  • NFR-BR-007: User authentication is mandatory for all actions beyond guest Browse.

docs.title: 3.4 Security & Privacy Considerations
docs.text:
• NFR-SEC-001: User passwords must be securely stored (e.g., hashed and salted).
  • NFR-SEC-002: The platform must implement measures to protect against common web vulnerabilities (e.g., XSS, CSRF, SQL Injection – Supabase helps significantly here, but input validation is still key).
  • NFR-SEC-003: Data privacy for user information (especially email addresses and any other PII collected) must be maintained.
  • NFR-SEC-004: Private user contact information (e.g., email, phone if collected beyond registration email) shall not be publicly displayed without explicit user consent per instance (e.g., a seller choosing to display contact info in a marketplace ad).
  • NFR-SEC-005: Anonymous posting of primary content (events, listings, articles) is not permitted. Resource suggestions may be anonymous but are subject to moderation.
  • NFR-SEC-006: The platform should not automatically enroll users in groups or events.
  • NFR-SEC-007: Session management should be secure.

docs.title: 4.0 Success Criteria & Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
The overall success of the platform will be measured by its adoption within the local community, user engagement levels across its various features, and its ability to meet the goals outlined in Section 1.2.

Specific acceptance criteria for key features (derived from "Definition of Done"):

  1. AC-EVT-CREATE & DISCOVER (Event Creation & Discovery):

    • Given a Registered User is logged in
    • When they navigate to "Events," click "Create Event," fill in all required fields (name: "Community Picnic," date, time, location: "Central Park," description), and click "Save"
    • Then a success message is displayed, AND the "Community Picnic" event is visible in their list of managed events.
    • And Given another User (Guest or Registered) navigates to the Events page
    • When they search for "picnic" or browse events for the specified date
    • Then the "Community Picnic" event is listed with its correct details.

  2. AC-GRP-JOIN (Joining a Group):

    • Given a Registered User is logged in
    • When they navigate to the "Groups" page, browse and find the "Local Gardeners Club," and click "Join Group"
    • Then their request is processed (either auto-joined or request sent for approval, depending on group settings).
    • And if successfully joined/approved, the "Local Gardeners Club" appears in their "My Groups" list, AND they can view group-specific content.

  3. AC-MKT-LIST & VIEW (Marketplace Listing & Viewing):

    • Given a Registered User is logged in
    • When they navigate to "Marketplace," click "List Item," fill in required fields (description: "Handmade Wooden Birdhouse," price: "$25"), upload a photo, and click "Save"
    • Then a success message is displayed, AND their listing for "Handmade Wooden Birdhouse" appears in the public marketplace.
    • And Given another User browses the marketplace
    • When they view the "Handmade Wooden Birdhouse" listing
    • Then they can see the photo, description, and price, AND there is a clear way to contact the seller.

docs.title: 5.0 Future Considerations / Roadmap
docs.text:
(Derived from "Nice-to-Haves" and "Long-Term Vision" – these are currently placeholders requiring Visionary input and are out of scope for the initial version.)

  • Potential Future Features (Post-MVP):
    • Direct messaging between users.
    • Integrated payment processing for marketplace transactions.
    • Map-based views for events and marketplace items.
    • User reviews and ratings for sellers, events, or services.
    • Subscription options for premium features (e.g., for businesses).
    • Gamification elements for community participation.
  • Potential Long-Term Evolution:
    • Expansion to multiple neighboring communities with interconnected platforms.
    • Becoming a primary digital hub for local government and community service announcements.
    • Deeper integrations with local schools or libraries.

docs.title: 6.0.1 Assumptions
docs.text:
• The "hyperlocal community" is a single, defined geographic area for the initial launch.
  • Users have reliable internet access to use the web-based platform.
  • Supabase will meet all backend requirements for scalability and performance for the initial user load.
  • The "Visionary" will provide specific content for community guidelines.
  • The "Visionary" will provide examples of "Similar Programs (Appearance)" to guide UI design.
  • The initial platform will be in English.

docs.title: 6.0.2 Open Questions for the Visionary
docs.text:
1. Marketplace Transactions: How should transactions in the marketplace be handled?
    • Option A: Platform facilitates contact only, transactions are handled offline between users.
    • Option B: Basic integration for online payments (e.g., Stripe, PayPal links) – (This would significantly increase scope).
    • The blueprint mentions "Process transactions (details on how this is handled would be needed, e.g., offline, integrated payment)" and "Purchase items (details on process needed)."
  2. Marketplace Listing Moderation: Should new marketplace listings require moderator approval before becoming public?
  3. Group Membership Approval: Should joining a group be automatic, or require approval by a Group Administrator by default? Should this be a configurable option per group?
  4. Content Moderation Details: What are the specific community guidelines for content and user behavior? What is the process for handling violations?
  5. Communication with Event Participants: What mechanism should be used for organizers to communicate with event participants (e.g., an in-platform messaging system, email notifications via the platform)?
  6. Company Representative Verification: Is there a process needed to verify that a user claiming to be a "Company Representative" is legitimate?
  7. Resource Suggestion Workflow: What is the exact workflow for users suggesting resources and for admins/moderators approving them?
  8. Applying for Opportunities: For job/volunteer applications, should the platform integrate an application system, or simply link out to external application sites/emails?
  9. Visual Style Guidance: Could you provide 2-3 examples of existing websites or apps whose visual look (not necessarily function) you admire for the "Community-focused & Welcoming, User-Friendly & Accessible, Organized & Informative, Clean & Modern" style? (From Blueprint Section 5.2)
  10. Likes/Dislikes of Similar Programs: Regarding existing similar platforms (Nextdoor, Facebook Events, etc.), what specific features or ways of doing things do you really like or dislike? (From Blueprint Section 9.2)
  11. Prioritization for Future Dreams: If resources were available post-launch, which of the "Nice-to-Haves" (Section 5.0) would be the highest priority?

docs.title: 7.0 Out of Scope (for initial version/MVP)
docs.text:
• Native Mobile Applications: Separate, installable mobile apps for iOS or Android are not in scope for this version. A responsive web design is expected.
  • Integrated Payment Processing: Unless explicitly clarified and prioritized (see Open Question 1), built-in payment processing for marketplace transactions is out of scope. The platform will facilitate contact.
  • Direct User-to-User Private Messaging: A comprehensive private messaging system between individual users is out of scope for the initial version (communication might be focused within event/group contexts or for marketplace inquiries).
  • Advanced Gamification: Complex badges, points systems, or leaderboards.
  • Multi-language Support.
  • Features listed in Section 5.0 (Future Considerations / Roadmap) unless explicitly prioritized and brought into scope by the Visionary.

docs.title: PRD Master Plan: Hyperlocal Community Platform
1. Overall Project Goal
docs.text:
AI Verifiable Project Goal: Build a fully functional hyperlocal community platform that enables local residents, businesses, and organizations to connect, share information, and engage in community activities through a web-based interface. The platform must pass all high-level acceptance tests defined in tests/high_level_tests.ts and meet all completion criteria specified in docs/acceptance_test_plan_updated_v2.md.

Success Criteria: - All 8 core feature modules (User Management, Events, Groups, Marketplace, News, Resources, Opportunities, Company Profiles) are fully functional - Platform supports role-based access control (Guest, Registered User, Moderator, Administrator, Company Representative) - All acceptance tests pass with 100% success rate - Platform is deployed and accessible via web browser - Data persistence through Supabase backend is operational

docs.title: 3. AI Verification Framework
docs.text:
The AI verification framework for this project consists of:

  1. Automated Test Execution: All tests defined in the acceptance test plan will be executed automatically to verify that the platform meets the requirements.
  2. File Existence Checks: The AI will verify that all required files exist and have the correct content.
  3. Database Schema Validation: The AI will verify that the database schema matches the expected structure.
  4. API Response Validation: The AI will verify that API endpoints return the expected responses.
  5. UI Component Rendering: The AI will verify that UI components render correctly.

docs.title: 4. Dependencies and Prerequisites
docs.text:
The project has the following dependencies and prerequisites:

  1. Supabase: The project uses Supabase for authentication, database, and storage.
  2. React: The frontend is built using React.
  3. TypeScript: The project uses TypeScript for type safety.
  4. Vite: The project uses Vite for fast development and building.
  5. React Router: The project uses React Router for routing.
  6. mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template: The project uses this template for authentication.

docs.title: 5. Risk Mitigation
docs.text:
The following risks have been identified and mitigated:

  1. Authentication Security: The template's authentication system will be hardened with additional security measures.
  2. Development Bypass: The development bypass for authentication will be properly secured.
  3. Template Integration: The template will be carefully integrated to avoid conflicts with existing code.

docs.title: 6. Success Metrics
docs.text:
The success of the project will be measured by:

  1. Test Pass Rate: All acceptance tests must pass.
  2. User Satisfaction: User feedback must be positive.
  3. Performance Metrics: The platform must meet performance requirements.
  4. Security Audit: The platform must pass security audits.

docs.title: 3. AI Verification Framework
docs.text:
Each micro-task includes specific, measurable completion criteria that can be programmatically verified:

  • Database State Verification: Check for presence and correctness of database records in Supabase tables (e.g., verify a new user record exists after registration with expected fields populated according to template schema)
  • Function Return Value Testing: Verify API and function responses match expected values (e.g., confirm adaptCompanyFromDatabase returns correctly formatted company object)
  • UI State Verification: Confirm correct page navigation and content display (e.g., verify redirect to profile page after successful login, confirm error messages display when validation fails)
  • Integration Testing: Validate cross-module functionality and data flow (e.g., verify that creating a company profile correctly associates with posted opportunities)
  • Adapter Transformation Testing: Verify data transformations between frontend and backend formats work correctly (e.g., test that adaptMemberFromDatabase correctly handles null values)
  • Performance Metrics: Measure and verify system performance benchmarks (e.g., confirm page load times under 3 seconds, API response times under 500ms)
  • Security Compliance: Automated security scanning and validation (e.g., verify that authentication checks prevent unauthorized access to protected routes)
  • Role-Based Access Control: Verify that permissions are correctly enforced based on user roles (e.g., confirm that only administrators can access admin-only features)

docs.title: 4. Dependencies and Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Technical Stack: JavaScript/TypeScript, React 18, Supabase, Node.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • Development Environment: Node.js runtime, npm package manager
  • External Services: Supabase backend-as-a-service (Authentication, Database, Storage)
  • Testing Framework: Jest for automated testing with co-located test files
  • State Management: React Query for server state, React Context for application state
  • Routing: React Router v6
  • Version Control: Git repository with proper branching strategy

docs.title: 5. Risk Mitigation
docs.text:
• Incremental Development: Each phase builds upon previous phases with clear dependencies
  • Continuous Testing: AI verification at each micro-task level prevents regression

docs.title: 6. Success Metrics
docs.text:
• Codebase Quality: Measured by code complexity, maintainability index, and adherence to coding standards.
  • Test Coverage: Percentage of code covered by automated tests.
  • Performance: Measured by page load times, API response times, and resource utilization.
  • Security: Number of identified vulnerabilities and time to remediation.
  • User Satisfaction: Measured by user feedback, surveys, and usage patterns.

docs.title: 3. AI Verification Framework
docs.text:
Each micro-task includes specific, measurable completion criteria that can be programmatically verified:

  • Database State Verification: Check for presence and correctness of database records in Supabase tables (e.g., verify a new user record exists after registration with expected fields populated according to template schema)
  • Function Return Value Testing: Verify API and function responses match expected values (e.g., confirm adaptCompanyFromDatabase returns correctly formatted company object)
  • UI State Verification: Confirm correct page navigation and content display (e.g., verify redirect to profile page after successful login using template routing, confirm error messages display when validation fails)
  • Integration Testing: Validate cross-module functionality and data flow (e.g., verify that creating a company profile correctly associates with posted opportunities)
  • Adapter Transformation Testing: Verify data transformations between frontend and backend formats work correctly (e.g., test that adaptMemberFromDatabase correctly handles null values)
  • Performance Metrics: Measure and verify system performance benchmarks (e.g., confirm page load times under 3 seconds, API response times under 500ms)
  • Security Compliance: Automated security scanning and validation (e.g., verify that template's authentication checks prevent unauthorized access to protected routes)
  • Role-Based Access Control: Verify that permissions are correctly enforced based on user roles (e.g., confirm that only administrators can access admin-only features using the extended template's permission system)
  • Template Component Integration: Verify that template components are correctly integrated and extended (e.g., confirm that SessionContext is accessible throughout the application, verify that protected routes correctly restrict access based on authentication state)

docs.title: 4. Dependencies and Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Technical Stack: JavaScript/TypeScript, React 18, Supabase, Node.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • Development Environment: Node.js runtime, npm package manager
  • External Services: Supabase backend-as-a-service (Authentication, Database, Storage)
  • Testing Framework: Jest for automated testing with co-located test files
  • State Management: React Query for server state, React Context for application state (leveraging template's SessionContext)
  • Routing: React Router v6 (integrated with template's protected routes)
  • Version Control: Git repository with proper branching strategy
  • Template Integration: mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template providing authentication foundation, session management, and protected routes

docs.title: 5. Risk Mitigation
docs.text:
• Incremental Development: Each phase builds upon previous phases with clear dependencies
  • Continuous Testing: AI verification at each micro-task level prevents regression
  • Modular Architecture: Independent modules reduce system-wide failure risk
  • Rollback Capability: Each phase can be independently deployed or rolled back
  • Documentation: Comprehensive documentation ensures maintainability

docs.title: 6. Success Metrics
docs.text:
• Functional Completeness: 100% of acceptance tests pass
  • Performance Standards: Page load times < 3 seconds, API response times < 500ms
  • Code Quality: No TypeScript errors, consistent adapter patterns, proper error handling
  • Test Coverage: All critical paths and edge cases covered by automated tests
  • Security: All inputs properly validated and sanitized, authentication and authorization secure
  • User Experience: Intuitive navigation, responsive design, accessibility compliance
  • Security Standards: No critical vulnerabilities, secure data handling
  • Deployment Success: Zero-downtime deployment, environment parity

This PRD Master Plan provides a comprehensive roadmap for building the hyperlocal community platform with clear, AI-verifiable milestones that ensure systematic progress toward a fully functional, tested, and deployed solution.

docs.title: Master Acceptance Test Plan: Hyperlocal Community Platform
1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document outlines the master acceptance test plan for the Hyperlocal Community Platform. It details the testing phases, test cases, and AI verifiable completion criteria. The plan aims to ensure that the platform meets its business goals, provides a positive user experience, and mitigates potential risks. This plan is based on the user's overall project goal, the blueprint, general research findings, the high-level test strategy report, and the current state of the codebase as documented in codereport/code_comprehension_report_updated.md.

The platform implements a custom authentication system built on Supabase that includes user registration, login, logout functionality, protected routes, and session management. This test plan has been updated to reflect the current implementation, ensuring that all components are properly tested according to London School TDD principles, focusing on behavior verification through collaborator interactions rather than internal state examination.

docs.title: 2.1 London School TDD Principles
docs.text:
This test plan explicitly adopts the London School of Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles, which emphasize:

  1. Interaction-Based Testing: Tests focus on the behavior of units through their interactions with collaborators rather than examining internal state.
  2. Collaborator Mocking: External dependencies and collaborators are mocked or stubbed to isolate the unit under test.
  3. Observable Outcome Verification: Tests verify observable outcomes (method calls, return values, UI changes) rather than internal state.
  4. Outside-In Development: Development proceeds from high-level acceptance tests down to unit tests.

docs.title: 2.2 Recursive Testing Strategy
docs.text: To ensure ongoing stability and catch regressions early, this test plan defines a comprehensive recursive testing strategy:

docs.title: Test Categories and Tags
docs.text:
Tests will be categorized and tagged for selective execution:

  • Unit Tests [unit]: Test individual components in isolation
  • Integration Tests [integration]: Test interactions between components
  • API Tests [api]: Test API endpoints and data flows
  • UI Tests [ui]: Test user interface components
  • Security Tests [security]: Test security features
  • Performance Tests [performance]: Test system performance
  • Feature Tests [feature:name]: Tests related to specific features (e.g., [feature:auth], [feature:events])
  • Critical Path Tests [critical]: Tests for critical functionality

docs.title: Regression Testing Triggers
docs.text:
Tests will be re-executed based on the following triggers:

  1. Code Changes: When code is modified, tests related to the modified components and their dependencies will be run.
  2. API Changes: When API contracts change, all tests interacting with those APIs will be run.
  3. Dependency Updates: When dependencies are updated, tests affected by those dependencies will be run.
  4. Pre-Release: Before releases, all tests will be run.
  5. Post-Deployment: After deployment, critical path tests will be run in the production environment.

docs.title: Test Selection Strategy
docs.text:
For different triggers, different subsets of tests will be selected:

  1. Minimal Set (for frequent development changes):
  2. Unit tests for changed components
  3. Integration tests directly involving changed components

  4. Tagged with [critical] if in critical path

  5. Extended Set (for significant changes or feature completion):

  6. All tests in the minimal set
  7. All integration tests for affected features
  8. UI tests for affected features

  9. Tagged with related feature

  10. Full Set (for releases or major changes):

  11. All tests

docs.title: Continuous Integration
docs.text:
All tests should be integrated into the CI/CD pipeline, with:

  1. Fast Feedback Loop: Unit and critical tests run on every commit
  2. Comprehensive Testing: Extended tests run on pull requests
  3. Full Regression: Complete test suite run before releases

docs.title: 3.1 User Account Management with Template-Based Authentication
docs.text:
• UAM-001: As a new user, I want to register for an account using my email address and a password, so that I can access features available to registered members.

    • Test Case: Verify that a new user can register with a valid email and password using the custom authentication system.
    • Completion Criterion: A new user account is created in the Supabase database with all required fields populated correctly, the user session is established, and the user is redirected to the home page after successful registration.
    • Units to Test:
    • AuthProvider component
    • Registration form component
    • Registration API methods
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Supabase client's auth.signUp method
    • Session context
    • Router for redirection
    • Expected Interactions:
    • Supabase client should receive correct registration data
    • Session context should be updated with new user information
    • Router should redirect to home page
    • Observable Outcome: Successful registration confirmed by redirect and session context update
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in minimal, extended, and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth] and [critical]

  • UAM-002: As a registered user, I want to log in to the platform with my credentials, so that I can access my account and personalized content.

    • Test Case: Verify that a registered user can log in with valid credentials using the custom authentication system.
    • Completion Criterion: The user is successfully authenticated with Supabase, a valid session token is created and stored, and the user is redirected to their profile page or the home page.
    • Units to Test:
    • AuthProvider component
    • Login form component
    • Login API methods
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Supabase client's auth.signInWithPassword method
    • Session context
    • Router for redirection
    • Expected Interactions:
    • Supabase client should receive correct login credentials
    • Session context should be updated with user information
    • Router should redirect to appropriate page
    • Observable Outcome: Successful login confirmed by redirect and session context update
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in minimal, extended, and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth] and [critical]

  • UAM-003: As a registered user, I want to log out of my account, so that my session is securely ended.

    • Test Case: Verify that a registered user can log out of their account using the custom authentication system.
    • Completion Criterion: The user's session is terminated in Supabase, the session context is updated to reflect the unauthenticated state, and the user is redirected to the login page or the home page as a guest.
    • Units to Test:
    • AuthProvider component
    • Logout functionality
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Supabase client's auth.signOut method
    • Session context
    • Router for redirection
    • Expected Interactions:
    • Supabase client should receive logout request
    • Session context should be cleared
    • Router should redirect to login or home page
    • Observable Outcome: Successful logout confirmed by redirect and session context update
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in minimal, extended, and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth] and [critical]

  • UAM-004: As a registered user, I want to view my user profile, so that I can see my information.

    • Test Case: Verify that a registered user can view their user profile.
    • Completion Criterion: The user's profile page is displayed with their information correctly retrieved from the Supabase database and transformed through the memberAdapter.
    • Units to Test:
    • Profile page component
    • Member data fetching hooks
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Member API client
    • Session context
    • Expected Interactions:
    • API client should fetch user profile data
    • Member adapter should transform the data
    • Observable Outcome: Profile page displays correct user information
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in extended and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth]

  • UAM-005: As a registered user, I want to edit my user profile (e.g., bio, profile picture), so that I can keep my information up-to-date and personalize my presence.

    • Test Case: Verify that a registered user can edit their user profile.
    • Completion Criterion: The user's profile information is updated in the Supabase database, the data is correctly transformed by the memberAdapter, and the updated information is displayed on their profile page.
    • Units to Test:
    • Profile edit form component
    • Profile update API methods
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Member API client's update method
    • Session context
    • Expected Interactions:
    • Form should collect and validate user input
    • API client should send update request with correct data
    • Member adapter should transform the data
    • Observable Outcome: Profile page displays updated user information after submission
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in extended and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth]

  • UAM-006: As an Administrator, I want to manage user roles and permissions, so that I can control access to platform functionalities.

    • Test Case: Verify that an administrator can manage user roles and permissions.
    • Completion Criterion: The user's role and permissions are updated in the Supabase database, the role-based access control system correctly enforces the new permissions, and the user's access to platform functionalities is changed accordingly.
    • Units to Test:
    • User management components
    • Role update API methods
    • Permission enforcement components
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • User role API client
    • Session context
    • Protected route components
    • Expected Interactions:
    • API client should update role information in database
    • Protected routes should enforce updated permissions
    • Observable Outcome: Changed user permissions correctly affect access to protected routes
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in extended and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth] and [security]

  • UAM-007: As a user, I want to be able to reset my password if I forget it, so that I can regain access to my account.

    • Test Case: Verify that a user can reset their password if they forget it.
    • Completion Criterion: The Supabase password reset functionality is triggered, the user receives a password reset email, they can successfully reset their password through the provided link, and they can log in with the new password.
    • Units to Test:
    • Password reset request component
    • Password reset confirmation component
    • Collaborators to Mock:
    • Supabase client's auth.resetPasswordForEmail method
    • Supabase client's auth.updateUser method
    • Session context
    • Expected Interactions:
    • Password reset form should trigger reset email
    • Password update form should update credentials
    • Login should succeed with new password
    • Observable Outcome: User can log in with new password after reset process
    • Recursive Testing Scope: Include in extended and full test sets; tagged with [feature:auth] and [security]

  • UAM-008: As a system administrator, I want to ensure that the development authentication bypass is disabled in production environments.

docs.title: Authentication Template Testing Status
docs.text: This document summarizes the testing status of the authentication template, specifically focusing on the recent debugging efforts related to the SignUpPageWithAPI component.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The SignUpPageWithAPI component was using window.alert to display a success message after user registration. This caused a test failure in the Jest environment, as window.alert is not implemented in JSDOM.

docs.title: Solution
docs.text: The window.alert call was removed from the SignUpPageWithAPI component. Instead, the component now relies on the existing success message displayed in the UI.

docs.title: Current Status
docs.text:
While removing the window.alert call fixed the initial test failure, it introduced new issues with other tests:

  • src/tests/userAccountManagement.test.tsx started failing.
  • src/auth_template/__tests__/userRegistrationAPI.test.tsx started failing.

These failures are likely due to changes in the component's behavior and the test environment configuration.

docs.title: Debugging Efforts
docs.text:
The following debugging efforts were undertaken:

  • Attempted to mock window.alert in the test setup.
  • Attempted to update the failing tests to reflect the new component behavior.
  • Attempted to configure Jest and Babel to handle import.meta syntax.
  • Attempted to mock the import.meta.env object in the test setup.

Unfortunately, none of these efforts were successful in resolving all test failures.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Further investigation is needed to understand the root cause of the test failures and to properly configure the test environment. This may involve:

  • Examining the test setup and dependencies.
  • Investigating the Jest and Babel configurations.
  • Exploring alternative testing strategies.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The testing status of the authentication template is currently unstable. Further work is needed to ensure that all tests pass and that the component is functioning correctly.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
This document outlines the detailed test plan for the Authentication Module of the Hyperlocal Community Platform. The authentication system is built upon the integrated mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template and includes user registration, login, logout, profile management, role-based access control, password reset, and security hardening features.

This test plan explicitly adopts London School of Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles, focusing on interaction-based testing and the mocking of collaborators to verify observable outcomes rather than internal state. It also defines a comprehensive recursive testing strategy to ensure ongoing stability and catch regressions early.

docs.title: 2. Test Scope
docs.text:
This test plan covers the granular testing of the Authentication Module, which maps directly to Phase 1 of the PRDMasterPlan (Foundation & Template-Based Authentication). The following AI Verifiable End Results from PRDMasterPlan.md are targeted for verification:

Microtask AI Verifiable End Result Test Coverage 1.1 Template files from mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template are successfully integrated into the project structure Environment and configuration verification tests 1.2 Supabase client connection established and authentication service configured to work with the template Supabase client integration tests 1.3 New users can register with email and password using the template's authentication system User registration test suite 1.4 Registered users can authenticate with valid credentials using the template's authentication system User login test suite 1.5 Users can securely end their session using the template's authentication system User logout test suite 1.6 Users can view and edit their profile information beyond the template's basic functionality User profile management test suite 1.7 Authentication system extended to support role-based permissions beyond the template's basic functionality Role-based access control test suite 1.8 Users can reset forgotten passwords via email, extending the template's functionality Password reset test suite 1.9 Template's authentication system is hardened with additional security measures Security hardening test suite 1.10 Template's authentication components are styled to match the platform's design system UI integration test suite 1.11 Development bypass for authentication is properly secured Development bypass security test suite

docs.title: 3.1 London School TDD Principles
docs.text:
This test plan adopts the London School of Test-Driven Development (TDD) principles, which emphasize:

  1. Interaction-Based Testing: Tests focus on the behavior of units through their interactions with collaborators rather than examining internal state.
  2. Collaborator Mocking: External dependencies and collaborators are mocked or stubbed to isolate the unit under test.
  3. Observable Outcome Verification: Tests verify observable outcomes (method calls, return values, UI changes) rather than internal state.
  4. Outside-In Development: Development proceeds from high-level acceptance tests down to unit tests.

docs.title: 3.2 Recursive Testing Strategy
docs.text: To ensure ongoing stability and catch regressions early, this test plan defines a comprehensive recursive testing strategy:

docs.title: 3.2.1 Test Categories and Tags
docs.text:
Tests will be categorized and tagged for selective execution:

  • Unit Tests [unit]: Test individual components in isolation
  • Integration Tests [integration]: Test interactions between components
  • UI Tests [ui]: Test user interface components
  • Security Tests [security]: Test security features
  • Authentication Module Tests [feature:auth]: Tests specifically for the authentication module
  • Critical Path Tests [critical]: Tests for critical functionality that must not fail

Additional tags for Authentication-specific features: - [auth:registration]: User registration tests - [auth:login]: User login tests - [auth:logout]: User logout tests - [auth:profile]: User profile management tests - [auth:rbac]: Role-based access control tests - [auth:password-reset]: Password reset tests - [auth:security]: Security hardening tests - [auth:ui]: Authentication UI integration tests - [auth:development]: Development bypass tests

docs.title: 3.2.2 Regression Testing Triggers
docs.text:
Tests will be re-executed based on the following triggers:

  1. Code Changes: When code is modified, tests related to the modified components and their dependencies will be run.
  2. API Changes: When Supabase API contracts change, all tests interacting with those APIs will be run.
  3. Dependency Updates: When dependencies (including the Supabase client, React, or testing libraries) are updated, tests affected by those dependencies will be run.
  4. Pre-Release: Before releases, all tests will be run.
  5. Post-Deployment: After deployment, critical path tests will be run in the production environment.
  6. Template Updates: When the base mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template is updated or modified, all authentication tests should be run.

docs.title: 3.2.3 Test Selection Strategy
docs.text:
For different triggers, different subsets of tests will be selected:

  1. Minimal Set (for frequent development changes):
  2. Unit tests for changed components
  3. Integration tests directly involving changed components

  4. Tagged with [critical] if in critical path

  5. Extended Set (for significant changes or feature completion):

  6. All tests in the minimal set
  7. All integration tests for authentication
  8. UI tests for authentication

  9. Tagged with [feature:auth]

  10. Full Set (for releases or major changes):

  11. All tests

docs.title: 3.2.4 Re-Testing Frequency Guidelines
docs.text:
The following guidelines should be followed for re-testing frequency:

  1. Continuous Testing: Unit tests and critical tests run on every commit
  2. Daily Testing: Extended tests run daily on the development branch
  3. Weekly Testing: Full test suite run weekly
  4. Pre-Release Testing: Full test suite run before any release
  5. Post-Deployment Testing: Critical path tests run after deployment

docs.title: 6.2 Mock Implementation Guidelines
docs.text:
1. Supabase Client Mocks: Create a mock Supabase client that mimics the behavior of the real client but returns predictable responses.
  2. Session Context Mocks: Create a mock session context that can simulate different authentication states.
  3. Router Mocks: Create a mock router that can track navigation and redirection.
  4. API Response Mocks: Create mock API responses for different scenarios (success, failure, error conditions).

docs.title: 6.3 Test Implementation Steps
docs.text:
1. Write Test First: Following TDD principles, write the test before implementing the feature.
  2. Create Mocks: Create all necessary mocks for collaborators.
  3. Define Expected Interactions: Clearly define the expected interactions and outcomes.
  4. Implement the Test: Implement the test to verify the expected interactions.
  5. Implement the Feature: Implement the feature to make the test pass.
  6. Refactor: Refactor the code while keeping the test passing.
  7. Add to CI: Ensure the test is included in the CI pipeline with appropriate tags.

docs.title: 7. Continuous Integration
docs.text:
All tests should be integrated into the CI/CD pipeline with the following guidelines:

  1. Fast Feedback Loop: Unit and critical tests run on every commit
  2. Comprehensive Testing: Extended tests run on pull requests
  3. Full Regression: Complete test suite run before releases

docs.title: 8. AI Verifiability
docs.text:
Each test case in this plan includes an explicit AI Verifiable Completion Criterion. These criteria define observable, measurable outcomes that can be programmatically verified. Test implementations should include assertions that directly verify these criteria.

To enable AI verification of test execution and results:

  1. Structured Test Output: Tests should produce structured output that can be parsed by AI agents.
  2. Clear Pass/Fail Conditions: Each test should have clear pass/fail conditions tied to the AI Verifiable Completion Criterion.
  3. Tagged Test Results: Test results should include the tags assigned to each test for selective verification.
  4. Coverage Reporting: Test runs should produce coverage reports to verify test scope.

docs.title: 9. Conclusion
docs.text:
This test plan provides a comprehensive approach to testing the Authentication Module of the Hyperlocal Community Platform. By following the London School TDD principles, focusing on interaction-based testing, and implementing a robust recursive testing strategy, we can ensure that the authentication system is reliable, secure, and maintainable.

The plan directly maps to the AI Verifiable End Results from PRDMasterPlan.md, ensuring that all requirements are properly tested and verified. Each test case includes specific interactions to test, collaborators to mock, expected interactions, observable outcomes, and AI verifiable completion criteria.

By implementing this test plan, we can ensure that the Authentication Module meets all requirements and contributes to the overall success of the Hyperlocal Community Platform.

docs.title: Functionality
docs.text:
The codebase provides the following features and capabilities:

  • Events Management: Allows users to create, manage, and discover local events.
  • Groups Management: Enables users to form and manage community groups.
  • Marketplace: Provides a platform for local businesses and individuals to list and sell products and services.
  • News: Delivers local news and articles.
  • Resources: Offers a directory of helpful resources for the community.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The project follows a modular architecture with the following key components:

  • API Endpoints: The src/api/ directory contains API endpoints for managing events, groups, marketplace listings, news, and resources. These endpoints use Supabase for data storage and retrieval.
  • UI Components: The src/components/ directory contains reusable UI components.
  • Pages: The src/pages/ directory contains the pages of the website.
  • Data Adapters: The src/adapters/ directory contains functions for adapting data between the application-specific format and the Supabase format.
  • Supabase: Supabase is used as the backend-as-a-service for data storage, authentication, and real-time updates.

The data flow is as follows:

  1. The user interacts with the UI components in the src/pages/ directory.
  2. The UI components call the API endpoints in the src/api/ directory.
  3. The API endpoints use the adapter functions in the src/adapters/ directory to convert the data between the application-specific format and the Supabase format.
  4. The API endpoints interact with Supabase to store and retrieve data.
  5. Supabase sends real-time updates to the UI components.

docs.title: User Stories
docs.text:
• Community Member: As a community member, I want to be able to easily find local events that are relevant to my interests so that I can participate in community activities.
  • Event Organizer: As an event organizer, I want to be able to create and manage events so that I can promote them to the community.
  • Local Business: As a local business, I want to be able to list my products and services on the marketplace so that I can reach more customers.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
The system has the following user roles:

  • Administrator: Has full access to the system and can manage all aspects of the website.
  • Moderator: Can moderate content and manage users.
  • Registered User: Can create and manage events, groups, and marketplace listings.
  • Guest: Can view content but cannot create or manage anything.

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text: This document provides a detailed guide on integrating the mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template into the Kootenay Tech Community Platform. It outlines the template's source, structure, intended use, alignment with project requirements, deviations, and required modifications.

docs.title: 2. Template Source
docs.text: • Repository URL: https://github.com/mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template

docs.title: 3. Template Structure
docs.text: The template follows a basic React project structure with the following key directories and files: - src/router/index.tsx: Contains the router configuration and protected routes. - src/context/SessionContext.tsx: Contains the SessionContext provider and the useSession hook. - src/Providers.tsx: Contains the provider setup.

docs.title: 4. Intended Use
docs.text: The template is intended to provide a basic authentication system for React applications using Supabase. It includes features such as: - User registration and login - Session management - Protected routes

docs.title: 5. Alignment with Project Requirements
docs.text: The template aligns with the project's requirements for authentication by providing a basic framework for user registration, login, and session management. It also includes protected routes, which can be used to restrict access to certain parts of the application based on user authentication status.

docs.title: 6. Deviations from Ideal Structure
docs.text: The template deviates from the project's ideal structure in the following ways: - It does not include user profile management features. - It does not include role-based access control. - It does not include password reset functionality. - It does not include security policies to protect against common attacks.

docs.title: 7. Required Modifications
docs.text: The following modifications are required to make the template fully usable and optimized for the project: - Integrate User Profiles: Implement user profile management features, including the ability to view and edit profile information. - Implement Role-Based Access Control: Extend the authentication system to support role-based permissions. - Secure Development Bypass: Ensure that the development bypass for authentication is properly secured and cannot be accidentally enabled in production. - Implement Password Reset: Implement password reset functionality. - Add Security Policies: Implement security policies to protect against common attacks, such as CSRF and rate limiting. - Implement Acceptance Tests: Implement acceptance tests (UAM-001 through UAM-007) to verify that the authentication system meets the project's requirements. - Integrate with Existing UI: The template's UI components need to be integrated with the existing Kootenay Tech Community Platform UI. This may require significant modifications to the template's styling and layout. - Update Supabase Client: Ensure the template uses the same Supabase client instance as the rest of the application to avoid conflicts.

docs.title: 8. Conclusion
docs.text: The mmvergara/react-supabase-auth-template provides a solid foundation for building an authentication system for the Kootenay Tech Community Platform. However, it requires significant modifications to meet the project's specific requirements. By following the steps outlined in this guide, developers can successfully integrate the template and create a secure and user-friendly authentication system.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document provides a comprehensive review of the testing framework implementation in the Nelson Tech project, focusing on the authentication components and their tests. The review aims to ensure that the testing framework is up to date with the current codebase, free of type errors, and that all tests are passing.

docs.title: Jest Configuration
docs.text:
The project uses Jest as its primary testing framework, with two main configuration files:

  1. Root Jest Configuration (jest.config.js):
  2. Configures the test environment as jsdom for browser-like testing
  3. Targets .tsx test files using the testRegex pattern
  4. Uses Babel for TypeScript transformation
  5. Sets up module name mapping for imports, including mocks for Supabase and API modules

  6. Configures setup files to run before tests

  7. Auth Template Jest Configuration (src/auth_template/jest.config.js):

  8. Similar to the root configuration but with specific paths for the auth template
  9. Uses ts-jest for TypeScript files and babel-jest for JavaScript files
  10. Has its own setup file (jest.setup.js)

docs.title: Babel Configuration
docs.text: The .babelrc file configures Babel with the following presets: - @babel/preset-env targeting the current Node environment - @babel/preset-react for React JSX support - @babel/preset-typescript for TypeScript support

docs.title: Test Setup
docs.text:
Two main setup files prepare the test environment:

  1. Root Setup (src/tests/setupTests.ts):
  2. Imports Jest DOM matchers
  3. Mocks the Vite import.meta.env object for environment variables
  4. Mocks window.alert

  5. Resets mocks before each test

  6. Auth Template Setup (src/auth_template/jest.setup.js):

  7. Imports Jest DOM matchers
  8. Mocks HTMLFormElement.prototype.requestSubmit for form submission
  9. Mocks window.alert
  10. Mocks import.meta.env with test values

docs.title: Mock Implementation
docs.text:
The project uses several mock files to isolate tests from external dependencies:

  1. API Mocks:
  2. src/tests/__mocks__/membersApi.ts: Mocks the members API with Jest functions

  3. src/tests/__mocks__/userAccountManagement.ts: Mocks both Supabase auth and members API

  4. Component Mocks:

  5. src/tests/__mocks__/SignUpPageWithAPI.tsx: A simplified version of the signup page for testing

These mocks use Jest's mocking capabilities to provide controlled test environments and predictable responses.
