docs.title: 3.1 Core Tables
docs.text:
-- Main embeddings table with optimized structure
CREATE TABLE content_embeddings (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    source_table TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_id UUID NOT NULL,
    content_type content_type_enum NOT NULL,

    -- Embedding data
    embedding vector(1536), -- OpenAI ada-002 dimensions
    embedding_model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'text-embedding-ada-002',
    embedding_version TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'v1',

    -- Chunking metadata
    chunk_index INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    chunk_text TEXT NOT NULL,
    chunk_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL,
    chunk_hash TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (encode(sha256(chunk_text::bytea), 'hex')) STORED,

    -- Contextual metadata
    metadata JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
    parent_context TEXT, -- Surrounding context for better retrieval

    -- Timestamps
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    indexed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- Constraints
    CONSTRAINT unique_source_chunk UNIQUE(source_table, source_id, chunk_index),
    CONSTRAINT valid_chunk_index CHECK (chunk_index >= 0),
    CONSTRAINT valid_tokens CHECK (chunk_tokens > 0 AND chunk_tokens <= 8192)
);

-- Indexes for performance
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_source ON content_embeddings(source_table, source_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_type ON content_embeddings(content_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_updated ON content_embeddings(updated_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_metadata ON content_embeddings USING GIN(metadata);

-- HNSW index for vector similarity search
CREATE INDEX idx_embeddings_vector_hnsw 
ON content_embeddings 
USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);

-- Embedding queue for async processing
CREATE TABLE embedding_queue (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    source_table TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_id UUID NOT NULL,
    action TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (action IN ('create', 'update', 'delete')),
    priority INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5 CHECK (priority BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
    content TEXT,
    metadata JSONB,
    status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'processing', 'completed', 'failed')),
    error_message TEXT,
    retry_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    processed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,

    -- Prevent duplicate queue entries
    CONSTRAINT unique_pending_source UNIQUE(source_table, source_id, status) 
    WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing')
);

-- Index for queue processing
CREATE INDEX idx_queue_status_priority ON embedding_queue(status, priority DESC, created_at);

-- Embedding statistics for monitoring
CREATE TABLE embedding_statistics (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE,
    content_type content_type_enum NOT NULL,
    total_embeddings INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    total_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    avg_chunk_size FLOAT,
    avg_processing_time_ms FLOAT,
    cache_hit_rate FLOAT,
    error_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

    CONSTRAINT unique_daily_stats UNIQUE(date, content_type)
);

docs.title: 3.2 Supporting Functions
docs.text:
-- Function to calculate semantic similarity
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION calculate_similarity(
    embedding1 vector(1536),
    embedding2 vector(1536)
) RETURNS FLOAT AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN 1 - (embedding1 <=> embedding2);
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE;

-- Function to get similar content
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION find_similar_content(
    query_embedding vector(1536),
    content_types content_type_enum[] DEFAULT NULL,
    similarity_threshold FLOAT DEFAULT 0.7,
    max_results INTEGER DEFAULT 10,
    user_id UUID DEFAULT NULL
) RETURNS TABLE (
    source_id UUID,
    source_table TEXT,
    content_type content_type_enum,
    chunk_text TEXT,
    similarity_score FLOAT,
    metadata JSONB
) AS $$
BEGIN
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT 
        ce.source_id,
        ce.source_table,
        ce.content_type,
        ce.chunk_text,
        calculate_similarity(ce.embedding, query_embedding) as similarity_score,
        ce.metadata
    FROM content_embeddings ce
    WHERE 
        (content_types IS NULL OR ce.content_type = ANY(content_types))
        AND calculate_similarity(ce.embedding, query_embedding) >= similarity_threshold
        -- Add permission check if user_id provided
        AND (user_id IS NULL OR check_content_permission(user_id, ce.source_id, ce.source_table))
    ORDER BY ce.embedding <=> query_embedding
    LIMIT max_results;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Trigger for automatic embedding updates
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION trigger_embedding_update()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Queue embedding generation for content changes
    INSERT INTO embedding_queue (source_table, source_id, action, content, priority)
    VALUES (
        TG_TABLE_NAME,
        NEW.id,
        CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN 'create' ELSE 'update' END,
        COALESCE(NEW.title, '') || ' ' || COALESCE(NEW.description, NEW.content, ''),
        CASE 
            WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME IN ('events', 'news') THEN 8
            WHEN TG_TABLE_NAME IN ('resources', 'opportunities') THEN 6
            ELSE 5
        END
    )
    ON CONFLICT (source_table, source_id, status) 
    WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing')
    DO UPDATE SET 
        content = EXCLUDED.content,
        metadata = EXCLUDED.metadata,
        created_at = NOW();

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

docs.title: 4.1 Content-Specific Chunking
docs.text:
interface ChunkingStrategy {
  maxTokens: number;
  overlapTokens: number;
  preserveBoundaries: boolean;
  contextWindow: boolean;
}

class ContentChunker {
  private strategies: Map<ContentType, ChunkingStrategy> = new Map([
    [ContentType.EVENT, {
      maxTokens: 600,
      overlapTokens: 100,
      preserveBoundaries: true,
      contextWindow: true
    }],
    [ContentType.NEWS, {
      maxTokens: 800,
      overlapTokens: 150,
      preserveBoundaries: true,
      contextWindow: true
    }],
    [ContentType.MESSAGE, {
      maxTokens: 400,
      overlapTokens: 50,
      preserveBoundaries: false,
      contextWindow: false
    }],
    [ContentType.PROFILE, {
      maxTokens: 300,
      overlapTokens: 0,
      preserveBoundaries: true,
      contextWindow: false
    }]
  ]);

  async chunkContent(
    content: string,
    contentType: ContentType,
    metadata?: any
  ): Promise<ContentChunk[]> {
    const strategy = this.strategies.get(contentType) || this.getDefaultStrategy();

    if (strategy.preserveBoundaries) {
      return this.semanticChunking(content, strategy, metadata);
    } else {
      return this.fixedSizeChunking(content, strategy);
    }
  }

  private semanticChunking(
    content: string,
    strategy: ChunkingStrategy,
    metadata?: any
  ): ContentChunk[] {
    // Implementation of semantic chunking
    // Preserves paragraph boundaries, headers, lists
    const chunks: ContentChunk[] = [];
    const sections = this.identifySections(content);

    for (const section of sections) {
      if (this.tokenCount(section.text) <= strategy.maxTokens) {
        chunks.push({
          text: section.text,
          index: chunks.length,
          tokens: this.tokenCount(section.text),
          metadata: { ...metadata, sectionType: section.type }
        });
      } else {
        // Split large sections with overlap
        const subChunks = this.splitWithOverlap(
          section.text,
          strategy.maxTokens,
          strategy.overlapTokens
        );
        chunks.push(...subChunks);
      }
    }

    if (strategy.contextWindow) {
      return this.addContextualInformation(chunks, content);
    }

    return chunks;
  }

  private fixedSizeChunking(
    content: string,
    strategy: ChunkingStrategy
  ): ContentChunk[] {
    // Simple fixed-size chunking with overlap
    return this.splitWithOverlap(
      content,
      strategy.maxTokens,
      strategy.overlapTokens
    );
  }
}

docs.title: 4.2 Contextual Retrieval Enhancement
docs.text:
class ContextualRetrieval {
  /**
   * Implements Anthropic's Contextual Retrieval pattern
   * Adds document-level context to each chunk
   */
  async enhanceChunksWithContext(
    chunks: ContentChunk[],
    document: Document
  ): Promise<EnhancedChunk[]> {
    const enhancedChunks: EnhancedChunk[] = [];

    for (const chunk of chunks) {
      const context = await this.generateChunkContext(chunk, document);

      enhancedChunks.push({
        ...chunk,
        contextualDescription: context,
        documentSummary: document.summary,
        documentTitle: document.title,
        enhancedText: `${context}\n\n${chunk.text}`
      });
    }

    return enhancedChunks;
  }

  private async generateChunkContext(
    chunk: ContentChunk,
    document: Document
  ): Promise<string> {
    // Generate a brief contextual description of where this chunk
    // fits within the larger document
    const prompt = `
      Document: ${document.title}
      Summary: ${document.summary}

      Chunk content: ${chunk.text}

      Provide a 1-2 sentence description of what this chunk discusses
      and how it relates to the overall document.
    `;

    return await this.llm.generateContext(prompt);
  }
}

docs.title: 5.1 Embedding Service Implementation
docs.text:
interface EmbeddingService {
  generateEmbedding(text: string): Promise<number[]>;
  generateBatchEmbeddings(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]>;
  getModel(): string;
  getMaxTokens(): number;
}

class OpenAIEmbeddingService implements EmbeddingService {
  private client: OpenAI;
  private model = 'text-embedding-ada-002';
  private maxTokens = 8191;
  private batchSize = 100;

  async generateEmbedding(text: string): Promise<number[]> {
    try {
      const response = await this.client.embeddings.create({
        model: this.model,
        input: text,
      });

      return response.data[0].embedding;
    } catch (error) {
      // Implement retry logic with exponential backoff
      return this.retryWithBackoff(() => this.generateEmbedding(text));
    }
  }

  async generateBatchEmbeddings(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]> {
    const embeddings: number[][] = [];

    // Process in batches to respect API limits
    for (let i = 0; i < texts.length; i += this.batchSize) {
      const batch = texts.slice(i, i + this.batchSize);

      const response = await this.client.embeddings.create({
        model: this.model,
        input: batch,
      });

      embeddings.push(...response.data.map(d => d.embedding));
    }

    return embeddings;
  }
}

class SentenceTransformerService implements EmbeddingService {
  private model = 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2';
  private maxTokens = 512;
  private dimensions = 384;

  async generateEmbedding(text: string): Promise<number[]> {
    // Local sentence transformer implementation
    // Using ONNX runtime for browser/edge deployment
    const tokenized = await this.tokenizer.encode(text);
    const truncated = tokenized.slice(0, this.maxTokens);
    const embedding = await this.model.embed(truncated);

    return Array.from(embedding);
  }

  async generateBatchEmbeddings(texts: string[]): Promise<number[][]> {
    // Batch processing for local model
    const embeddings = await Promise.all(
      texts.map(text => this.generateEmbedding(text))
    );

    return embeddings;
  }
}

docs.title: 5.2 Hybrid Embedding Strategy
docs.text:
class HybridEmbeddingStrategy {
  private openAI: OpenAIEmbeddingService;
  private sentenceTransformer: SentenceTransformerService;

  async generateEmbedding(
    text: string,
    contentType: ContentType
  ): Promise<EmbeddingResult> {
    // Use different models based on content type and importance
    const strategy = this.selectStrategy(contentType);

    if (strategy === 'openai') {
      return {
        embedding: await this.openAI.generateEmbedding(text),
        model: 'text-embedding-ada-002',
        dimensions: 1536
      };
    } else if (strategy === 'local') {
      return {
        embedding: await this.sentenceTransformer.generateEmbedding(text),
        model: 'all-MiniLM-L6-v2',
        dimensions: 384
      };
    } else {
      // Dual embedding for high-value content
      const [openAIEmb, localEmb] = await Promise.all([
        this.openAI.generateEmbedding(text),
        this.sentenceTransformer.generateEmbedding(text)
      ]);

      return {
        embedding: openAIEmb,
        alternativeEmbedding: localEmb,
        model: 'hybrid',
        dimensions: 1536
      };
    }
  }

  private selectStrategy(contentType: ContentType): 'openai' | 'local' | 'hybrid' {
    const highValueContent = [
      ContentType.EVENT,
      ContentType.NEWS,
      ContentType.RESOURCE
    ];

    const userGeneratedContent = [
      ContentType.MESSAGE,
      ContentType.PROFILE
    ];

    if (highValueContent.includes(contentType)) {
      return 'openai';
    } else if (userGeneratedContent.includes(contentType)) {
      return 'local';
    } else {
      return 'hybrid';
    }
  }
}

docs.title: 6.1 Hybrid Search System
docs.text:
class HybridSearchSystem {
  async search(
    query: string,
    options: SearchOptions
  ): Promise<SearchResult[]> {
    // Generate query embedding
    const queryEmbedding = await this.embeddingService.generateEmbedding(query);

    // Perform parallel searches
    const [semanticResults, keywordResults] = await Promise.all([
      this.semanticSearch(queryEmbedding, options),
      this.keywordSearch(query, options)
    ]);

    // Combine results using Reciprocal Rank Fusion
    return this.fuseResults(semanticResults, keywordResults, options);
  }

  private async semanticSearch(
    queryEmbedding: number[],
    options: SearchOptions
  ): Promise<SemanticResult[]> {
    const results = await this.db.query(`
      SELECT 
        source_id,
        source_table,
        content_type,
        chunk_text,
        metadata,
        1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) as similarity
      FROM content_embeddings
      WHERE 
        ($2::content_type_enum[] IS NULL OR content_type = ANY($2))
        AND 1 - (embedding <=> $1::vector) >= $3
      ORDER BY embedding <=> $1::vector
      LIMIT $4
    `, [queryEmbedding, options.contentTypes, options.minSimilarity || 0.7, options.limit || 20]);

    return results.rows;
  }

  private async keywordSearch(
    query: string,
    options: SearchOptions
  ): Promise<KeywordResult[]> {
    // Implement full-text search across content tables
    const searchQuery = this.buildFullTextQuery(query);

    const results = await this.db.query(`
      WITH search_results AS (
        SELECT 
          id as source_id,
          'events' as source_table,
          title,
          description as content,
          ts_rank(
            to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || description),
            plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
          ) as rank
        FROM events
        WHERE 
          to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || description) @@
          plainto_tsquery('english', $1)

        UNION ALL

        SELECT 
          id as source_id,
          'news' as source_table,
          title,
          content,
          ts_rank(
            to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || content),
            plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
          ) as rank
        FROM news
        WHERE 
          to_tsvector('english', title || ' ' || content) @@
          plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
      )
      SELECT * FROM search_results
      ORDER BY rank DESC
      LIMIT $2
    `, [query, options.limit || 20]);

    return results.rows;
  }

  private fuseResults(
    semanticResults: SemanticResult[],
    keywordResults: KeywordResult[],
    options: SearchOptions
  ): SearchResult[] {
    const k = options.rrfK || 60;
    const semanticWeight = options.semanticWeight || 0.7;
    const keywordWeight = options.keywordWeight || 0.3;

    // Calculate RRF scores
    const scores = new Map<string, number>();

    // Add semantic results
    semanticResults.forEach((result, index) => {
      const key = `${result.source_table}-${result.source_id}`;
      const rrfScore = 1 / (k + index + 1);
      scores.set(key, rrfScore * semanticWeight);
    });

    // Add keyword results
    keywordResults.forEach((result, index) => {
      const key = `${result.source_table}-${result.source_id}`;
      const rrfScore = 1 / (k + index + 1);
      const existing = scores.get(key) || 0;
      scores.set(key, existing + (rrfScore * keywordWeight));
    });

    // Sort by combined score
    const sortedResults = Array.from(scores.entries())
      .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1])
      .slice(0, options.limit || 10);

    // Fetch full content for top results
    return this.fetchFullContent(sortedResults);
  }
}

docs.title: 7.1 Caching Strategy
docs.text:
class EmbeddingCache {
  private redis: Redis;
  private localCache: LRUCache<string, number[]>;

  constructor() {
    this.localCache = new LRUCache({
      max: 1000,
      ttl: 1000 * 60 * 60 // 1 hour
    });
  }

  async get(text: string): Promise<number[] | null> {
    const hash = this.hashText(text);

    // Check local cache first
    const local = this.localCache.get(hash);
    if (local) return local;

    // Check Redis cache
    const cached = await this.redis.get(`embedding:${hash}`);
    if (cached) {
      const embedding = JSON.parse(cached);
      this.localCache.set(hash, embedding);
      return embedding;
    }

    return null;
  }

  async set(text: string, embedding: number[]): Promise<void> {
    const hash = this.hashText(text);

    // Store in both caches
    this.localCache.set(hash, embedding);
    await this.redis.setex(
      `embedding:${hash}`,
      3600 * 24, // 24 hours
      JSON.stringify(embedding)
    );
  }

  private hashText(text: string): string {
    return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
  }
}

docs.title: 7.2 Batch Processing
docs.text:
class BatchEmbeddingProcessor {
  private queue: EmbeddingTask[] = [];
  private processing = false;
  private batchSize = 50;
  private batchInterval = 5000; // 5 seconds

  async processQueue(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.processing || this.queue.length === 0) return;

    this.processing = true;

    try {
      // Get batch of tasks
      const batch = this.queue.splice(0, this.batchSize);

      // Group by content type for optimal processing
      const grouped = this.groupByContentType(batch);

      for (const [contentType, tasks] of grouped) {
        await this.processBatch(tasks, contentType);
      }
    } finally {
      this.processing = false;

      // Schedule next batch
      if (this.queue.length > 0) {
        setTimeout(() => this.processQueue(), this.batchInterval);
      }
    }
  }

  private async processBatch(
    tasks: EmbeddingTask[],
    contentType: ContentType
  ): Promise<void> {
    // Extract texts
    const texts = tasks.map(t => t.text);

    // Generate embeddings in batch
    const embeddings = await this.embeddingService.generateBatchEmbeddings(texts);

    // Store embeddings
    const storagePromises = tasks.map((task, index) => 
      this.storeEmbedding(task, embeddings[index])
    );

    await Promise.all(storagePromises);

    // Update statistics
    await this.updateStatistics(contentType, tasks.length);
  }
}

  async recordEmbeddingGeneration(
    contentType: ContentType,
    duration: number,
    tokens: number
  ): Promise<void> {
    this.metrics.embeddingGenerationTime.observe({ contentType }, duration);
    this.metrics.tokensUsed.inc({ contentType }, tokens);
    this.metrics.dailyEmbeddings.inc({ contentType });
  }

  async recordSearch(
    queryType: 'semantic' | 'keyword' | 'hybrid',
    duration: number,
    resultCount: number
  ): Promise<void> {
    this.metrics.searchLatency.observe({ queryType }, duration);
    this.metrics.searchQueries.inc({ queryType });
  }
}

docs.title: 9.2 Backfill Strategy
docs.text:
class EmbeddingBackfill {
  async backfillContent(): Promise<void> {
    const contentTypes = [
      ContentType.EVENT,
      ContentType.NEWS,
      ContentType.RESOURCE,
      ContentType.PROFILE,
      ContentType.COMPANY
    ];

    for (const contentType of contentTypes) {
      await this.backfillContentType(contentType);
    }
  }

  private async backfillContentType(contentType: ContentType): Promise<void> {
    const batchSize = 100;
    let offset = 0;
    let hasMore = true;

    while (hasMore) {
      const items = await this.fetchContent(contentType, batchSize, offset);

      if (items.length === 0) {
        hasMore = false;
        continue;
      }

      // Process in parallel with rate limiting
      await this.processWithRateLimit(items, contentType);

      offset += batchSize;

      // Progress logging
      console.log(`Processed ${offset} ${contentType} items`);
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the comprehensive plan to convert the Kootenay Tech Community platform from a single-tenant application into a multi-tenant SaaS platform. Each community will have its own domain, isolated data, and customizable configuration while sharing the same underlying infrastructure.

  2. React 18 + TypeScript for robust frontend

docs.title: Architecture Pattern: Schema-Per-Tenant with Shared Infrastructure
docs.text: Why This Approach: - Data Isolation: Each tenant gets complete data isolation - Compliance: Easier to meet data residency and privacy requirements - Customization: Per-tenant schema customizations possible - Performance: No cross-tenant query interference - Security: Tenant breaches cannot affect other tenants

docs.title: 1.1 Tenant Management System
docs.text:
Database Changes: 

-- Core tenant table
CREATE TABLE public.tenants (
    id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    name TEXT NOT NULL,
    slug TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- URL-friendly identifier
    domain TEXT UNIQUE, -- Custom domain (optional)
    subdomain TEXT UNIQUE, -- Default: {slug}.platform.com
    status TEXT DEFAULT 'active' CHECK (status IN ('active', 'inactive', 'suspended')),
    plan_type TEXT DEFAULT 'basic' CHECK (plan_type IN ('basic', 'pro', 'enterprise')),
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),

    -- Subscription info
    trial_ends_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    subscription_status TEXT DEFAULT 'trial',

    -- Billing
    billing_email TEXT,
    billing_address JSONB,

    -- Configuration
    settings JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    feature_flags JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
    branding JSONB DEFAULT '{}',

    -- Limits
    max_users INTEGER DEFAULT 100,
    max_storage_gb INTEGER DEFAULT 10,

    -- Contact info
    owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),
    admin_emails TEXT[],

    CONSTRAINT valid_domain_or_subdomain CHECK (domain IS NOT NULL OR subdomain IS NOT NULL)

-- Domain routing table for fast lookup

// src/features/companies/api/companiesApi.ts
class CompaniesAPI {
  private getTenantId(): string {
    const tenant = getCurrentTenant();
    if (!tenant) throw new Error('No tenant context available');
    return tenant.id;
  }

  async getCompanies(filters?: CompanyFilters) {
    const tenantId = this.getTenantId();
    // All queries now include tenant filter
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('companies')
      .select('*')
      .eq('tenant_id', tenantId)
      .match(filters || {});

    if (error) throw error;
    return data;
  }
}

// src/utils/tenantResolver.ts
export const resolveTenantFromRequest = async (request: Request): Promise<Tenant | null> => {
  const hostname = request.headers.host;

  // Check for custom domain first
  let tenant = await getTenantByDomain(hostname);

  // Fall back to subdomain
  if (!tenant) {
    const subdomain = extractSubdomain(hostname);
    if (subdomain) {
      tenant = await getTenantBySubdomain(subdomain);
    }
  }

  return tenant;
};

docs.title: Vision Statement
docs.text: Uluntu provides the digital places where hyper-local communities of practice gather, grow, and thrive—transforming scattered conversations into purposeful community spaces that respect privacy and foster meaningful connections.

docs.title: Market Opportunity
docs.text:
The fragmentation of online communities across social media platforms, messaging apps, and generic tools creates a massive opportunity for dedicated digital places serving hyper-local communities of practice. Our addressable market includes:

  • 500,000+ communities of practice globally across all industries and interests
  • $5+ billion total addressable market with current solutions generating \(200-\)2,000+ monthly revenue
  • 45% annual growth in professional and interest-based community formation

docs.title: Product Solution
docs.text:
A multi-Uluntu SaaS platform that provides complete digital places for communities of practice:

  • The Directory - privacy-first member networking space
  • The Calendar - event management and RSVP hub

  • The Market & The Board - economic activity spaces
  • The Studio - content creation and publishing center
  • The Watchtower - analytics and community health insights

docs.title: Kootenay Tech Community UI Component System
docs.text: This documentation provides guidelines and examples for using the shared UI components in the Kootenay Tech Community application. Our component system is designed to create a consistent user experience across all pages while reducing code duplication and improving maintainability.

docs.title: Design Principles
docs.text:
Our component system follows these principles:

  1. Consistency: Components should look and behave consistently across the application
  2. Modularity: Components should be reusable and composable
  3. Simplicity: Components should be simple to use and understand
  4. Accessibility: Components should be accessible to all users
  5. Responsive: Components should adapt to different screen sizes

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
To use our shared components, import them from their respective modules:

import { ContentContainer, PageHeader } from '../components/ui/PageLayout';
import { Card } from '../components/ui/Card';
import { SkeletonGrid } from '../components/ui/Skeleton';
import { QueryError } from '../components/ui/ErrorDisplay';

See the individual component documentation for specific usage details.

docs.title: Common UI Patterns
docs.text: This guide documents the common UI patterns used throughout the Kootenay Tech Community application. Following these patterns ensures consistency in structure, behavior, and appearance across the application.

docs.title: Page Structure Pattern
docs.text:
Every page in the application should follow this standard structure:

import { Helmet } from 'react-helmet-async';
import { ContentContainer, EmptyState } from '../../components/ui/PageLayout';
import { SkeletonGrid } from '../../components/ui/Skeleton';
import { QueryError } from '../../components/ui/ErrorDisplay';
import PageHeader from './PageHeader';
import ActionBar from './ActionBar';

export default function ExamplePage() {
  // Data fetching with Tanstack Query
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useExampleData();
  const hasData = data && data.length > 0;

  return (
    <>
      {/* SEO metadata */}
      <Helmet>
        <title>Page Title - Kootenay Tech Community</title>
        <meta name="description" content="Page description for SEO" />
      </Helmet>

      {/* Page header */}
      <PageHeader />

      {/* Main content container */}
      <ContentContainer>
        <ActionBar />

        {/* Conditional rendering based on data state */}
        {isLoading ? (
          <SkeletonGrid count={6} columns={{ sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 3 }} />
        ) : error ? (
          <QueryError 
            error={error} 
            retry={() => console.log('Retrying query')} 
            message="We couldn't load the data. Please try again."
          />
        ) : !hasData ? (
          <EmptyState
            title="No Items Found"
            description="There are no items available."
            primaryActionUrl="/create"
            primaryAction={{
              text: "Create Item",
              onClick: () => console.log('Navigate to create')
            }}
          />
        ) : (
          <ItemsList data={data} />
        )}
      </ContentContainer>
    </>
  );
}

docs.title: Edit/Create Form Pattern
docs.text:
Forms for editing or creating content follow this structure:

export default function ItemEditPage() {
  const { id } = useParams();
  const isEditing = !!id;
  const navigate = useNavigate();

  const [formData, setFormData] = useState(initialFormData);
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});
  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);
  const [submitSuccess, setSubmitSuccess] = useState(false);

  // Fetch existing data if editing
  const { data: item, isLoading } = useItemById(isEditing ? id : undefined);

  // Populate form when data is available
  useEffect(() => {
    if (isEditing && item) {
      setFormData({
        // Map API data to form fields
      });
    }
  }, [isEditing, item]);

  // Form change handler
  const handleChange = (e) => {
    const { name, value } = e.target;
    setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));

    // Clear error when field is edited
    if (errors[name]) {
      setErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: undefined }));
    }
  };

  // Form validation
  const validateForm = () => {
    const newErrors = {};

    // Validation logic

    setErrors(newErrors);
    return Object.keys(newErrors).length === 0;
  };

  // Form submission
  const handleSubmit = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();

    if (!validateForm()) {
      return;
    }

    setIsSubmitting(true);

    try {
      // API call to submit/update

      setSubmitSuccess(true);

      // Redirect after success
      setTimeout(() => {
        navigate('/items');
      }, 1500);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error submitting form:', error);
    } finally {
      setIsSubmitting(false);
    }
  };

  if (isLoading && isEditing) {
    return <LoadingState />;
  }

  return (
    <>
      <Helmet>
        <title>
          {isEditing ? `Edit Item: ${item?.name || 'Loading...'}` : 'Create New Item'} - Kootenay Tech Community
        </title>
      </Helmet>

      <ContentContainer maxWidth="lg">
        <FormHeader 
          title={isEditing ? `Edit ${item?.name || 'Item'}` : 'Create New Item'}
          backUrl="/items"
        />

        {submitSuccess ? (
          <Card className="mb-6">
            <div className="bg-green-50 dark:bg-green-900/20 border-l-4 border-green-500 p-4">
              <p className="text-sm text-green-700 dark:text-green-400">
                {isEditing ? 'Item updated successfully!' : 'Item created successfully!'} Redirecting...
              </p>
            </div>
          </Card>
        ) : (
          <Card>
            <form onSubmit={handleSubmit} className="p-6 space-y-6">
              {/* Form sections and fields */}

              <FormActions 
                isEditing={isEditing}
                isSubmitting={isSubmitting}
                submitText={isEditing ? 'Update Item' : 'Create Item'}
                onCancel={() => navigate('/items')}
                showDelete={isEditing}
                onDelete={() => setShowDeleteConfirm(true)}
              />
            </form>
          </Card>
        )}
      </ContentContainer>

      {/* Delete confirmation modal if needed */}
    </>
  );
}

docs.title: List Component Pattern
docs.text:
Components that display lists of items follow this pattern:

const ItemsList = ({ filter = '', category = '' }) => {
  const { 
    data = [], 
    isLoading, 
    error,
    refetch
  } = useItems({ filter, category });

  if (isLoading) {
    return <SkeletonGrid count={6} />;
  }

  if (error) {
    return (
      <QueryError 
        error={error} 
        retry={refetch}

      />
    );
  }

  if (data.length === 0) {
    return (

  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
      {data.map(item => (
        <ItemCard key={item.id} item={item} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
};

docs.title: Responsive Design Pattern
docs.text:
All components should be designed with mobile-first responsiveness:

  1. Use Tailwind's responsive prefixes (sm:, md:, lg:, xl:) to adapt layouts at different breakpoints
  2. Use grid systems with responsive column counts
  3. Stack elements vertically on mobile, horizontally on larger screens

Example:

<div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
  {/* Grid items */}
</div>

<div className="flex flex-col sm:flex-row items-center justify-between gap-4">
  <div className="w-full sm:w-auto">
    {/* Content */}
  </div>
  <div className="w-full sm:w-auto mt-4 sm:mt-0">
    {/* Content */}
  </div>
</div>

docs.title: Dark Mode Support
docs.text:
All components should support both light and dark modes:

  1. Use Tailwind's dark mode classes (dark:bg-slate-800, dark:text-white, etc.)
  2. Ensure sufficient contrast in both modes
  3. Test all components in both light and dark mode

Example:

<div className="bg-white dark:bg-slate-800 text-slate-900 dark:text-white">
  <h2 className="text-xl font-medium text-slate-800 dark:text-slate-200">
    Section Title
  </h2>
  <p className="text-slate-600 dark:text-slate-400">
    Description text
  </p>
</div>

Use Tanstack Query for all data fetching:

export function useItems(params: ItemsParams) {

    staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000, // 5 minutes

}

docs.title: State Management Pattern
docs.text:
1. Use React Query for server state (data from API)
  2. Use React Context for global UI state
  3. Use component state (useState) for local UI state
  4. Pass callbacks for actions that modify state

Example Context Pattern:

// Create context
const UserContext = createContext();

// Provider component
export function UserProvider({ children }) {
  const [user, setUser] = useState(null);

  const login = async (credentials) => {
    // Login logic
  };

  const logout = async () => {
    // Logout logic
  };

  return (
    <UserContext.Provider value={{ user, login, logout }}>
      {children}
    </UserContext.Provider>
  );
}

// Custom hook to use the context
export function useUser() {
  const context = useContext(UserContext);

  if (!context) {
    throw new Error('useUser must be used within a UserProvider');
  }

  return context;
}

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: The Kootenay Tech Community application implements a consistent approach to error handling across all pages and components to provide clear feedback to users when something goes wrong.

docs.title: QueryError
docs.text:
QueryError is the primary component for displaying errors related to data fetching or API requests.

import { QueryError } from '../../components/ui/ErrorDisplay';

function MyComponent() {
  const { data, error, refetch } = useMyData();

  if (error) {
    return (
      <QueryError 
        error={error}
        message="We couldn't load the data. Please try again."
        retry={refetch}
      />
    );
  }

  return <div>{/* Your component content */}</div>;
}

docs.title: NotFoundError

docs.title: FormError
docs.text:
FormError is used to display validation or submission errors within forms.

import { FormError } from '../../components/ui/ErrorDisplay';

function MyForm() {
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);

  const handleSubmit = async (data) => {
    try {
      await submitData(data);
    } catch (err) {
      setError('Unable to submit the form. Please try again.');
    }
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      {error && <FormError message={error} onDismiss={() => setError(null)} />}
      {/* Form fields */}
      <button type="submit">Submit</button>
    </form>
  );
}

docs.title: Page-Level Error States
docs.text:
Each page should have its own ErrorState component that is customized for that page's context. The component should provide:

  1. Clear explanation of what went wrong
  2. Options for the user to resolve the issue
  3. Consistent styling with the rest of the application

docs.title: Error Handling Pattern
docs.text:
For each page in the application, use the following pattern to handle errors:

function MyPage() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useMyData();

docs.title: Form Error Handling
docs.text:
For form validation errors, display specific error messages next to the relevant fields:

function MyForm() {
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});

  const validateForm = () => {
    const newErrors: Record<string, string> = {};

    if (!formData.name) {
      newErrors.name = 'Name is required';
    }

    if (!formData.email) {
      newErrors.email = 'Email is required';
    } else if (!/\S+@\S+\.\S+/.test(formData.email)) {
      newErrors.email = 'Email is invalid';
    }

    setErrors(newErrors);
    return Object.keys(newErrors).length === 0;
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <div className="mb-4">
        <label htmlFor="name">Name</label>
        <input
          id="name"
          value={formData.name}
          onChange={handleChange}
          className={errors.name ? 'border-red-500' : ''}
        />
        {errors.name && (
          <p className="text-red-500 text-sm mt-1">{errors.name}</p>
        )}
      </div>

      {/* Other form fields */}

      <button type="submit">Submit</button>
    </form>
  );
}

docs.title: ConfirmDialog
docs.text:
ConfirmDialog provides a standardized confirmation dialog for potentially destructive actions like deletion.

import { ConfirmDialog } from '../../components/ui/Dialog';

function ResourceEditPage() {
  const [showDeleteConfirm, setShowDeleteConfirm] = useState(false);
  const [isDeleting, setIsDeleting] = useState(false);

  const handleDelete = async () => {
    setIsDeleting(true);
    try {
      await deleteResource(id);
      navigate('/resources');
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error deleting resource:', error);
    } finally {
      setIsDeleting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <>
      <form>
        {/* Form content */}
        <button onClick={() => setShowDeleteConfirm(true)}>Delete</button>
      </form>

      <ConfirmDialog
        title="Delete Resource"
        message="Are you sure you want to delete this resource? This action cannot be undone."
        confirmText="Delete"
        cancelText="Cancel"
        isOpen={showDeleteConfirm}
        isProcessing={isDeleting}
        onConfirm={handleDelete}
        onCancel={() => setShowDeleteConfirm(false)}
        type="danger"
      />
    </>
  );
}

docs.title: Form Validation Pattern
docs.text:
function MyForm() {
  const [formData, setFormData] = useState({
    name: '',
    email: '',
    message: ''
  });

  const [errors, setErrors] = useState({});
  const [isSubmitting, setIsSubmitting] = useState(false);

  const handleChange = (e) => {
    const { name, value } = e.target;
    setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value }));

    // Clear error when field is edited
    if (errors[name]) {
      setErrors(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: undefined }));
    }
  };

  const validateForm = () => {
    const newErrors = {};

    if (!formData.name.trim()) {
      newErrors.name = 'Name is required';
    }

    if (!formData.email.trim()) {
      newErrors.email = 'Email is required';
    } else if (!/\S+@\S+\.\S+/.test(formData.email)) {
      newErrors.email = 'Email is invalid';
    }

    if (!formData.message.trim()) {
      newErrors.message = 'Message is required';
    }

    setErrors(newErrors);
    return Object.keys(newErrors).length === 0;
  };

  const handleSubmit = async (e) => {
    e.preventDefault();

    if (!validateForm()) {
      return;
    }

    setIsSubmitting(true);

    try {
      // API call to submit form
      await submitForm(formData);

      // Show success message or redirect
    } catch (error) {
      // Handle submission error
    } finally {
      setIsSubmitting(false);
    }
  };

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <FormSection title="Contact Form">
        <TextInput
          label="Name"
          id="name"
          name="name"
          value={formData.name}
          onChange={handleChange}
          error={errors.name}
          required
        />

        <TextInput
          label="Email"
          id="email"
          name="email"
          type="email"
          value={formData.email}
          onChange={handleChange}
          error={errors.email}
          required
        />

        <TextAreaInput
          label="Message"
          id="message"
          name="message"
          value={formData.message}
          onChange={handleChange}
          error={errors.message}
          required
          rows={4}
        />
      </FormSection>

      <FormActions
        submitText="Send Message"
        isSubmitting={isSubmitting}
        onCancel={() => navigate(-1)}
      />
    </form>
  );
}

import React from 'react';

docs.title: Usage Pattern
docs.text:
For each page in the application, use the following pattern to handle loading states:

function MyPage() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useMyData();

  if (isLoading) {
    return <LoadingState />;
  }

  if (error || !data) {
    return <ErrorState />;
  }

  return (
    <ContentContainer>
      {/* Actual page content */}
    </ContentContainer>
  );
}

For list components that may have their own loading states:

function MyListComponent() {
  const { data, isLoading, error } = useMyListData();

  if (isLoading) {
    return <SkeletonGrid count={6} columns={{ sm: 1, md: 2, lg: 3 }} />;
  }

  if (error) {
    return <QueryError error={error} retry={refetch} />;
  }

  if (!data || data.length === 0) {
    return <EmptyState title="No items found" />;
  }

  return (
    <div className="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-6">
      {data.map(item => (
        <ItemCard key={item.id} item={item} />
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}

docs.title: ActionBar
docs.text: ActionBar provides a consistent way to present filtering, search, and action controls for collections of items.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import { ActionBar } from '../../components/ui/PageLayout';

function MyListPage() {
  return (
    <ActionBar 
      searchPlaceholder="Search events..."
      onSearch={handleSearch}
      filters={/* filter components */}
      actions={/* action buttons */}
    />
  );
}

docs.title: Props
docs.text: Prop Type Default Description searchPlaceholder string 'Search...' Placeholder text for the search input onSearch function undefined Callback function when search input changes filters ReactNode undefined Filter controls to display actions ReactNode undefined Action buttons to display className string '' Additional CSS classes to apply

docs.title: Basic Search Bar
docs.text:
<ActionBar 
  searchPlaceholder="Search companies..."
  onSearch={(term) => setSearchTerm(term)}
/>

<ActionBar 
  searchPlaceholder="Search events..."
  onSearch={handleSearch}
  filters={
    <select value={category} onChange={(e) => setCategory(e.target.value)}>
      <option value="">All Categories</option>
      <option value="workshop">Workshops</option>
      <option value="meetup">Meetups</option>
    </select>
  }
  actions={
    <button className="btn primary">Create Event</button>
  }
/>

docs.title: EmptyState
docs.text: EmptyState provides a consistent way to display when no content is available, with optional actions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
import { EmptyState } from '../../components/ui/PageLayout';

function MyListPage() {
  const hasItems = items.length > 0;

  return (
    <>
      {!hasItems && (
        <EmptyState
          title="No items found"
          description="There are currently no items in this view."
          primaryAction={{
            text: "Create Item",
            onClick: handleCreateItem
          }}
        />
      )}
    </>
  );
}

docs.text: Prop Type Default Description title string required Main heading text for the empty state description string undefined Optional description text icon ReactNode undefined Optional icon to display primaryAction { text: string, onClick: function } undefined Main call-to-action button primaryActionUrl string undefined URL for primary action if it's a link secondaryAction { text: string, onClick: function } undefined Optional secondary action secondaryActionUrl string undefined URL for secondary action if it's a link className string '' Additional CSS classes to apply

docs.title: Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers deploying the Nelson Tech Community Platform to various hosting providers.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start
docs.text: The platform is a single-page application (SPA) built with Vite + React that connects to a hosted Supabase backend. It can be deployed to any static hosting provider.

docs.title: 📋 Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before deploying, ensure you have:

  1. Production Supabase instance configured
  2. Environment variables ready
  3. Domain name (optional but recommended)
  4. SSL certificate (provided automatically by most hosts)

docs.title: 🔧 Pre-deployment Steps
docs.text:
1. Test the production build locally: 

    npm run build
npm run preview

  2. Update environment variables for production:

  3. Set VITE_APP_URL to your production domain
  4. Ensure VITE_ENVIRONMENT=production

  5. Verify all API keys are production keys

  6. Remove sensitive data:

  7. Ensure .env is in .gitignore
  8. Never commit API keys or secrets

docs.title: Netlify - Recommended for simplicity
docs.text:
• Zero-configuration deployment
  • Automatic SSL and CI/CD
  • Generous free tier
  • Built-in form handling

docs.title: Cloudflare Pages - Best for performance
docs.text:
• Global edge network
  • Unlimited bandwidth
  • Superior DDoS protection
  • Fast build times

docs.title: Coolify - Best for control
docs.text:
• Self-hosted solution
  • Full control over infrastructure
  • Supports additional services
  • Docker-based deployment

docs.title: 📊 Platform Comparison
docs.text: Feature Netlify Cloudflare Pages Coolify Setup Ease ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ ⭐⭐⭐ Free Tier 100GB/month Unlimited Self-hosted Build Minutes 300/month 500/month Unlimited SSL Automatic Automatic Manual/Auto Custom Domain ✅ ✅ ✅ Edge Network ✅ ✅ (Best) ❌ Preview Deploys ✅ ✅ ✅ Rollbacks ✅ ✅ ✅ Server Functions ✅ ✅ ✅ (Full)

docs.title: 🔐 Security Considerations
docs.text:
1. Environment Variables:
  2. Never expose service role keys in frontend
  3. Use only public anon keys in client code

  4. Store sensitive keys in hosting provider's environment settings

  5. Headers Configuration:

  6. All deployment configs include security headers
  7. CSP policies are configured for Supabase integration

  8. CORS is handled by Supabase

  9. API Security:

  10. Row Level Security (RLS) enabled on all tables
  11. Authentication required for protected routes
  12. Rate limiting handled by Supabase

docs.title: 🚨 Post-deployment Checklist
docs.text:
• Verify all environment variables are set correctly
  • Test authentication flow (sign up, sign in, sign out)
  • Check that images load from Supabase Storage
  • Verify API calls work (load some data)
  • Test responsive design on mobile devices
  • Check browser console for errors
  • Verify custom domain and SSL certificate
  • Set up monitoring/analytics (optional)

docs.title: 📈 Monitoring & Maintenance
docs.text:
1. Application Monitoring:
  2. Use browser error tracking (e.g., Sentry)
  3. Monitor Supabase dashboard for API usage

  4. Check hosting provider analytics

  5. Performance Optimization:

  6. Enable caching headers (included in configs)
  7. Use CDN for static assets

  8. Monitor Core Web Vitals

  9. Regular Updates:

  10. Keep dependencies updated
  11. Monitor security advisories
  12. Backup Supabase data regularly

docs.title: Build Failures
docs.text:
• Check Node.js version (requires 18+)
  • Clear cache and reinstall dependencies
  • Verify all environment variables are set

docs.title: API Connection Issues
docs.text:
• Verify Supabase URL and anon key
  • Check Supabase project is active
  • Ensure RLS policies allow access

docs.title: Routing Problems
docs.text:
• Verify SPA redirect rules are configured
  • Check that _redirects or equivalent is in place
  • Test direct URL access to routes

docs.text:

  • Supabase Production Checklist
  • Security Best Practices

docs.title: Coolify Deployment Guide for Nelson Tech Community Platform
docs.text: This guide covers deploying the Nelson Tech Community Platform using Coolify v4 with Docker Compose.

docs.title: 📋 Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Coolify v4 installed and configured
  • Domain name pointed to your Coolify server
  • SSL certificates (Coolify can handle Let's Encrypt automatically)
  • Access to Coolify dashboard

docs.title: 1. Create New Project in Coolify
docs.text:
1. Log into your Coolify dashboard
  2. Click "New Project"
  3. Name it: nelson-tech-community

docs.title: 2. Add New Resource
docs.text:
1. Click "New Resource" in your project
  2. Select "Docker Compose"
  3. Choose deployment method:
  4. Public Repository (if open source)
  5. Private Repository (requires GitHub/GitLab integration)

docs.title: 3. Configure Repository
docs.text:
Repository URL: https://github.com/yourusername/nelson-tech.git
Branch: main
Docker Compose File: docker-compose.coolify.yml

docs.title: 4. Environment Variables
docs.text:
Add these environment variables in Coolify's environment section:

# Frontend URLs
SITE_URL=https://your-domain.com
API_EXTERNAL_URL=https://api.your-domain.com

# Database
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=your-secure-password
POSTGRES_DB=nelson_tech
POSTGRES_USER=postgres

# Supabase Keys (generate these)
JWT_SECRET=your-jwt-secret-min-32-chars
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key
SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY=your-service-key

# Frontend Environment
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://api.your-domain.com
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key

# Email Configuration (optional)
SMTP_HOST=smtp.your-provider.com
SMTP_PORT=587
SMTP_USER=your-email@domain.com
SMTP_PASS=your-email-password
SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@your-domain.com

# Optional Features
ENABLE_EMAIL_SIGNUP=true
ENABLE_EMAIL_AUTOCONFIRM=false
DISABLE_SIGNUP=false
JWT_EXPIRY=3600

docs.title: 5. Network Configuration
docs.text:
In Coolify's network settings:

  1. Frontend Service:
  2. Domain: your-domain.com
  3. Port: 80
  4. Enable HTTPS redirect

  5. Enable Let's Encrypt SSL

  6. API Gateway (Kong):

  7. Domain: api.your-domain.com
  8. Port: 8000
  9. Enable HTTPS redirect

  10. Enable Let's Encrypt SSL

  11. Supabase Studio (optional):

  12. Domain: studio.your-domain.com
  13. Port: 3000
  14. Enable authentication

docs.title: Custom Domain Setup
docs.text:
1. Add A records for:
  2. your-domain.com → Coolify server IP
  3. api.your-domain.com → Coolify server IP

  4. studio.your-domain.com → Coolify server IP (optional)

  5. Configure reverse proxy in Coolify: 

    services:
  frontend:
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.frontend.rule=Host(`your-domain.com`)"
      - "traefik.http.routers.frontend.tls=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.frontend.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt"

docs.title: Database Initialization
docs.text:
The database will be automatically initialized with migrations on first run. To manually run migrations:

# SSH into Coolify server
docker exec -it nelson-tech-postgres psql -U postgres -d nelson_tech -f /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql

docs.title: Storage Configuration
docs.text:
For production, consider using S3-compatible storage:

# Additional environment variables for S3
STORAGE_BACKEND=s3
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-key
AWS_DEFAULT_REGION=us-east-1
AWS_BUCKET=your-bucket-name

docs.title: View Logs in Coolify
docs.text:
1. Navigate to your deployment
  2. Click on any service
  3. Select "Logs" tab
  4. Use filters:
  5. frontend - Application logs
  6. postgres - Database logs
  7. auth - Authentication logs
  8. storage - File storage logs

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
All services include health checks. Monitor status:

# Check all services
docker-compose -f docker-compose.coolify.yml ps

# Check specific service health
docker inspect nelson-tech-frontend --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}'

docs.title: 1. Secure Environment Variables
docs.text:
• Use Coolify's encrypted environment variables
  • Never commit .env files to repository
  • Rotate JWT secrets regularly

docs.title: 2. Database Security
docs.text:
-- Create read-only user for analytics
CREATE USER analytics_user WITH PASSWORD 'secure-password';
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE nelson_tech TO analytics_user;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO analytics_user;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO analytics_user;

docs.title: 3. API Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Configure in Kong:

plugins:
  - name: rate-limiting
    config:
      minute: 100
      policy: local

docs.title: Initial Deployment
docs.text:
1. Push code to repository
  2. Coolify auto-detects changes
  3. Builds and deploys automatically
  4. Zero-downtime deployment with health checks

docs.title: Updates
docs.text:
# Automatic deployment on push to main
git push origin main

# Manual deployment in Coolify
# Click "Redeploy" button in dashboard

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
1. Go to Deployments history
  2. Find previous successful deployment
  3. Click "Rollback to this version"

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
1. Frontend not loading 

    # Check nginx logs
docker logs nelson-tech-frontend

# Verify environment variables
docker exec nelson-tech-frontend env | grep VITE_

  2. Database connection issues 

    # Test database connection
docker exec -it nelson-tech-postgres pg_isready

# Check database logs
docker logs nelson-tech-postgres

  3. Storage upload failures 

    # Check storage permissions
docker exec -it nelson-tech-storage ls -la /var/lib/storage

# Verify storage environment
docker exec nelson-tech-storage env | grep STORAGE

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable debug logging:

services:
  frontend:
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=development
      - DEBUG=true

docs.title: 1. Enable Caching
docs.text:
# In nginx.conf
location ~* \.(js|css|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|ico|svg)$ {
    expires 1y;
    add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
}

docs.title: 2. Database Optimization
docs.text:
-- Add indexes for common queries
CREATE INDEX idx_members_status ON members(status);
CREATE INDEX idx_events_date ON events(date);
CREATE INDEX idx_companies_featured ON companies(featured);

docs.title: 3. Enable CDN
docs.text: Configure Cloudflare or similar: - Cache static assets - Enable Brotli compression - Set up page rules for API endpoints

docs.text: For deployment issues: 1. Check Coolify logs first 2. Review this guide's troubleshooting section 3. Open an issue in the repository 4. Contact Coolify support for platform-specific issues

docs.title: Minimal Coolify Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide covers deploying the Nelson Tech Community Platform using Coolify with hosted Supabase (single container deployment).

docs.title: 🎯 Overview
docs.text: This minimal deployment: - Uses hosted Supabase (no self-hosted database) - Runs a single container serving the frontend - Requires minimal configuration - Perfect for small teams or MVPs

docs.title: 📋 Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Supabase Account with a project created
  2. Coolify v4 installed
  3. Domain name pointed to your Coolify server

docs.title: 1. Set Up Supabase
docs.text:
1. Create a new project at supabase.com
  2. Go to Settings → API
  3. Copy:
  4. Project URL → VITE_SUPABASE_URL
  5. anon public key → VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

docs.title: 2. Configure Coolify
docs.text:
1. Create New Project in Coolify
  2. Add Resource → Docker Compose
  3. Configure Repository: 
    Repository URL: https://github.com/yourusername/nelson-tech.git
Branch: main
Docker Compose File: docker-compose.coolify-minimal.yml

docs.title: 3. Environment Variables
docs.text:
Add these in Coolify's environment section:

# Required - From Supabase Dashboard
VITE_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co
VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key-here

# Required - Your Domain
VITE_APP_URL=https://your-domain.com
VITE_ENVIRONMENT=production

# Optional - Email Service
VITE_RESEND_API_KEY=your-resend-key
VITE_FROM_EMAIL=hello@your-domain.com
VITE_FROM_NAME=Nelson Tech Community

docs.title: 4. Deploy
docs.text:
1. Click Deploy in Coolify
  2. Wait for build to complete (~2-3 minutes)
  3. Your app will be available at your configured domain

docs.title: Database Setup
docs.text: Since you're using hosted Supabase: 1. Run migrations in Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor 2. Copy contents of supabase/migrations/*.sql 3. Execute in order

docs.title: Domain Configuration
docs.text: In Coolify's settings for your app: - Domain: your-domain.com - Enable HTTPS redirect - Enable Let's Encrypt SSL

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• ✅ Simple deployment (one container)
  • ✅ No database maintenance
  • ✅ Automatic Supabase updates
  • ✅ Built-in backups
  • ✅ Lower resource usage

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• ❌ Supabase free tier limits
  • ❌ Less control over database
  • ❌ Network latency to Supabase
  • ❌ Monthly costs for Supabase Pro

docs.title: Updating Your App
docs.text:
# Push to main branch
git push origin main

# Coolify auto-deploys
# Or manually click "Redeploy"

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text:
• Check Coolify logs for app issues
  • Monitor Supabase Dashboard for:
  • Database usage
  • API requests
  • Storage usage

docs.title: App Not Loading
docs.text:
# Check environment variables
docker exec nelson-tech env | grep VITE_

# Verify Supabase connection
curl https://your-project.supabase.co/rest/v1/

docs.title: Build Failures
docs.text:
• Ensure Node 20 compatibility
  • Check for TypeScript errors
  • Verify environment variables

docs.title: Supabase Connection Issues
docs.text:
1. Check API keys are correct
  2. Verify Row Level Security (RLS) policies
  3. Check Supabase service status

docs.title: Coolify Server
docs.text:
• VPS costs (~$5-20/month)
  • Domain name (~$12/year)

1. Environment Variables

docs.title: Coolify Routing Fix - "No Available Server" Error
Issue
docs.text: Your app builds and starts successfully, but shows "no available server" when visiting the domain.

docs.title: 1. Check Domain Configuration in Coolify
docs.text:
• Go to your application in Coolify
  • Click on "Domains" or "URLs" section
  • Verify that https://nelson-tech.apps.iaminawe.net is configured
  • Ensure "Generate SSL Certificate" is enabled if using HTTPS

docs.title: 2. Check Container Port Mapping
docs.text: Your app is running on port 80 inside the container. Verify in Coolify: - Application Settings → Port = 80 - Or check if it's expecting port 3000 (some configs use this)

docs.title: 3. Health Check Issues
docs.text: The container might be failing health checks. Check: - Application logs in Coolify - Container status: Is it marked as "healthy"?

docs.title: 4. Verify Container is Running
docs.text:
SSH into your Coolify server and check: 

# List running containers
docker ps | grep l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg

# Check container logs
docker logs app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 --tail 50

# Test the app directly
docker exec app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 curl -I http://localhost:80

docs.title: 5. Proxy/Traefik Configuration
docs.text:
Coolify uses Traefik as a reverse proxy. Check: - Coolify → Settings → Proxy is running - Check Traefik labels on your container: 

docker inspect app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 | grep -A 20 Labels

docs.title: Fix 1: Update Application Port
docs.text: In Coolify application settings: - Set "Port" to 80 (matching nginx in your container) - Save and wait for routing to update

docs.title: Fix 2: Force Proxy Reload
docs.text:
# On Coolify server
docker restart coolify-proxy

docs.title: Fix 3: Check DNS
docs.text:
Verify the domain points to your Coolify server: 

nslookup nelson-tech.apps.iaminawe.net
ping nelson-tech.apps.iaminawe.net

docs.title: 7. Container-Specific Checks
docs.text:
Since your container ID is app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276:

# Check if nginx is running inside
docker exec app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 ps aux | grep nginx

# Check nginx config
docker exec app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 nginx -t

# Check if the app files are there
docker exec app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 ls -la /usr/share/nginx/html

docs.title: 8. Manual Test
docs.text:
Test if the app works directly (bypassing proxy): 

# Get container IP
docker inspect app-l8owcko8g4wcwccwogo0kkcg-201337555276 | grep IPAddress

# Test directly (replace with actual IP)
curl -I http://[CONTAINER_IP]:80

docs.title: Most Likely Solution
docs.text:
Based on your setup, the most common fix is: 1. Go to Coolify → Your Application → Settings 2. Set "Port" to 80 (not 3000) 3. Ensure domain is set to https://nelson-tech.apps.iaminawe.net 4. Click "Save" 5. Wait 30-60 seconds for proxy to reconfigure

The issue is usually that Coolify's proxy isn't correctly routing traffic to your container's port 80.

docs.title: 1. Check Server Status in Coolify
docs.text:
• Go to Coolify Dashboard → Servers
  • Verify your server is listed and shows as "Connected"
  • Check the server health status

docs.title: 2. SSH into Your Coolify Server
docs.text: ssh root@your-coolify-server-ip

docs.title: 3. Check Docker Status
docs.text:
# Check if Docker is running
sudo systemctl status docker

# If not running, start it
sudo systemctl start docker

# Check Docker version
docker --version

# Test Docker
docker run hello-world

docs.title: 4. Check Coolify Services
docs.text:
# Check Coolify containers
docker ps | grep coolify

# Check Coolify logs
docker logs coolify

# Restart Coolify if needed
docker restart coolify

docs.title: 5. Check Server Resources
docs.text:
# Check disk space
df -h

# Check memory
free -h

# Check CPU load
top

docs.title: Fix 1: Restart Docker
docs.text: sudo systemctl restart docker

docs.title: Fix 2: Clean Up Docker Resources
docs.text:
# Remove unused containers, networks, images
docker system prune -a

# Remove unused volumes
docker volume prune

docs.title: Fix 3: Re-register Server in Coolify
docs.text:
1. Go to Coolify → Servers
  2. Remove the problematic server
  3. Add it back with the correct SSH credentials
  4. Test the connection

docs.title: Fix 4: Check Coolify Application Settings
docs.text:
1. Go to your application in Coolify
  2. Check "Server" dropdown - ensure a server is selected
  3. Check "Destination" - ensure it's set correctly

docs.title: If Using Coolify Cloud
docs.text:
• Check your subscription status
  • Verify server limits haven't been reached
  • Check Coolify status page for any ongoing issues

docs.title: Still Having Issues?
docs.text:
1. Check Coolify Logs: 

    docker logs coolify --tail 100

  2. Check Application Logs:

  3. In Coolify dashboard, go to your application

  4. Click on "Logs" to see deployment logs

  5. Verify Network Connectivity: 

    # From your local machine
ping your-coolify-server-ip

# Test SSH
ssh root@your-coolify-server-ip "echo 'Connection successful'"

  6. Check Firewall Rules:

  7. Ensure ports 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS) are open
  8. Check if Docker ports are accessible

docs.title: Emergency Recovery
docs.text:
If nothing else works:

  1. Restart the entire server: 

    sudo reboot

  2. Reinstall Coolify (last resort): 

    curl -fsSL https://get.coolify.io | bash

Remember to backup your data before any major changes!

docs.title: 🔍 White Screen Issue
docs.text: If you're seeing a white screen in Docker but the app works locally, here are the most common causes and solutions:

docs.title: 1. Environment Variables Not Being Passed During Build
docs.text:
Problem: Vite requires environment variables at build time, not runtime.

Solution: Update your Dockerfile to use build arguments:

# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY . .

# CRITICAL: Add build arguments
ARG VITE_SUPABASE_URL
ARG VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY

# Build with environment variables

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide provides step-by-step instructions for implementing the hybrid state management pattern when creating new features or refactoring existing ones. Follow these patterns to ensure consistency with the established architecture.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start: Creating a New Feature
docs.text: Let's walk through creating a hypothetical "notifications" feature using the hybrid pattern.

docs.title: Step 1: Create Feature Structure
docs.text: mkdir -p src/features/notifications/{api,components,hooks,store,types}

docs.title: Step 2: Define Types
docs.text:
// src/features/notifications/types/index.ts
export interface Notification {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  message: string;
  type: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'success';
  read: boolean;
  created_at: string;
  user_id: string;
}

export interface NotificationFilters {
  read?: boolean;
  type?: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'success';
  search?: string;
}

export interface NotificationInput {
  title: string;
  message: string;
  type: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error' | 'success';
  user_id: string;
}

docs.title: Step 3: Create API Layer (React Query)
docs.text:
// src/features/notifications/api/notificationsApi.ts
import { useQuery, useMutation, useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';
import { Notification, NotificationFilters, NotificationInput } from '../types';

// Query Keys
export const queryKeys = {
  notifications: ['notifications'] as const,
  notification: (id: string) => ['notifications', id] as const,
  notificationsWithFilters: (filters: NotificationFilters) => 
    ['notifications', 'filtered', filters] as const,
};

// API Functions
const notificationsApi = {
  async getAll(filters?: NotificationFilters): Promise<Notification[]> {
    let query = supabase
      .from('notifications')
      .select('*')
      .order('created_at', { ascending: false });

    if (filters?.read !== undefined) {
      query = query.eq('read', filters.read);
    }

    if (filters?.type) {
      query = query.eq('type', filters.type);
    }

    if (filters?.search) {
      query = query.or(`title.ilike.%${filters.search}%,message.ilike.%${filters.search}%`);
    }

    const { data, error } = await query;
    if (error) throw error;
    return data || [];
  },

  async getById(id: string): Promise<Notification | null> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('notifications')
      .select('*')
      .eq('id', id)
      .single();

    if (error) throw error;
    return data;
  },

  async create(notification: NotificationInput): Promise<Notification> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('notifications')
      .insert(notification)
      .select()
      .single();

    if (error) throw error;
    return data;
  },

  async markAsRead(id: string): Promise<Notification> {
    const { data, error } = await supabase
      .from('notifications')
      .update({ read: true })
      .eq('id', id)
      .select()
      .single();

    if (error) throw error;
    return data;
  },

  async delete(id: string): Promise<void> {
    const { error } = await supabase
      .from('notifications')
      .delete()
      .eq('id', id);

    if (error) throw error;
  },
};

// React Query Hooks
export const useNotifications = () => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: queryKeys.notifications,
    queryFn: () => notificationsApi.getAll(),
    staleTime: 2 * 60 * 1000, // 2 minutes for real-time data
  });
};

export const useNotificationsWithFilters = (filters?: NotificationFilters) => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: queryKeys.notificationsWithFilters(filters || {}),
    queryFn: () => notificationsApi.getAll(filters),
    enabled: !!filters && Object.keys(filters).length > 0,
    staleTime: 2 * 60 * 1000,
  });
};

export const useNotification = (id?: string) => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: queryKeys.notification(id!),
    queryFn: () => notificationsApi.getById(id!),
    enabled: !!id,
  });
};

export const useCreateNotification = () => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: notificationsApi.create,
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.notifications });
    },
  });
};

export const useMarkNotificationAsRead = () => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: notificationsApi.markAsRead,
    onSuccess: (data) => {
      // Update specific notification in cache
      queryClient.setQueryData(queryKeys.notification(data.id), data);
      // Invalidate list queries
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.notifications });
    },
  });
};

export const useDeleteNotification = () => {
  const queryClient = useQueryClient();

  return useMutation({
    mutationFn: notificationsApi.delete,
    onSuccess: () => {
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: queryKeys.notifications });
    },
  });
};

// src/features/notifications/store/notificationsUISlice.ts
import { createSlice, PayloadAction } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import { NotificationFilters } from '../types';

export interface NotificationsUIState {
  filters: NotificationFilters;
  selectedNotifications: string[];
  viewMode: 'list' | 'compact';
  showUnreadOnly: boolean;
  sortBy: 'date' | 'type' | 'read';
  sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc';
  pagination: {
    page: number;
    itemsPerPage: number;
  };
}

const initialState: NotificationsUIState = {
  filters: {},
  selectedNotifications: [],
  viewMode: 'list',
  showUnreadOnly: false,
  sortBy: 'date',
  sortDirection: 'desc',
  pagination: {
    page: 1,
    itemsPerPage: 20,
  },
};

const notificationsUISlice = createSlice({
  name: 'notificationsUI',
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    updateFilters: (state, action: PayloadAction<Partial<NotificationFilters>>) => {
      state.filters = { ...state.filters, ...action.payload };
      state.pagination.page = 1; // Reset page when filters change
    },

    clearFilters: (state) => {
      state.filters = {};
      state.pagination.page = 1;
    },

    setViewMode: (state, action: PayloadAction<'list' | 'compact'>) => {
      state.viewMode = action.payload;
    },

    toggleUnreadOnly: (state) => {
      state.showUnreadOnly = !state.showUnreadOnly;
      state.filters.read = state.showUnreadOnly ? false : undefined;
      state.pagination.page = 1;
    },

    toggleNotificationSelection: (state, action: PayloadAction<string>) => {
      const notificationId = action.payload;
      const index = state.selectedNotifications.indexOf(notificationId);

      if (index > -1) {
        state.selectedNotifications.splice(index, 1);
      } else {
        state.selectedNotifications.push(notificationId);
      }
    },

    selectAllNotifications: (state, action: PayloadAction<string[]>) => {
      state.selectedNotifications = action.payload;
    },

    clearSelection: (state) => {
      state.selectedNotifications = [];
    },

    setSorting: (state, action: PayloadAction<{ sortBy: string; sortDirection: 'asc' | 'desc' }>) => {
      state.sortBy = action.payload.sortBy as any;
      state.sortDirection = action.payload.sortDirection;
    },

    setPage: (state, action: PayloadAction<number>) => {
      state.pagination.page = action.payload;
    },

    setItemsPerPage: (state, action: PayloadAction<number>) => {
      state.pagination.itemsPerPage = action.payload;
      state.pagination.page = 1;
    },
  },
});

export const {
  updateFilters,
  clearFilters,
  setViewMode,
  toggleUnreadOnly,
  toggleNotificationSelection,
  selectAllNotifications,
  clearSelection,
  setSorting,
  setPage,
  setItemsPerPage,
} = notificationsUISlice.actions;

// Selectors
export const selectNotificationsFilters = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => 
  state.notificationsUI.filters;
export const selectSelectedNotifications = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => 
  state.notificationsUI.selectedNotifications;
export const selectViewMode = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => 
  state.notificationsUI.viewMode;
export const selectShowUnreadOnly = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => 
  state.notificationsUI.showUnreadOnly;
export const selectSorting = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => ({
  sortBy: state.notificationsUI.sortBy,
  sortDirection: state.notificationsUI.sortDirection,
});
export const selectPagination = (state: { notificationsUI: NotificationsUIState }) => 
  state.notificationsUI.pagination;

export default notificationsUISlice.reducer;
