// onboardingService.test.ts
describe('OnboardingService', () => {
  let service: OnboardingService;

  beforeEach(() => {
    service = new OnboardingService();
  });

  describe('Session Management', () => {
    it('should create new session', async () => {
      // Given: A user ID
      const userId = 'user-123';

      // When: Creating session
      const session = await service.createSession(userId);

      // Then: Should return valid session
      expect(session).toMatchObject({
        userId,
        currentStep: 1,
        completedSteps: [],
        skippedSteps: [],
        startedAt: expect.any(Date)
      });
    });

    it('should handle session retrieval failure', async () => {
      // Given: API error
      mockApi.get.mockRejectedValue(new Error('Network error'));

      // When: Getting session
      const session = await service.getSession('user-123');

      // Then: Should return null
      expect(session).toBeNull();
    });
  });

  describe('Data Persistence', () => {
    it('should save step data with retry logic', async () => {
      // Given: API fails once then succeeds
      mockApi.post
        .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error('Network error'))
        .mockResolvedValueOnce({ success: true });

      // When: Saving step data
      await service.saveStepData('user-123', 1, { name: 'John' });

      // Then: Should retry and succeed
      expect(mockApi.post).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2);
    });

    it('should validate data before saving', async () => {
      // Given: Invalid data for step 1
      const invalidData = { name: '' };

      // When/Then: Should throw validation error
      await expect(
        service.saveStepData('user-123', 1, invalidData)
      ).rejects.toThrow('Validation failed');
    });
  });
});

// profileCompletionService.test.ts
describe('ProfileCompletionService', () => {
  let service: ProfileCompletionService;

  beforeEach(() => {
    service = new ProfileCompletionService();
  });

  it('should calculate completion percentage correctly', async () => {
    // Given: User with partial profile
    mockGetUserProfile.mockResolvedValue({
      name: 'John Doe',
      title: 'Developer',
      location: 'Vancouver',
      bio: null,
      skills: [],
      employment_status: null,
      image: null
    });

    // When: Calculating completion
    const completion = await service.calculateCompletion('user-123');

    // Then: Should return correct percentage
    expect(completion.percentage).toBe(43); // 3 of 7 fields
    expect(completion.missingFields).toContain('bio');
    expect(completion.missingFields).toContain('skills');
  });

  it('should identify completion milestones', async () => {
    // Given: User at 75% completion
    mockGetUserProfile.mockResolvedValue({
      /* ... 75% complete profile ... */
    });

    // When: Getting milestones
    const milestones = await service.getMilestones('user-123');

    // Then: Should show appropriate milestones
    expect(milestones).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({
        name: 'Profile Starter',
        achieved: true,
        threshold: 50
      })
    );
    expect(milestones).toContainEqual(
      expect.objectContaining({
        name: 'Almost There',
        achieved: true,
        threshold: 75
      })
    );
  });
});

// onboardingFlow.test.tsx
describe('Onboarding Flow Integration', () => {
  it('should complete full onboarding flow', async () => {
    // Given: A new user starting onboarding
    const { getByTestId, getByLabelText, getByText } = render(
      <App initialRoute="/onboarding" userId="new-user" />
    );

    // Step 1: Welcome & Basic Info
    fireEvent.change(getByLabelText('Name'), { 
      target: { value: 'Jane Smith' } 
    });
    fireEvent.change(getByLabelText('Title'), { 
      target: { value: 'Senior Developer' } 
    });
    fireEvent.change(getByLabelText('Location'), { 
      target: { value: 'Toronto' } 
    });
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('next-button'));

    // Step 2: Professional Info (Skip)
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(getByText('Professional Information')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('skip-button'));

    // Step 3: Privacy Settings
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(getByText('Privacy Settings')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    fireEvent.click(getByLabelText('Members Only'));
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('next-button'));

    // Step 4: Company Association (Skip)
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(getByText('Company Association')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('skip-button'));

    // Step 5: Community Engagement (Skip)
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(getByText('Community Engagement')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('skip-button'));

    // Complete onboarding
    fireEvent.click(getByTestId('complete-button'));

    // Then: Should redirect to dashboard
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(window.location.pathname).toBe('/dashboard/welcome');
    });
  });

  it('should handle resume after interruption', async () => {
    // Given: User who left at step 3
    mockGetSession.mockResolvedValue({
      userId: 'user-123',
      currentStep: 3,
      completedSteps: [1, 2],
      skippedSteps: [],
      stepData: {
        1: { name: 'John', title: 'Dev', location: 'NYC' },
        2: { bio: 'Experienced developer', skills: ['React', 'Node'] }
      }
    });

    // When: User returns to onboarding
    const { getByText, getByTestId } = render(
      <OnboardingWizard userId="user-123" />
    );

    // Then: Should resume at step 3
    await waitFor(() => {
      expect(getByText('Privacy Settings')).toBeInTheDocument();
      expect(getByTestId('progress-bar')).toHaveAttribute('aria-valuenow', '40');
    });
  });
});

// completeOnboarding.test.ts
describe('Complete Onboarding E2E', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    cy.task('db:seed');
    cy.task('auth:createUser', { id: 'test-user' });
  });

  it('should complete full onboarding with all features', () => {
    // Given: New user logs in
    cy.login('test-user');
    cy.visit('/onboarding');

    // Step 1: Welcome
    cy.findByLabelText('Name').type('Alice Johnson');
    cy.findByLabelText('Title').type('Full Stack Developer');
    cy.findByLabelText('Location').type('Seattle, WA');

    // Upload photo
    cy.findByLabelText('Profile Photo').attachFile('profile.jpg');
    cy.findByTestId('photo-preview').should('be.visible');

    cy.findByTestId('next-button').click();

    // Step 2: Professional Info
    cy.findByLabelText('Bio').type('Experienced developer with 5 years...');

    // Add skills
    ['React', 'Node.js', 'PostgreSQL', 'Docker'].forEach(skill => {
      cy.findByLabelText('Skills').type(skill);
      cy.findByText('Add').click();
    });

    cy.findByLabelText('Employment Status').select('Employed');
    cy.findByLabelText('Years of Experience').type('5');
    cy.findByLabelText('Open to Volunteering').check();

    cy.findByTestId('next-button').click();

    // Step 3: Privacy Settings
    cy.findByLabelText('Profile Visibility').select('Members Only');
    cy.findByLabelText('Show Email').uncheck();
    cy.findByLabelText('Allow Messages').check();
    cy.findByLabelText('Newsletter').check();

    cy.findByTestId('next-button').click();

    // Step 4: Company Association
    cy.findByLabelText('Search Companies').type('Existing Corp');
    cy.findByText('Existing Corp Ltd.').click();
    cy.findByLabelText('Your Role').type('Senior Developer');
    cy.findByLabelText('Department').type('Engineering');
    cy.findByTestId('join-company-button').click();

    // Wait for verification
    cy.findByText('Verification email sent').should('be.visible');
    cy.findByTestId('next-button').click();

    // Step 5: Community Engagement
    cy.findByText('React').click();
    cy.findByText('Node.js').click();
    cy.findByText('Cloud Computing').click();

    cy.findByLabelText('Available as Mentor').check();
    cy.findByLabelText('Open to Networking').check();

    // Join suggested groups
    cy.findByText('React Developers Group').click();
    cy.findByText('Join').click();

    cy.findByTestId('complete-button').click();

    // Verify completion
    cy.url().should('include', '/dashboard/welcome');
    cy.findByText('Welcome to the Community!').should('be.visible');
    cy.findByTestId('profile-completion').should('contain', '85%');
  });

  it('should handle errors gracefully', () => {
    cy.login('test-user');
    cy.visit('/onboarding');

    // Simulate network error
    cy.intercept('POST', '/api/onboarding/step/*', { 
      statusCode: 500 
    }).as('saveError');

    cy.findByLabelText('Name').type('Test User');
    cy.findByLabelText('Title').type('Developer');
    cy.findByLabelText('Location').type('City');
    cy.findByTestId('next-button').click();

    cy.wait('@saveError');

    // Should show error but allow retry
    cy.findByText('Failed to save. Please try again.').should('be.visible');
    cy.findByTestId('retry-button').should('be.visible');
  });
});

docs.title: 🚨 Critical Issues to Fix
docs.text: Based on analysis of the codebase, these issues require immediate attention:

docs.title: 1. Redux Slices Using Direct Environment Checks
docs.text:
Problem: Redux slices are checking import.meta.env.VITE_USE_SUPABASE directly instead of using the centralized configuration.

Impact: This causes mock data to be shown even when Supabase is enabled.

Solution: Use getIsSupabaseEnabled() from @/config/env in all Redux slices.

docs.title: 2. Authentication Role Loading Race Condition
docs.text:
Problem: User roles are fetched asynchronously after authentication, causing the admin dashboard to disappear.

Impact: Admin users can't access admin features immediately after login.

Solution: Ensure roles are fully loaded before setting authentication loading state to false.

  • API Services: camelCase with 'Api' suffix (e.g., marketplaceApi.ts)
  • Redux Slices: camelCase with 'Slice' suffix (e.g., authSlice.ts)
  • Types: PascalCase (e.g., MarketplaceListing)

docs.title: 1. Fix Redux Slices Environment Configuration
docs.text:
Impact: High - Causes incorrect data source usage Effort: Low - Simple find/replace Files: All Redux slice files

Current Issue:

Migration Steps: 1. Import the centralized configuration: 

import { getIsSupabaseEnabled } from '@/config/env';

  1. Replace all instances in async thunks:

if (getIsSupabaseEnabled()) {
  // Use Supabase API

// Before

  return null;
}

// After
try {
  // ... code
} catch (error) {
  console.error('[FeatureName] Error description:', error);
  throw handleApiError(error);
}

#!/bin/bash
# fix-env-checks.sh

# Find and replace direct env checks in Redux slices
find src/features -name "*Slice.ts" -type f -exec sed -i '' \
  's/const USE_SUPABASE = import\.meta\.env\.VITE_USE_SUPABASE === '\''true'\'';/import { getIsSupabaseEnabled } from '\''@\/config\/env'\'';/g' {} \;

find src/features -name "*Slice.ts" -type f -exec sed -i '' \
  's/if (import\.meta\.env\.VITE_USE_SUPABASE === '\''true'\'')/if (getIsSupabaseEnabled())/g' {} \;

echo "Environment checks updated. Please review changes and fix any import issues."

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The Nelson Tech platform follows a feature-based architecture with clear separation of concerns:

src/
├── features/         # Feature modules (self-contained)
├── shared/          # Shared utilities and components
├── pages/           # Route pages (thin orchestration layer)
├── store/           # Redux store configuration
└── lib/             # External library configurations

docs.title: Key Principles
docs.text:
1. Feature Independence: Each feature should be self-contained
  2. Single Source of Truth: Use centralized configuration
  3. Consistent Patterns: Follow established patterns across all features
  4. Type Safety: TypeScript for all code
  5. Test Coverage: Maintain high test coverage

docs.title: Feature Module Structure
docs.text:
Every feature MUST follow this structure:

features/[feature-name]/
├── api/                 # API service layer
│   └── [feature]Api.ts
├── components/         # Feature-specific components
│   ├── [Component]/
│   │   ├── index.tsx
│   │   ├── types.ts
│   │   └── __tests__/
├── hooks/              # Custom React hooks
│   └── use[Feature]Redux.ts
├── store/              # Redux slice
│   └── [feature]Slice.ts
├── types/              # TypeScript types
│   └── [feature].ts
├── utils/              # Feature utilities
└── index.ts            # Public API exports

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
• Components: PascalCase (e.g., UserProfile.tsx)
  • Hooks: camelCase with 'use' prefix (e.g., useAuth.ts)
  • API Services: camelCase with 'Api' suffix (e.g., marketplaceApi.ts)
  • Redux Slices: camelCase with 'Slice' suffix (e.g., authSlice.ts)
  • Types: PascalCase (e.g., MarketplaceListing)
  • Utils: camelCase (e.g., formatDate.ts)
  • Constants: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., API_ENDPOINTS)

docs.title: Page Component Pattern
docs.text:
Pages should be thin orchestration layers that compose feature components:

// pages/MarketplaceDetailPage/index.tsx
import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
import { useParams } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Helmet } from 'react-helmet-async';
import { useMarketplaceListingByIdRedux } from '@/features/marketplace/hooks/useMarketplaceRedux';
import { ContentContainer } from '@/shared/components/ui/PageLayout';
import { Card } from '@/shared/components/ui/Card';
import LoadingState from './LoadingState';
import ErrorState from './ErrorState';
import DetailContent from './DetailContent';

export default function MarketplaceDetailPage() {
  const { id } = useParams();
  const [showModal, setShowModal] = useState(false);

  const { 
    listing, 
    isLoading, 
    error,
    fetchListing
  } = useMarketplaceListingByIdRedux(id || '');

  useEffect(() => {
    if (id) {
      fetchListing();
    }
  }, [id, fetchListing]);

  if (isLoading) return <LoadingState />;
  if (error || !listing) return <ErrorState error={error} />;

  return (
    <>
      <Helmet>
        <title>{listing.title} - Nelson Tech</title>
        <meta name="description" content={listing.description} />
      </Helmet>

      <ContentContainer>
        <DetailContent 
          listing={listing}
          onAction={() => setShowModal(true)}
        />
      </ContentContainer>
    </>
  );
}

docs.title: Feature Component Pattern
docs.text:
Feature components should be focused and reusable:

// features/marketplace/components/ListingCard/index.tsx
import { Link } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Card } from '@/shared/components/ui/Card';
import { formatCurrency, formatDate } from '@/shared/utils';
import { MarketplaceListing } from '../../types';
import { ListingCardProps } from './types';

export default function ListingCard({ 
  listing, 
  onAction,
  variant = 'default' 
}: ListingCardProps) {
  const handleClick = (e: React.MouseEvent) => {
    e.preventDefault();
    onAction?.(listing);
  };

  return (
    <Card className={`listing-card listing-card--${variant}`}>
      <Link to={`/marketplace/${listing.id}`}>
        <img 
          src={listing.images?.[0] || '/placeholder.jpg'}
          alt={listing.title}
          className="w-full h-48 object-cover"
        />
      </Link>

      <div className="p-4">
        <h3 className="text-lg font-semibold">{listing.title}</h3>
        <p className="text-gray-600 mt-2">{formatCurrency(listing.price)}</p>
        <p className="text-sm text-gray-500">{formatDate(listing.createdAt)}</p>

        {onAction && (
          <button
            onClick={handleClick}
            className="mt-4 btn btn-primary"
          >
            View Details
          </button>
        )}
      </div>
    </Card>
  );
}

docs.title: Redux Slice Pattern
docs.text:
All Redux slices MUST follow this pattern:

// features/[feature]/store/[feature]Slice.ts
import { createSlice, createAsyncThunk, PayloadAction } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import { [feature]Api } from '../api/[feature]Api';
import { RootState } from '@/store';
import { getIsSupabaseEnabled } from '@/config/env';
import mockData from '@/data/mock/mockData';

// State interface
export interface [Feature]State {
  items: [Feature]Item[];
  currentItem: [Feature]Item | null;
  filters: [Feature]Filters;
  status: 'idle' | 'loading' | 'succeeded' | 'failed';
  error: string | null;
}

// Initial state
const initialState: [Feature]State = {
  items: [],
  currentItem: null,
  filters: {},
  status: 'idle',
  error: null
};

// Async thunks - ALWAYS use getIsSupabaseEnabled()
export const fetch[Feature]Items = createAsyncThunk(
  '[feature]/fetchItems',
  async (_, { rejectWithValue }) => {
    try {
      if (getIsSupabaseEnabled()) {
        return await [feature]Api.getAll();
      } else {
        // Use mock data with proper adaptation
        return mockData.[feature]Items.map(adapt[Feature]Item);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      return rejectWithValue(
        error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Failed to fetch items'
      );
    }
  }
);

// Slice definition
const [feature]Slice = createSlice({
  name: '[feature]',
  initialState,
  reducers: {
    setFilters: (state, action: PayloadAction<[Feature]Filters>) => {
      state.filters = action.payload;
    },
    clearError: (state) => {
      state.error = null;
    }
  },
  extraReducers: (builder) => {
    builder
      // Fetch items
      .addCase(fetch[Feature]Items.pending, (state) => {
        state.status = 'loading';
        state.error = null;
      })
      .addCase(fetch[Feature]Items.fulfilled, (state, action) => {
        state.status = 'succeeded';
        state.items = action.payload;
      })
      .addCase(fetch[Feature]Items.rejected, (state, action) => {
        state.status = 'failed';
        state.error = action.payload as string;
      });
  }
});

// Export actions and reducer
export const { setFilters, clearError } = [feature]Slice.actions;

// Selectors
export const selectAll[Feature]Items = (state: RootState) => state.[feature].items;
export const select[Feature]Status = (state: RootState) => state.[feature].status;
export const select[Feature]Error = (state: RootState) => state.[feature].error;

export default [feature]Slice.reducer;

docs.title: Critical: Environment Configuration Usage
docs.text:
NEVER check import.meta.env.VITE_USE_SUPABASE directly in Redux slices. ALWAYS use:

import { getIsSupabaseEnabled } from '@/config/env';

// In async thunks
if (getIsSupabaseEnabled()) {
  // Use Supabase
} else {
  // Use mock data
}

docs.title: API Service Structure
docs.text:
// features/[feature]/api/[feature]Api.ts
import { supabase, handleSupabaseError } from '@/lib/supabase';
import { adapt[Feature]FromSupabase, adapt[Feature]ToSupabase } from '../adapters';
import { [Feature]Item, [Feature]Input } from '../types';

export const [feature]Api = {
  async getAll(filters?: [Feature]Filters): Promise<[Feature]Item[]> {
    try {
      let query = supabase
        .from('[feature]_table')
        .select('*, related_table(*)');

      // Apply filters
      if (filters?.search) {
        query = query.or(`title.ilike.%${filters.search}%`);
      }

      const { data, error } = await query;

      if (error) throw handleSupabaseError(error);

      return (data || []).map(adapt[Feature]FromSupabase);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error fetching [feature] items:', error);
      throw error;
    }
  },

  async getById(id: string): Promise<[Feature]Item | null> {
    try {
      const { data, error } = await supabase
        .from('[feature]_table')
        .select('*, related_table(*)')
        .eq('id', id)
        .single();

      if (error) throw handleSupabaseError(error);

      return data ? adapt[Feature]FromSupabase(data) : null;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error fetching [feature] item:', error);
      return null;
    }
  },

  async create(input: [Feature]Input): Promise<[Feature]Item> {
    try {
      const supabaseData = adapt[Feature]ToSupabase(input);

      const { data, error } = await supabase
        .from('[feature]_table')
        .insert(supabaseData)
        .select()
        .single();

      if (error) throw handleSupabaseError(error);

      return adapt[Feature]FromSupabase(data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error creating [feature] item:', error);
      throw error;
    }
  },

  async update(id: string, input: Partial<[Feature]Input>): Promise<[Feature]Item> {
    try {
      const supabaseData = adapt[Feature]ToSupabase(input);

      const { data, error } = await supabase
        .from('[feature]_table')
        .update(supabaseData)
        .eq('id', id)
        .select()
        .single();

      if (error) throw handleSupabaseError(error);

      return adapt[Feature]FromSupabase(data);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error updating [feature] item:', error);
      throw error;
    }
  },

  async delete(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
    try {
      const { error } = await supabase
        .from('[feature]_table')
        .delete()
        .eq('id', id);

      if (error) throw handleSupabaseError(error);

      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      console.error('Error deleting [feature] item:', error);
      return false;
    }
  }
};

// features/[feature]/hooks/use[Feature]Redux.ts
import { useCallback, useEffect } from 'react';
import { useAppDispatch, useAppSelector } from '@/store/hooks';
import {
  selectAll[Feature]Items,
  select[Feature]Status,
  select[Feature]Error,
  fetch[Feature]Items,
  create[Feature]Item,
  update[Feature]Item,
  delete[Feature]Item
} from '../store/[feature]Slice';
import { [Feature]Input } from '../api/[feature]Api';

export function use[Feature]ItemsRedux() {
  const dispatch = useAppDispatch();
  const items = useAppSelector(selectAll[Feature]Items);
  const status = useAppSelector(select[Feature]Status);
  const error = useAppSelector(select[Feature]Error);

  const fetchItems = useCallback(() => {
    return dispatch(fetch[Feature]Items());
  }, [dispatch]);

  const createItem = useCallback((data: [Feature]Input) => {
    return dispatch(create[Feature]Item(data)).unwrap();
  }, [dispatch]);

  const updateItem = useCallback((id: string, data: Partial<[Feature]Input>) => {
    return dispatch(update[Feature]Item({ id, data })).unwrap();
  }, [dispatch]);

  const deleteItem = useCallback((id: string) => {
    return dispatch(delete[Feature]Item(id)).unwrap();
  }, [dispatch]);

  // Fetch on mount if needed
  useEffect(() => {
    if (status === 'idle') {
      fetchItems();
    }
  }, [status, fetchItems]);

  return {
    items,
    isLoading: status === 'loading',
    isError: status === 'failed',
    error,
    fetchItems,
    createItem,
    updateItem,
    deleteItem
  };
}

// features/[feature]/components/__tests__/[Component].test.tsx
import { render, screen, fireEvent, waitFor } from '@testing-library/react';
import { BrowserRouter } from 'react-router-dom';
import { Provider } from 'react-redux';
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
import [Component] from '../[Component]';
import [feature]Reducer from '../../store/[feature]Slice';

// Test utilities
const renderWithProviders = (
  ui: React.ReactElement,
  {
    preloadedState = {},
    store = configureStore({
      reducer: { [feature]: [feature]Reducer },
      preloadedState
    }),
    ...renderOptions
  } = {}
) => {
  const Wrapper = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => (
    <Provider store={store}>
      <BrowserRouter>
        {children}
      </BrowserRouter>
    </Provider>
  );

  return { store, ...render(ui, { wrapper: Wrapper, ...renderOptions }) };
};

// Mock data
const mock[Feature]Item = {
  id: '1',
  title: 'Test Item',
  description: 'Test description',
  // ... other fields
};

describe('[Component]', () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    jest.clearAllMocks();
  });

  describe('Rendering', () => {
    it('should render component with data', () => {
      renderWithProviders(
        <[Component] item={mock[Feature]Item} />
      );

      expect(screen.getByText('Test Item')).toBeInTheDocument();
      expect(screen.getByText('Test description')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });

    it('should handle loading state', () => {
      renderWithProviders(
        <[Component] isLoading />
      );

      expect(screen.getByTestId('loading-spinner')).toBeInTheDocument();
    });

    it('should handle error state', () => {
      renderWithProviders(
        <[Component] error="Failed to load" />
      );

      expect(screen.getByText(/Failed to load/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
  });

  describe('User Interactions', () => {
    it('should handle click events', async () => {
      const mockOnClick = jest.fn();
      renderWithProviders(
        <[Component] item={mock[Feature]Item} onClick={mockOnClick} />
      );

      const button = screen.getByRole('button');
      fireEvent.click(button);

      await waitFor(() => {
        expect(mockOnClick).toHaveBeenCalledWith(mock[Feature]Item);
      });
    });
  });

  describe('Edge Cases', () => {
    it('should handle missing data gracefully', () => {
      renderWithProviders(
        <[Component] item={null} />
      );

      expect(screen.getByText(/No data available/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    });
  });
});

// shared/utils/errorHandling.ts
export class AppError extends Error {
  constructor(
    message: string,
    public code: string,
    public statusCode?: number
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'AppError';
  }
}

export function handleApiError(error: unknown): AppError {
  if (error instanceof AppError) {
    return error;
  }

  if (error instanceof Error) {
    return new AppError(error.message, 'UNKNOWN_ERROR');
  }

  return new AppError('An unexpected error occurred', 'UNKNOWN_ERROR');
}

// In API services
try {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.from('table').select();
  if (error) throw new AppError(error.message, error.code);
  return data;
} catch (error) {
  throw handleApiError(error);
}

docs.title: 2. Inconsistent Data Fetching
docs.text:
❌ WRONG: 

// Fetching in multiple places
useEffect(() => {
  fetchData();
}, []);

// Also in onClick
const handleClick = () => {
  fetchData();
};

✅ CORRECT: 

// Single source of truth
const { fetchItems } = useItemsRedux();

useEffect(() => {
  fetchItems();
}, [fetchItems]);

docs.title: 3. Mixed Data Sources
docs.text:
❌ WRONG: 

// Using both Redux and React Query in same component
const { data: queryData } = useQuery();
const reduxData = useSelector(selectData);
const finalData = queryData || reduxData;

✅ CORRECT: 

// Use only Redux hooks
const { items, isLoading } = useItemsRedux();

docs.title: 4. Untyped API Responses
docs.text:
❌ WRONG: 

const { data } = await supabase.from('table').select();
return data; // any type

✅ CORRECT: 

const { data } = await supabase.from('table').select();
return (data || []).map(item => adaptFromSupabase(item as DatabaseType));

docs.text:
❌ WRONG: 

<Parent user={user} settings={settings}>
  <Child user={user} settings={settings}>
    <GrandChild user={user} settings={settings} />
  </Child>
</Parent>

✅ CORRECT: 

// Use Redux or Context
const { user, settings } = useAuth();

docs.text:
❌ WRONG:

  // ... code
} catch (e) {
  console.log(e);
  return null;
}

✅ CORRECT:

  // ... code

docs.title: QA Validation Report: Super Admin Settings System
docs.text: Report Date: 2025-06-22 QA Lead: Quality Assurance Specialist System Version: Development Branch Testing Phase: Comprehensive System Analysis Report Status: Complete - Ready for Development Review

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text: The Super Admin Settings system has been comprehensively analyzed across all quality dimensions including functionality, security, performance, user experience, and accessibility. The system demonstrates excellent architectural design but requires critical implementation work to become functional.

docs.title: Overall Assessment
docs.text:
• Architecture Quality: A (95/100) - Excellent design and structure
  • Implementation Status: D (25/100) - Non-functional due to stubbed API
  • Security Design: B+ (87/100) - Strong security framework
  • User Experience: B (78/100) - Good foundation, needs improvements
  • Accessibility: B- (72/100) - Partially compliant, needs work

docs.title: Key Findings
docs.text:
1. 🏗️ Excellent Foundation: Database schema, UI components, and permission system are well-designed
  2. 🚨 Critical Gap: API layer is completely stubbed, making system non-functional
  3. 🔒 Security Ready: Strong security architecture requires validation testing
  4. ♿ Accessibility Gaps: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance needs improvement
  5. 📱 Mobile Optimization: Interface needs mobile-specific enhancements

docs.title: Systems Tested
docs.text:
• Database Layer: Schema, RLS policies, audit logging, indexing
  • API Layer: adminFeaturesApi module and integration points
  • Frontend Layer: React components, state management, UI/UX
  • Security Layer: Permission system, access controls, input validation
  • Performance: Load times, query performance, scalability
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, screen reader support

docs.title: Testing Standards Applied
docs.text:
• Functional: Custom test scenarios and edge cases
  • Security: OWASP guidelines, RLS policy validation
  • Performance: Web Performance standards, database optimization
  • Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA, Section 508 compliance
  • Usability: Nielsen's heuristics, user journey testing

docs.title: 1. Database Infrastructure Analysis ✅ EXCELLENT
docs.text:
Score: 95/100

Strengths: - Complete and well-structured schema design - Comprehensive RLS policies for security - Proper audit logging with triggers - Appropriate indexing strategy - Data integrity constraints

Evidence: 

-- Example of excellent RLS policy design
CREATE POLICY "Superadmins can manage admin features" ON admin_features
  FOR ALL USING (
    EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_roles ur WHERE ur.user_id = auth.uid() AND ur.role = 'superadmin')
  );

Minor Issues: - Some indexes could be optimized for specific query patterns - Audit log retention policy not defined

docs.title: 2. API Implementation ❌ CRITICAL FAILURE
docs.text:
Score: 25/100

Critical Issues: - All API methods return empty/mock data - No database integration implemented - Console warnings indicate "temporarily disabled" - Complete system non-functionality

Impact: - Settings page displays empty state - No persistence of any user changes - Unable to test real-world scenarios - Blocks all further functional testing

Code Evidence: 

// Current non-functional implementation
async getFeatures() {
  console.warn('Admin features temporarily disabled - returning empty data');
  return [] as AdminFeature[];
}

Required Action: Complete API implementation is prerequisite for system functionality

docs.title: 3. Frontend Components ✅ GOOD
docs.text:
Score: 82/100

Strengths: - Well-structured React components - Proper state management with React Query - Clean and professional UI design - Responsive layout implementation - Proper TypeScript typing

Areas for Improvement: - Loading states could be more informative - Error handling needs enhancement - Mobile optimization required - Accessibility improvements needed

UI Quality Assessment: - Tab navigation: ✅ Intuitive and functional - Feature management interface: ✅ Clear and organized - Translation management: ✅ Well-designed workflow - Configuration editing: ⚠️ Could be more user-friendly

docs.title: 4. Security Architecture ✅ STRONG
docs.text:
Score: 87/100

Security Strengths: - Comprehensive permission system with role inheritance - RLS policies properly configured for data protection - Audit logging captures all administrative actions - Input validation framework in place - Proper authentication integration

Security Analysis: 

// Excellent permission checking
const { isSuperAdmin, hasPermission } = usePermissions();
if (!isSuperAdmin()) {
  return <UnauthorizedAccess />;
}

Security Gaps Requiring Attention: - Server-side input validation needs implementation - XSS prevention testing required once API is functional - Rate limiting not implemented - Error messages could leak information

docs.title: 5. Accessibility Assessment ⚠️ NEEDS IMPROVEMENT
docs.text:
Score: 72/100

WCAG 2.1 AA Compliance Status: - ✅ Color contrast requirements met - ✅ Keyboard navigation functional - ✅ Semantic HTML structure proper - ❌ ARIA labels missing on toggle buttons - ❌ Dynamic content changes not announced - ❌ Form accessibility needs enhancement

Screen Reader Testing Results: - Page structure: ✅ Well announced - Navigation: ✅ Clear and logical - Interactive elements: ⚠️ Some missing labels - Form fields: ✅ Properly labeled - Dynamic updates: ❌ Not announced

Critical Accessibility Fixes Needed: 

// Current problematic implementation
<button onClick={toggleFeature}>
  {enabled ? <ToggleRight /> : <ToggleLeft />}
</button>

// Required accessible implementation
<button 
  onClick={toggleFeature}
  aria-label={`${enabled ? 'Disable' : 'Enable'} ${featureName} feature`}
  aria-pressed={enabled}
>
  {enabled ? <ToggleRight /> : <ToggleLeft />}
</button>

docs.title: 6. Performance Analysis ⏳ PENDING
docs.text:
Status: Cannot be tested until API is functional

Performance Framework Assessment: - ✅ React Query for efficient caching - ✅ Proper component optimization - ✅ Lazy loading preparation - ⏳ Database query performance unknown - ⏳ Large dataset handling untested

Expected Performance Requirements: - Page load time: < 2 seconds - API response time: < 500ms - UI interaction response: < 200ms - Support for 10+ concurrent admins

The UserSettingsPage has been successfully refactored from a 1,560-line monolithic component into a well-organized, modular structure. Each tab is now independent, reusable components have been extracted, and custom hooks manage complex state logic. The refactoring improves:

  • Maintainability: Easier to understand and modify
  • Testability: Components can be tested in isolation
  • Scalability: Easy to add new settings tabs
  • Developer Experience: Clear structure and organization
  • Code Quality: Better separation of concerns

All original functionality has been preserved, and the component is ready for production use.

docs.title: Project Goal
docs.text: Implement Redux for state management in a hyperlocal community platform, considering the existing authentication flow (Supabase), scalability, maintainability, and performance.

docs.title: 1. Redux Toolkit + TS template for Vite
docs.text:
• Description: Official Redux Toolkit template for React and TypeScript using Vite.
  • Pros:
    • Official and well-maintained.
    • Includes TypeScript support.
    • Uses modern tooling (Vite).
    • Includes RTK Query.
    • Provides a solid foundation for Redux Toolkit.
  • Cons:
    • Doesn't include Supabase integration out-of-the-box.
    • Requires manual integration with existing Supabase authentication.

docs.title: 2. Next.js + Supabase + Redux Integration (Example: nextjs-supabase-dashboard-starter)
docs.text:
• Description: A Next.js 14 dashboard starter using Supabase and Redux Toolkit with Persist.
  • Pros:
    • Combines Next.js, Supabase, and Redux Toolkit.
    • Includes Redux Persist for state hydration.
    • Implements RBAC with Supabase policies.
  • Cons:
    • Next.js specific, which may not align with the current project.
    • Requires adaptation to the existing project structure and authentication flow.
    • Might include unnecessary features for the current project.

docs.title: Comparative Analysis
docs.text: Feature Redux Toolkit + TS template for Vite Next.js + Supabase + Redux Integration Framework React (Vite) Next.js Supabase No Yes Authentication Requires manual integration Requires adaptation TypeScript Yes Yes RTK Query Yes Yes State Persistence No Yes (Redux Persist) Code organization Standard Redux Toolkit Potentially custom

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
After thorough research, no single template perfectly fits the project's requirements. The official Redux Toolkit + TS template for Vite provides a solid foundation for Redux Toolkit but lacks Supabase integration. The Next.js + Supabase + Redux integration example (e.g., nextjs-supabase-dashboard-starter) offers a more integrated solution but is specific to Next.js.

Given the existing project's architecture and the need to minimize significant changes, integrating a full template with Next.js seems unsuitable. While a template with direct Supabase integration would be ideal, the effort required to adapt the existing authentication flow and project structure might outweigh the benefits.

Therefore, the decision is to proceed with the official Redux Toolkit + TS template for Vite and manually integrate it with the existing Supabase authentication. This approach allows for a more controlled and gradual integration, ensuring compatibility with the project's existing architecture.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: No suitable template was found that meets the high certainty criteria for integration. The project should proceed based on the original plans, with manual integration of Redux Toolkit using the official template.

docs.title: 1. Unit Tests (src/features/*/__tests__/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Test individual functions, components, and modules in isolation.

Coverage: - Menu API functions (CRUD operations) - Menu utilities and helpers - Individual React components - Custom hooks - Type validation - Data transformation functions

Key Features: - Mock external dependencies - Test edge cases and boundary conditions - Validate input/output contracts - Performance benchmarks for critical functions

Example Test Files: 

// API unit tests
src/features/admin/api/__tests__/menuManagement.comprehensive.test.ts

// Component unit tests  
src/features/menu/components/__tests__/DynamicMenu.test.tsx

docs.title: 2. Integration Tests (src/tests/integration/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Test how different parts of the system work together.

Coverage: - Complete CRUD workflows - Component interactions - Data flow from API to UI - State management - Form validation and submission - Bulk operations

Key Features: - End-to-end data flow testing - Mock external services only - Test realistic user scenarios - Validate system behavior under load

docs.title: 3. Component Tests
docs.text:
Purpose: Test React components with user interactions and rendering.

Coverage: - Component rendering with various props - User interactions (clicks, form inputs, drag & drop) - State changes and updates - Error boundary handling - Conditional rendering logic

Key Features: - Comprehensive prop testing - Event handling validation - Accessibility attribute checking - Responsive behavior testing

docs.title: 4. End-to-End Tests (tests/e2e/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Test complete user journeys in a real browser environment.

Coverage: - Full admin workflow from login to menu management - Multi-step operations (create, edit, delete, reorder) - Tab navigation and filtering - Bulk operations - Form validation and error handling - Responsive design across devices

Key Features: - Real browser automation with Playwright - Cross-browser testing (Chrome, Firefox, Safari) - Mobile and tablet device testing - Visual regression testing - Performance monitoring

docs.title: 5. Performance Tests (src/tests/performance/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Ensure the system performs well under various conditions.

Coverage: - Large menu structure rendering (1000+ items) - Memory usage monitoring - Interaction responsiveness - Bundle size optimization - Core Web Vitals compliance

Key Performance Metrics: - Initial render time: < 100ms (100 items) - Memory usage: < 50MB increase - First Contentful Paint: < 1.8s - Largest Contentful Paint: < 2.5s - Interaction to Next Paint: < 200ms

docs.title: 6. Accessibility Tests (src/tests/accessibility/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Ensure WCAG 2.1 AA compliance and inclusive design.

Coverage: - Keyboard navigation - Screen reader compatibility - Focus management - ARIA attributes and semantic HTML - Color contrast ratios - Touch target sizes (44px minimum)

Key Features: - Automated accessibility scanning with jest-axe - Manual keyboard testing - Screen reader announcements - High contrast mode support - Reduced motion preferences

docs.title: 7. Security Tests (src/tests/security/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Validate security measures and prevent vulnerabilities.

Coverage: - Role-based access control - Input sanitization (XSS prevention) - SQL injection protection - CSRF token validation - Data exposure prevention - Authentication and authorization

Security Test Cases: - XSS attempts in form inputs - SQL injection in search queries - Path traversal in URLs - Role elevation attempts - Session validation - CSRF attack simulation

docs.title: 8. Error Handling Tests (src/tests/error-handling/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Ensure graceful degradation and error recovery.

Coverage: - Network failures (timeout, offline, server errors) - Malformed API responses - Data corruption handling - Component error boundaries - Validation errors - Edge cases and boundary conditions

Error Scenarios: - API timeouts and retries - Invalid form submissions - Corrupted menu hierarchies - Memory leaks detection - Progressive enhancement fallbacks

docs.title: 9. Database Tests (src/tests/database/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Test database schema, migrations, and data integrity.

Coverage: - Migration scripts execution - Schema validation - Data integrity constraints - Performance optimizations - Backup and recovery procedures

Database Test Areas: - Table creation and indexing - Foreign key constraints - Trigger functionality - Stored procedures - Migration rollbacks

docs.title: 10. Cross-Browser Tests (tests/cross-browser/)
docs.text:
Purpose: Ensure compatibility across different browsers and devices.

Coverage: - Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge - Desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports - Touch interactions - Feature detection and fallbacks - Progressive enhancement

Browser Matrix: 

Desktop: Chrome 90+, Firefox 88+, Safari 14+, Edge 90+
Mobile: iOS Safari, Chrome Mobile, Samsung Internet
Tablet: iPad Safari, Android Chrome
